## How to Track Cash Expenses on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/track-cash-expenses.html
 How to track cash expenses on iPhone without forgetting them  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated October 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Why cash goes missing from budgets    The method: cash as its own account    Make logging take three seconds    A daily reminder, if you need one    Shared cash and splitting    Cash in other currencies    What a cash budget looks like    Common mistakes    Frequently asked questions
 Cash is the spending that leaves no alert behind, so it has to be captured at the moment you pay or it is gone. The reliable method is to treat cash as an account, record the withdrawal as a transfer into it, log each cash purchase in a few seconds, and compare what the app says is in your wallet with what is actually there once a week.
 Why cash goes missing from budgets
 Card purchases generate a receipt, an alert and a statement line. Cash generates nothing. A taxi, a coffee, a tip and a market stall can add up to a meaningful share of a month, and none of them will appear on any statement you review later. When people say their budget "doesn't add up", untracked cash is one of the usual reasons.
 The second reason is the withdrawal itself. Writing "ATM 500" as an expense feels like tracking, but it hides where the money went. You end up with one large, uncategorised entry and no idea whether the cash went on food, transport or gifts.
 The method: cash as its own account
 1. Create an account called Cash. Its balance should match the notes and coins in your wallet. 2. When you withdraw money, record a transfer from your bank account to Cash. Nothing is spent yet; money has only moved. 3. Each time you pay in cash, record an expense from the Cash account with the right category. 4. Once a week, count your wallet. If the app says 140 and you hold 100, you have 40 of forgotten spending. Record it as a single "unrecorded cash" expense so the balance is true again, and notice which days it happened.
 The weekly count is what makes the method honest. It turns forgotten purchases from an invisible leak into one visible number you can shrink over time.
 Make logging take three seconds
 The method only works if each entry is fast enough to do at the counter or in the taxi. Some ways to get there on an iPhone:

  Say it.  Tap Say and speak: "taxi 40 cash", or a whole morning at once: "coffee 15, newspaper 5 and parking 10 with cash". Each purchase becomes a draft with the Cash account already chosen; check and save. A recording stops by itself when you pause.
  Lock Screen and Control Center.  Add the Quick Add widget or, on iOS 18 and later, the Say an Expense control, so logging starts without finding the app.
  Templates.  For the same coffee every morning, turn on "Save as template" once. Afterwards it is one tap from Quick Add.
  The keypad.  The entry sheet's keypad does arithmetic, so "12 + 8" for two items is fine; the saved amount is always what the expression on screen adds up to.

 The  voice entry guide  covers what Say it understands and which devices support it.
 A daily reminder, if you need one
 If you tend to forget, turn on More → Daily Reminder in TrackExpenses and pick an evening time. Use the reminder to empty your pockets and log anything missing while the day is still fresh. After a few weeks most people find they need it less, because logging at the moment of payment becomes a habit.
 Shared cash and splitting
 If you pay cash for a group and others pay you back, record the full amount you paid as an expense, then record each repayment as income on the Cash account, or reduce the expense to your share once everyone has paid. Pick one approach and keep it; mixing them makes the category totals hard to read. For cash you receive as a gift or allowance, record income on the Cash account so the balance stays right.
 Cash in other currencies
 Travel cash works the same way, with one extra field. Record the withdrawal abroad as a transfer into a cash account, and record purchases in the currency you paid. TrackExpenses asks for the exchange rate and prefills the last one you used, so totals still convert into your main currency. A small separate cash account for each trip makes it easy to see what you spent there and what you brought home.
 What a cash budget looks like
 Once cash is tracked, it can be budgeted like anything else. Look at last month's cash expenses by category under Stats. If transport in cash was 300, set a transport budget and watch its bar against the today marker during the month. If you are halfway through the month and the bar is at 80%, you know before the wallet is empty, not after.
 Some people prefer the opposite approach: withdraw a fixed amount at the start of each period and spend only that. The cash account fits this too. The transfer at the start of the period is your allowance, and the account balance tells you how much of it is left.
 Common mistakes

  Recording the ATM withdrawal as an expense  and then also logging the purchases. That counts the same money twice. Use a transfer.
  Rounding everything into one daily "cash" entry.  It is better than nothing, but you lose the categories that make the data useful.
  Skipping the weekly count.  Without it, the cash balance drifts and stops meaning anything.
  Logging only "big" cash.  Small daily purchases are exactly the ones that add up.

 Frequently asked questions
 Should an ATM withdrawal be an expense? No. Record it as a transfer from your bank account to a cash account. The individual purchases you make with that cash are the expenses.
 What is the fastest way to log cash on iPhone? Speaking it, for example "taxi 40 cash" with Say it in TrackExpenses, or a one-tap template for repeat purchases. Both start from the Lock Screen.
 How do I find cash I forgot to record? Count your wallet weekly and compare it with the cash account balance. Record the difference as one entry and look at which days you skipped.
 Is tracking cash free in TrackExpenses? Yes. Cash accounts, transfers, templates, widgets and the daily reminder are free. Voice entry includes 10 saved entries per calendar month for free; Pro makes it unlimited.
 Source: TrackExpenses accounts, transfers, templates, voice entry and reminder features, checked against the app in October 2026. Figures are examples, not financial advice. ## Arabic Bank SMS Expense Tracking on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/arabic-bank-sms-expenses.html
 Track expenses from Arabic bank SMS alerts on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated October 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Use the app in Arabic    What Arabic bank alerts look like    How TrackExpenses reads them    Set up the automation    Test with a real alert before relying on it    Link your cards and accounts    Salary and incoming transfers    Limits    Frequently asked questions
 TrackExpenses can turn supported Arabic bank SMS alerts into ledger entries on iPhone through a Shortcuts Message automation. Version 1.6.0 also includes an Arabic interface with right-to-left layout, alongside English; message parsing happens on your device.
 You can keep a ledger without an automation: read each alert and enter its amount, date and merchant in a spreadsheet or expense app. Check the transaction amount separately from the remaining balance, and reconcile against your bank statement. Automation saves repeated entry, but the same checks still matter.
 Use the app in Arabic
 Update TrackExpenses to version 1.6.0 or later. Open More → Language under Look & feel to open the app's page in iOS Settings, then choose Arabic in the language setting. The row shows the language currently in use. These menu names describe the English interface; translated labels depend on your current language.
 If iOS does not offer a language choice, first add another preferred language in Settings → General → Language & Region → Add Language. You can keep English as your iPhone's primary language while choosing Arabic for TrackExpenses. The app's interface language and the wording of your bank alerts are separate: an English interface can still process supported Arabic messages.
 What Arabic bank alerts look like
 A purchase might read "شراء بـSAR 140 لـ MERCHANT" or "تم خصم AED 18.50 من بطاقتك المنتهية بالرقم 6878 لدى ENOC". Incoming transfers use حوالة واردة; salaries may say تم إيداع الراتب. Alerts often use labelled lines rather than sentences.
 Arabic attaches prefixes such as بـ and لـ to words, mixes right-to-left sentences with Latin merchant names, and may use Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣). One-time password messages can also contain an amount and transfer wording, so an amount alone does not prove money moved.
 How TrackExpenses reads them
 TrackExpenses reads alerts with a rule-based reader that knows Arabic banking vocabulary, not only English. It converts Arabic-Indic and Persian digits before reading amounts, recognises the glued forms of words such as خصم، شراء، الرصيد and the bi/li prefixes, and treats a balance phrase like "رصيدك الحالي" as a balance rather than the amount spent.
 Direction comes from the words: خصم and شراء are money out, حوالة واردة and تم إيداع الراتب are money in, and "تم استلام حوالة" is a received remittance. A card-bill message can be recognised as paying your card rather than spending. Rules skip recognised one-time codes, including رمز التفعيل، رمز مؤقت، كلمة مرور لمرة واحدة, and failed operations such as "لم يتم تنفيذ العملية". Test your own bank's wording; this is not a promise that every format is understood.
 Set up the automation

  1.  Open TrackExpenses, create the receiving account, then open More → SMS Auto-Import. Check your iOS version in Settings → General → About.
  2.  In Shortcuts, create a Message automation. On iOS 27, start in Library → Automation → +, open Editor if prompted, then add Automation → Message.
  3.  Filter on wording present in real alerts, such as شراء or خصم. In the iOS 27 trigger, change the blue Sender field to Message, then enter the text to match. A currency code such as AED or SAR is another option if your bank uses it consistently.
  4.  Add TrackExpenses' Import Bank Message action. On iOS 27, select the trigger's Message variable, then choose its Content property. Turn Confirm Before Run off in the trigger and Show When Run off in the action; check Allow Running When Locked under the editor's Privacy settings.
  5.  On iOS 26, use Message Contains, choose Run Immediately, and connect the action's Message parameter to Shortcut Input instead. Save and confirm the automation is enabled.

 If your bank writes ريال or درهم without a currency code, use wording the alerts actually contain. Check recent messages first. Avoid overlapping automations and remember that a currency filter can also match personal texts.
 The  complete SMS setup guide  has separate iOS 27 and iOS 26 videos and screenshots. Use the  troubleshooting checklist  if no activity appears, and the  SMS feature page  for the overall workflow.
 Test with a real alert before relying on it
 The SMS Auto-Import screen lets you test a copied message and see the amount, direction, merchant and card, or the reason it would be skipped. Try a purchase, transfer and salary alert. For example, an alert with a purchase of AED 18.50 and a remaining balance of AED 2,000 should produce an expense of 18.50, not 2,000. Check the account and currency too.
 You can also copy an alert in Messages, open Quick Add and paste it under "From a bank message". Review the resulting draft before saving. This manual route does not use the automatic import allowance. A successful paste test does not prove the automation is connected: wait for the next genuine matching alert, then check the setup screen's activity.
 Link your cards and accounts
 Arabic alerts usually print the last digits of the card or account: "المنتهية بالرقم 6878" or "**1000". Add those digits to the matching account in TrackExpenses (the account editor has a field for them), or use "File under…" on the review sheet once. After that, purchases on that card land in the right account automatically. When an alert describes an ATM withdrawal (سحب صراف آلي) or a transfer between your own accounts (حوالة بين حساباتك), it becomes a transfer only when both accounts can be matched; otherwise it is flagged for review instead of guessed.
 Salary and incoming transfers
 A salary credit is the alert a ledger most wants. With "Import money coming in" turned on in the SMS Auto-Import settings, credits such as تم إيداع الراتب and حوالة واردة are imported as income and flagged, so you confirm them on the review sheet. Leave it off if you prefer to record income yourself.
 Limits
 Free includes 10 successful automatic imports per calendar month on each device. Further alerts are kept but locked outside your totals until Pro releases them, or the next calendar month's allowance releases as many as it covers. Saved entries remain available. Raw message text is not saved in the ledger. Only alerts passed by your configured automation reach the reader; the app cannot read your inbox or backfill old texts. System notifications vary by iOS version and settings.
 Frequently asked questions
 Does TrackExpenses support Arabic bank SMS? Yes. It reads common Arabic purchase, transfer, salary and card-payment wordings by rule on your device, and refuses Arabic one-time codes. Test your own bank's alert in the setup screen.
 Is the app available in Arabic? Yes. Version 1.6.0 adds an Arabic interface with right-to-left layout. Supported Arabic bank messages and spoken entries can also be used.
 Which phrase should the automation look for? Choose purchase wording or a currency code present in your bank's actual alerts. Test several messages and avoid filters that forward unrelated texts.
 Can it read the Arabic-Indic digits in my alerts? Yes. Arabic-Indic and Persian digits are converted before the amount is read.
 Sources: TrackExpenses 1.6.0 language settings, bank-message reader and FreeTier code, checked 29 October 2026;  Apple's language settings instructions . Version-specific Shortcuts steps follow the app's  recorded setup walkthroughs . Example alerts are illustrative, not bank compatibility guarantees. ## Track Subscriptions and Recurring Bills on iPhone
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/track-subscriptions-recurring-bills.html
 How to track subscriptions and recurring bills on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Find what you already pay    Recurring rules in TrackExpenses    Bills that change every month    Put bills inside your payday month    Let alerts confirm the charge    Review the list every quarter    Annual subscriptions    Frequently asked questions
 Write every subscription and fixed bill down once as a recurring rule, so it appears in your ledger on the day it is charged without being typed again. Then review the list every few months: recurring rules make bills visible, and visible bills are the ones you actually cancel.
 Find what you already pay
 Before tracking anything, make a list. Most people underestimate their subscriptions because each one is small and arrives on a different day.
 1.  App Store subscriptions.  On iPhone, open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions. This lists everything billed through Apple, active and expired. 2.  Card and bank statements.  Scan the last three months for repeated amounts and merchants: streaming, music, cloud storage, gym, software, news. 3.  Fixed bills.  Rent, phone, internet, utilities, insurance and loan instalments. Note the amount, the day of the month and the account it comes from. 4.  Annual charges.  Domain names, memberships, insurance and some software renew once a year. They are the most likely to surprise you.
 Write each one with four fields: name, amount, how often, and the next date. That list is the input for everything below. To see what it adds up to, enter it in the  subscription cost calculator : it totals every price as a month, a year and five years, biggest first.
 Recurring rules in TrackExpenses
 TrackExpenses calls these Recurring. Open More → Recurring and tap the plus button. For each item:

 Choose expense or income. Salary is a recurring income rule.
 Enter the amount, category and account it is paid from.
 Choose how often: every day, week, month or year. You can also repeat every N periods, for example every 2 weeks or every 3 months for a quarterly bill.
 Set the start date to the next charge.

 When the date arrives, the transaction is added to your ledger automatically the next time you open the app. Each occurrence is created once, even if you use two devices with iCloud sync, so a rent rule never charges twice. The Recurring screen groups income and expenses and shows their totals, so you can see at a glance how much of your month is already committed. To hear about each bill the day before it is due, see the  bill reminders guide .
 Free includes two recurring rules, enough for salary and rent. Pro makes rules unlimited, so every subscription can have its own.
 Bills that change every month
 Electricity and phone bills vary. Two approaches work:

  Recurring with an estimate.  Create the rule with a typical amount and edit the generated entry when the real bill arrives. Your budget sees the bill coming from the start of the month.
  Log when charged.  Skip the rule and record the bill when it arrives, by hand or from your bank's SMS alert. Accurate, but invisible until it happens.

 The  payday budget guide  explains how to make the period match your salary.
 For budgeting, the first is usually better, because the money is spoken for even before the bill lands.
 Put bills inside your payday month
 If you are paid on the 25th, set your budget month to start on the 25th under More → Period & Entry. Then rent on the 1st and the phone bill on the 10th fall inside the same period as the salary that pays them. Budget pacing becomes clearer too: a large rent payment early in the period explains a high percentage on the budget bar, and you can see it is planned rather than overspending.
 Let alerts confirm the charge
 If your bank texts you for each charge, a TrackExpenses SMS automation can record bills and subscriptions as they happen. Combined with a recurring rule, this can create two entries for the same charge. Choose one source per bill: use a recurring rule for things that don't send alerts, such as direct debits some banks don't announce, and let the alert record the ones that do. Imported entries with the same amount and payee as a nearby entry are flagged as possible duplicates, so a double is easy to spot and remove.
 Review the list every quarter
 A subscription list is only useful if you act on it. Every three months:
 1. Open More → Recurring and read each rule. 2. For each subscription, ask whether you used it in the last month. 3. Cancel what you didn't use. App Store subscriptions are cancelled in Settings → your name → Subscriptions; others on the provider's website. 4. Delete the rule in TrackExpenses so your forecast stops counting it. 5. Look for price increases. If a rule says 9.99 but your statement says 12.99, update the rule.
 Use Stats to see the total of your subscriptions category over the last few months. A number you can see is easier to reduce than one spread across twelve statement lines.
 Annual subscriptions
 Yearly charges deserve their own rules, with the repeat set to every year. Some people also divide the annual cost by twelve and set aside that amount each month in a savings account with a monthly transfer rule, so the renewal never feels like a shock. TrackExpenses records the transfer without counting it as spending, and the yearly charge as an expense on the day it happens.
 Frequently asked questions
 How do I see all my subscriptions on iPhone? Open Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions for anything billed through Apple. Subscriptions billed to your card directly appear only on your statements.
 Can TrackExpenses add bills automatically every month? Yes. Recurring rules add each occurrence on its date, every day, week, month or year, or every N of them. Two rules are free and Pro is unlimited.
 What if the bill amount changes? Create the rule with a typical amount and edit the entry when the actual bill arrives, or log variable bills when they are charged.
 Will a recurring rule and a bank SMS import create duplicates? They can if both cover the same bill, so pick one source per bill. Imports that match a nearby entry are flagged as possible duplicates.
 Source: Apple Subscriptions settings and TrackExpenses Recurring rules, checked in October 2026. Amounts are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login. ## Budget Pacing: Are You Spending Too Fast This Month?
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/budget-pacing-explained.html
 Budget Pacing: Are You Spending Too Fast This Month?  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Check pacing with an iPhone calculator    Read the spending bar and today marker together    Work through a payday-month example    Turn the remainder into a daily reference    Move money when one category needs more    Avoid misleading comparisons    Frequently asked questions
 Budget pacing compares the share of your budget already spent with the share of the period already elapsed. TrackExpenses puts a time marker beside spending progress, so you can check the two together without treating an early bill as proof that the whole month is going wrong.
 Check pacing with an iPhone calculator
 You need a spending budget, recorded expenses and the dates the budget covers. Use one currency and one period for every number. A payday month beginning on the 25th should not be compared with expenses counted from the 1st.
 First calculate spending as a percentage: expenses divided by budget, multiplied by 100. Then calculate the percentage of the period that has passed. For a simple check, use completed days divided by the total days in the period, multiplied by 100. Calculator on iPhone is enough for both, or use the  budget pacing calculator .
 Spending ahead of time means purchases arrived faster than an even daily spread; spending behind time means they arrived more slowly. Check transactions before changing your plan, especially if rent or an annual renewal landed early.
 For a reusable worksheet, Numbers can calculate from table cells. Keep your budget and expenses in separate cells, then divide expenses by budget. Apple's  Numbers formula instructions  explain opening the formula keyboard, selecting cells and using arithmetic operators. Label your period dates beside the calculation so the result remains understandable next week.
 Read the spending bar and today marker together
 In TrackExpenses, open Stats, choose Budget and check the period dates at the top. Tap Budget Setting to enter a Total budget and any category budgets. The budget is kept in your period length (set under More → Period & Entry); other lengths are worked out from it.
 The filled bar represents expenses divided by the budget. The vertical marker represents where the current moment falls between the period's start and end. The app uses elapsed time, so its marker moves through the day; it need not match a calculation using only completed days exactly.
 Look at both positions. If the fill passes the marker, spending is ahead of an even spread. If the marker passes the fill, spending is behind it. Check the total first, then categories. A large early household payment and steadily rising food expenses can produce the same total percentage while needing different attention.
 Budgets and these pacing bars are free. The  budget planner feature page  explains the wider workflow. To change the dates your month follows, use the  payday budget guide .
 Work through a payday-month example
 Imagine a budget of 3,000 for 25 September through 24 October, a 30-day period. At the start of 10 October, 15 complete days have passed. Your recorded expenses total 1,800.

 Spending progress: 1,800 divided by 3,000 equals 60%.
 Time progress: 15 divided by 30 equals 50%.
 An even spread at halfway would be 1,500.
 Recorded spending is 300 ahead of that reference, with 1,200 left in the budget.

 The ten-percentage-point gap is a prompt to examine purchases, not a prediction that you will overspend.
 Suppose rent of 1,200 was paid near the beginning. That used 40% of the total immediately, even though the next rent payment falls outside this period. An early jump can be expected. Compare everyday categories separately and check whether upcoming bills are already recorded before drawing a conclusion from the total bar.
 Turn the remainder into a daily reference
 A daily reference answers a different question: how much of the remaining budget is available per remaining calendar day? In the example, 10–24 October contains 15 days, including today. Dividing 1,200 by 15 gives 80 per day.
 TrackExpenses Pro calculates the daily budget after accounting for repeating bills, paid or still due, and other spending before today. It shares the available amount across the days left, including today, and rounds down in your currency’s precision. Today’s spending counts against that allowance; it does not keep moving the starting figure. If the budget is used up, the basic Budget used up message stays free.
 The Budget tab also shows a daily amount for each category budget with Pro, including Lifetime. Each category’s own repeating bills come out first; a bills-only category does not show a daily figure. Days left appear once in the header, and every budget labels spent and left amounts.
 Use the  free daily-budget calculator  to try remaining-budget arithmetic. It lets you subtract extra commitments before dividing. If a bill of 300 is still due, the example becomes 900 divided by 15, or 60 per day. Do not subtract a bill again if it is already included in your spending figure. The app accounts for repeating rules you have entered; it cannot know a commitment you have never recorded.
 Move money when one category needs more
 If transport goes over while groceries has room, you can adjust this period without changing the overall budget. In Stats → Budget, tap ••• on a budget and choose Move money in or Move money out. Check the amount before confirming. The move lasts for this budget period; change your standing amounts in Budget Setting or the  salary plan  if the change should repeat.
 An over-budget row offers Cover. Suggested moves leave repeating bills still due covered; a manually chosen amount that would use their reserved money gets a warning. Moves and Cover are free. The  budget planner page  explains the steps and shows a before-and-after example.
 The daily figure is a budget reference, not a bank-balance check. It depends on complete records, and spending the reference amount every day is not a requirement.
 Avoid misleading comparisons
 Check transfers and credit-card payments. Moving money between your own accounts should not become a second purchase; otherwise spending and pacing are inflated. See  credit-card payment versus expense  for the distinction.
 Check missing entries too. A nearly empty bar can mean you are spending less, or that cash purchases and late bank alerts have not been entered yet. Correct duplicates and dates before interpreting the result.
 Keep planned and recorded figures clear. A pacing bar summarizes recorded expenses in the selected period. It cannot know every unentered commitment. The Pro Plan view can help explore scenarios, but forecasts still depend on the records and assumptions supplied.
 Compare like periods: month lengths, payday boundaries and unusually timed bills affect the picture. Review purchases and commitments together. A marker is useful context, not a guarantee about available cash.
 Frequently asked questions
 Does spending ahead of the today marker mean I have exceeded my budget? No. It means spending is ahead of an even spread over time. Exceeding the budget means recorded expenses are greater than the budget itself.
 Why does rent make my pacing look high early in the month? A large bill uses budget immediately, while the time marker has barely moved. Check whether that bill was expected and whether it will recur inside the same period.
 Do I need Pro to see budget pacing? No. Budgets and pacing bars are free. Positive daily spending guidance, forecasts and what-if planning require Pro.
 Why can the app's time marker differ from my day-count calculation? The marker uses elapsed time through the current moment. A worksheet using only completed calendar days gives a simpler approximation.
 Source: TrackExpenses BudgetStatsView, MoveBudgetSheet, BudgetMoves, BudgetBar, FiscalPeriod, InsightsEngine and FreeTier checked in November 2026;  Apple's iPhone Calculator guide  and the Numbers formula guide linked above. Figures are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login. ## Track Expenses Without Connecting Your Bank on iPhone
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/expense-tracker-without-bank-connection.html
 Track expenses on iPhone without connecting your bank  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Start with a simple record you control    Compare manual, SMS and bank-connected tracking    Set up a ledger without a bank login    Make entry quick enough to repeat    Reconcile instead of assuming automation is complete    Understand what private storage means    Frequently asked questions
 You can track expenses without sharing a bank login: keep a ledger in a spreadsheet or an app, then reconcile it against your statements. TrackExpenses adds manual entry, on-device voice drafts and optional Shortcuts imports for supported bank alerts; it does not connect to your bank or read your Messages inbox.
 The useful question is how much entry work you will actually keep doing. A private ledger with missing purchases can be less useful than a simpler record you maintain consistently. Start with one account and a week of real spending before building an elaborate system.
 Start with a simple record you control
 Apple Numbers is a reasonable built-in option if it is already on your phone. Create a table with date, description, amount, currency, category and account. Enter each purchase as one row. Keep money entering an account separate from purchases, and record movements between your own accounts consistently.
 For the first week, use a few recognizable categories rather than dozens. Groceries, transport, eating out and bills can be enough to discover whether the routine works. Keep the currency alongside the amount: 50 in one currency is not interchangeable with 50 in another.
 A spreadsheet gives you flexible columns and direct control over formulas. Its trade-off is the work of maintaining those formulas and entering purchases on a small screen. If entry becomes the obstacle, look for a faster input method before abandoning the record. The  iPhone expense tracking guide  compares Notes, Numbers, Wallet and app entry.
 Compare manual, SMS and bank-connected tracking
 Manual entry works for cash, cards and purchases that never generate an alert. You choose what to save and can correct the description immediately. The cost is attention: a forgotten purchase stays missing until you catch it.
 SMS-assisted entry reduces typing when your bank sends supported transaction alerts. In TrackExpenses, a Shortcuts Message automation passes selected incoming messages to the app. It is an optional workflow you set up, rather than permission for the app to browse old messages. Alerts can be delayed, incomplete or unsupported, so compare saved entries with your statement.
 Bank-connected services offer another workflow: supported institutions send records through a connection arranged by that service. Coverage, authorization, timing and retention depend on the provider and bank. Read their current documentation before choosing one. This guide does not claim that a particular connection is unsafe, or that manual tracking is always more accurate.
 Set up a ledger without a bank login
 Add the account you spend from and give it a clear name. Enter an opening balance only if you know the balance at your chosen starting point. Otherwise, start recording purchases and reconcile the account before relying on its displayed balance.
 Choose your main currency and the start of your monthly budget period. A monthly period beginning on payday can make the record easier to read if that matches how you plan. A fixed monthly start is different from a rolling two-week pay cycle; do not assume the app models both.
 Then enter a few purchases manually. Check their dates, categories and accounts. TrackExpenses includes unlimited manual transactions and budgets in the free ledger. Its  private expense tracker page  explains the privacy model and current limits.
 Make entry quick enough to repeat
 Use one reliable habit: record a purchase after paying, or review receipts at a set time each evening. A widget or template can reduce the number of steps. Cash still needs an explicit record because there may be no notification to import.
 On compatible devices and languages, voice entry creates drafts on your device. Say the purchases, inspect the amounts and accounts, then save the intended entries. The free allowance is 10 saved voice entries per calendar month on each device; Pro removes that limit. See the  voice entry guide  before treating it as your main input method.
 If you enable SMS import, start with the  bank SMS setup guide . Test a supported alert and inspect the result before enabling more filters. Free use includes 10 successful automatic SMS imports per calendar month per device. Later alerts are retained but locked outside totals until Pro or a later allowance releases them.
 Reconcile instead of assuming automation is complete
 Once a week, compare the ledger with your bank statement and your cash on hand. Look for missing purchases, duplicate imports, refunds and the wrong account. A matching transaction count alone is insufficient: two incorrect entries can cancel each other numerically.
 For example, suppose you record a card purchase of 40 and later pay 40 from a bank account toward that card. The purchase is spending; the payment moves money between your accounts. Recording both as purchases doubles the apparent spending. The  credit card payment guide  explains the workflow in more detail.
 Keep a short note about unresolved differences. Correct the record when you understand the cause rather than adding an unexplained balancing entry immediately. The aim is a ledger you can explain, including any known gaps.
 Understand what private storage means
 No bank connection does not mean that every service is offline. TrackExpenses can sync the ledger through your private iCloud account; Apple and RevenueCat handle purchases. Read the  privacy policy  for the actual data flow and decide whether that fits your needs.
 With Pro, export a month or a longer span as CSV when you want a portable table. CSV is useful for reviewing rows in Numbers, but it is not a complete app backup; Pro also writes a full JSON backup you can restore. Check an exported file before depending on it, and store copies somewhere you control.
 Frequently asked questions
 Does TrackExpenses need my bank password? No. The app does not connect to your bank. You enter purchases or configure optional Shortcuts workflows for supported alerts.
 Can it import my entire SMS history? No. A configured Shortcuts automation passes matching incoming messages; the app cannot read your Messages inbox or retrieve your old banking messages.
 Is bank-free tracking automatically more accurate? No. Accuracy depends on complete entries, correct account assignments and reconciliation. Any input method can leave gaps or duplicates.
 Sources:  Apple: Message event triggers in Shortcuts . Product features and allowances checked against the TrackExpenses 1.4.0 listing and app source on 18 October 2026. Examples describe record keeping, not personalized financial recommendations.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login.  See Private by design →          Related reading    How to Track Expenses on iPhone    Double Tap Your iPhone Back to Log Expenses    December Money Reset: A Spending Challenge    How to Set a Daily Spending Limit    Track Travel Expenses Abroad on iPhone    Get Reminded Before Bills Are Due on iPhone

## SMS Auto-Import Setup: iOS 27 and 26 | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/sms-setup.html
 Set up bank SMS auto-import on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated October 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Before you start    Watch the setup videos    iOS 27 setup    iOS 26 and earlier setup    Choose a reliable bank filter    Test and confirm the connection    Accounts, review and import options    If something does not work    Allowance and privacy    Frequently asked questions
 Connect a Shortcuts Message automation to TrackExpenses to turn supported new bank alerts into expenses. Choose the instructions for your iOS version below: iOS 27 puts the trigger inside a shortcut, while iOS 26 uses a separate automation setup flow.
 Before you start
 Open TrackExpenses once, finish onboarding and create the account that should receive purchases. Go to More → SMS Auto-Import. Keep one genuine bank alert nearby to choose a filter. You need Apple’s Shortcuts app on the same iPhone that receives the messages; TrackExpenses cannot read your inbox or backfill old texts.
 Check your version in Settings → General → About → iOS Version. The videos are silent and have written captions. Pause whenever you need to switch apps. The written steps below cover the same controls, including the message variable that connects the two apps.
 Watch the setup videos
  Choose your iOS version   iOS 27   iOS 26 or earlier   iOS 27    Your browser cannot play this video. Follow the written steps below.   Download the iOS 27 video  ·  Watch with chapters and transcript  ·  Read the steps     iOS 26 and earlier    Your browser cannot play this video. Follow the written steps below.   Download the iOS 26 video  ·  Watch with chapters and transcript  ·  Read the steps
 iOS 27 setup
 These steps were checked in Shortcuts on iOS 27.0 on 25 October 2026. The screenshots are real simulator captures. Labels can vary with system language and later updates.

  1. Start from Library.  Open Shortcuts. If you see All Shortcuts, tap back to Library. Choose Automation and tap the + at the bottom.
  2. Open the editor.  If a Describe a Shortcut screen appears, tap Editor or Edit. In the actions panel, tap Automation, then choose Message under Communication. This adds the trigger inside your shortcut.
  3. Choose a text filter.  Tap the first blue Sender field and choose Message. The condition changes to Message contains Text. Tap Text and enter wording your bank repeats, such as “purchase” or “debited”. The video’s Purchase is an example, not a required password. Use a currency code only if it appears in the alerts you want.
  4. Enable automatic runs.  Close the input bar with ×. Expand the blue arrow in the Message trigger. Keep Automation on and Confirm Before Run off. You do not need to find the older Run Immediately screen.
  5. Add the app action.  Tap Search in the editor, find Import Bank Message, and select the TrackExpenses action. It appears as Import transaction from Message beneath your trigger.
  6. Select the incoming message.  Tap the blue Message placeholder in the import action. Tap Select Variable in the bottom bar, then the Message output directly beneath the trigger. This is a variable selection: do not type the word Message.
  7. Pass its content.  Close the variable bar with ×, tap the inserted Message variable, and choose Content in its Get list. Tap Return and close the bar. The import action should now contain a blue Content token. This passes the message body rather than its sender or recipients.
  8. Save quietly.  Expand the import action’s blue arrow and switch Show When Run off. Open ⓘ in the editor toolbar → Privacy and check Allow Running When Locked is on. Return to Details, tap Done, then use the editor’s back button to save. Confirm the saved automation’s switch is enabled.

    Automation is in the editor’s actions panel.     Automation on; Confirm Before Run off.     Select the Message output beneath the trigger.     Choose Content in the variable’s Get list.     Content connected; Show When Run off.     Allow Running When Locked in the shortcut’s Privacy settings.
 iOS 26 and earlier setup

 Open Shortcuts → Automation → + or New Automation, then choose Message.
 Set Message Contains to wording from your bank alerts. Leave Sender as Any Sender unless you deliberately want both conditions. Choose Run Immediately, then Next. Older releases may use Ask Before Running; turn it off when available.
 Under Get Started, choose Create New Shortcut, sometimes called New Blank Automation. Search for Import Bank Message and add the TrackExpenses action.
 Tap its blue Message field → Select Variable in the bottom bar → Shortcut Input beneath Receive messages as input. Do not type “Shortcut Input” into the field.
 Close the variable bar with ×. Expand the import action, turn Show When Run off, and save using Done or the checkmark. Reopen the automation and confirm it is enabled.

 The older video was recorded on iOS 26. Some buttons differ on iOS 17 or 18; the essential connection remains the incoming message variable passed to Import Bank Message.
 Choose a reliable bank filter
 Use text present in actual purchase alerts, not an imagined phrase. A currency code can also match personal messages. A contact-only sender filter may miss a bank’s short code or changing sender identity. If you add several conditions, all must match. Add separate, narrowly filtered automations for genuinely different alert formats, and avoid overlapping filters that forward the same purchase twice.
 Test and confirm the connection
 First, use the message check in More → SMS Auto-Import with an alert you copy yourself. It tests whether the reader understands that format. For example, an AED 45 purchase with a remaining balance of AED 2,000 should produce a 45 expense. Check the currency, merchant, direction and account too.
 Then wait for the next genuine matching alert on your iPhone. Return to SMS Auto-Import and check its connection status and activity. A paste test or manually pressing Play in Shortcuts does not prove that incoming messages are connected. Simulator captures demonstrate setup; carrier-message delivery needs a real device.
 Accounts, review and import options
 Use the setup screen’s account matching controls to associate masked card or account digits with your ledger accounts. Review imported amounts, categories and dates. Income importing and app notifications have separate options there. A foreign-currency entry may need an exchange rate. Check possible duplicates, especially if both SMS and Wallet automations cover a purchase. Wallet setup has its  own guide .
 If something does not work
 If no activity appears, check the trigger’s filter and enabled state. On iOS 27 also check Confirm Before Run is off and Allow Running When Locked is on. If a Message typing box appears, reconnect the import parameter to the incoming variable: Message → Content on iOS 27, Shortcut Input on iOS 26. Disable Show When Run. If activity records a skip, read its reason before recreating the automation. See the  full troubleshooting checklist .
 Allowance and privacy
 Free includes 10 successful automatic SMS imports per calendar month per device. Later alerts are kept locked outside totals; Pro releases them, or the next month’s allowance releases as many as it covers. Budget start dates do not change this reset. Manual entries remain unlimited.
 Only messages passed by your configured automation reach the reader. There is no bank login or inbox permission. Parsing happens on your device; raw message text is not saved in the ledger. Delete or disable the shortcut to stop this route. Read the  privacy policy  for full storage and purchase details.
 Frequently asked questions
 Do I need Apple Intelligence for setup? No. Use the manual editor and add the trigger and import action yourself.
 Will old messages import automatically? No. The automation responds to new matching messages after setup; you can copy an older alert into the app’s message reader yourself.
 Does every bank work? No. Formats vary, so test your own alert and review the first imported transaction.
 Sources:  Apple: add automations on iOS 27 ,  Apple: communication triggers ,  Apple: use variables , and the app’s setup screens. ## 50/30/20 Budget: How to Split Your Take-Home Pay
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/50-30-20-budget.html
 50/30/20 Budget: How to Split Your Take-Home Pay  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    What counts as needs, wants and savings    Work out your three amounts on iPhone    A worked example with real numbers    Plan it in TrackExpenses    Check it at the end of the month    Limits to know    Frequently asked questions
 To do a 50/30/20 budget, take your monthly take-home pay and plan 50% of it for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for savings: on a take-home of 12,000 that is 6,000, 3,600 and 2,400. Then sort every spending category into one of the three groups and check, each month, that your actual spending stayed close to those amounts.
 What counts as needs, wants and savings
 The split was popularised by the book All Your Worth by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi (2005). It works on take-home pay: what reaches your account after tax and deductions. Where salaries are not taxed, that is simply the salary that arrives.

  Needs (50%)  are payments you would have to make even in a tight month: rent or mortgage, utilities, groceries, insurance, getting to work, childcare and the minimum payment on any loan or card.
  Wants (30%)  are the things you choose: eating out, delivery, shopping, entertainment, travel and most subscriptions.
  Savings (20%)  is money you keep: an emergency fund, investments, retirement, and loan payments above the minimum.

 Decide the grey areas once and keep them there. A gym membership can be a want; a phone plan is usually a need, an upgrade is a want. Consistency matters more than the perfect label: the point is to compare months.
 Work out your three amounts on iPhone
 The  50/30/20 budget calculator  does the arithmetic in your browser. On iPhone, open Calculator, type your take-home pay and multiply by 0.5, then 0.3, then 0.2. Apple's  Calculator guide  covers the basic keypad.
 For a reusable sheet, open Numbers, type your take-home pay into one cell and add three result cells. Apple's  Numbers formula instructions  explain how to tap a result cell, open the Formula Editor, tap the pay cell and multiply it by 0.5, 0.3 or 0.2. When your pay changes, the three amounts update with it.
 Then list your categories in two columns, needs and wants, and write a monthly amount beside each. Add the needs: if they come to more than half your pay, you have found the real constraint before you spend anything.
 A worked example with real numbers
 Take-home pay is 12,000 a month. The targets are 6,000 for needs, 3,600 for wants and 2,400 for savings.
 Here is one way to fill the three groups, with each line's share of pay:

 Needs: Rent 4,000 (33%), Groceries 1,200 (10%), Transport 500 (4%), Utilities and phone 300 (3%). Total 6,000, 50%.
 Wants: Dining out 1,000 (8%), Shopping 800 (7%), Entertainment 600 (5%), Everything else 1,200 (10%). Total 3,600, 30%.
 Savings: transfer to a savings account 2,400. Total 2,400, 20%.

 Planned spending is 9,600, which is 80% of pay, and with savings the plan uses all 12,000. The shares are rounded to whole numbers, so a group's lines can add up to one percent more or less than its total.
 If rent were 5,000 instead, needs would reach 7,000, or 58%. The honest choices are to accept a different split for now, such as 60/20/20, or to cut a need. Taking the difference out of savings without noticing is how a 50/30/20 plan quietly stops working.
 Plan it in TrackExpenses
 TrackExpenses does the same split with its salary plan, a Pro feature. Open Stats, choose Budget and tap Salary plan, the first row.

  Income:  tap Add your income and enter your take-home pay under Monthly income. If a repeating salary rule exists, the Repeating income suggestion fills it in with one tap.
  Spending:  under Spending, tap each need and want and enter its amount. The editor reminds you that this is the category's budget too, so the plan and your budget bars always agree. Categories you do not plan one by one are counted in Everything else.
  Savings:  add a Savings or Investment account in the Accounts tab, if you have none, then plan your 20% on it under Saving & investing.

 Every line shows its share of your income, and the Spending and Saving & investing headers show their totals with a percentage. In the example, Spending reads 9,600 and 80%, Saving & investing 2,400 and 20%, and the plan says Your income covers your plan exactly. Plan less and it tells you how much is still to plan; plan more and it says how much your income is short.
 Your plan follows your budget month, so if you are paid on the 25th, set More → Period & Entry first; the  payday budget guide  walks through it. Since version 1.10.0, each month can keep its own amounts: a change carries to later months unless one has its own, and months already lived keep what they had.
 Check it at the end of the month
 The budget only helps if you compare it with what happened. Switch the salary plan from Plan to Actual to see Received, Spent and Saved for the month, and on each line how much you spent of the planned amount and how much is left or over. Saved is what reached the account: money moved or paid in, less anything taken out.
 During the month, the  budget pacing guide  explains how to read the spending bar against the today marker. If one category runs over while another has room, Move money between them for this month only; see the  budget planner page .
 Record a transfer to savings as a transfer, not an expense, or it will be counted twice. The  credit card guide  explains the same rule for card payments.
 Limits to know
 The app does not label categories as needs or wants. You decide which category belongs where and add up each group from its lines; naming categories clearly helps.
 Saving & investing only lists Savings and Investment accounts. Extra loan payments are not a line there, so plan them with your own category if you record them as spending.
 The salary plan requires Pro. Without it, you can still set a total and category budgets under More → Budgets and record transfers to a savings account, but the plan's income, percentages and Plan versus Actual view are Pro. The free version includes 3 accounts. Everything depends on your records: an unrecorded cash purchase is invisible to any budget. This guide explains a method, not financial advice.
 Frequently asked questions
 Is 50/30/20 based on gross or take-home pay? Take-home pay: what you actually receive after tax and deductions. Using gross pay overstates every amount.
 What if my needs are more than 50%? Write down the real figure and adjust the split, for example 60/20/20, while you work on the largest need. A plan you can follow is more useful than a ratio you always miss.
 Do loan payments count as needs or savings? The minimum payment is a need. Anything above the minimum is part of the 20% savings group.
 Can TrackExpenses show my 50/30/20 percentages? The Pro salary plan shows each line's share of your income and the total share for spending and for saving. It does not group categories into needs and wants for you.
 Sources: Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi,  All Your Worth , Free Press, 2005; Apple's Calculator and Numbers guides linked above; TrackExpenses 1.10.0 SalaryPlanScreen, SalaryPlan, Account and FreeTier checked on 4 November 2026. Figures are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login. ## Log Expenses with Siri and Shortcuts on iPhone
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/log-expenses-with-siri.html
 Log Expenses with Siri, Widgets and Shortcuts on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    The method that works anywhere    Doing it in TrackExpenses    A worked example    Limits and common mistakes    Frequently asked questions
 You can track spending on iPhone without opening an app each time: ask Siri what you can spend today, keep your budget on the Home Screen or Lock Screen, and log a regular purchase with one tap from a widget, Control Center or the Action button. TrackExpenses provides all of these, and More → Siri, Shortcuts & Widgets in the app shows each one with your own figures.
 The method that works anywhere
 Before any app, iPhone already gives you two quick habits. A Notes checklist pinned to the top of Notes holds the day's purchases, and a Reminders list with a daily alert at the end of the day prompts you to write them down. Both work, and both leave the arithmetic to you: neither knows your budget, how many days are left before payday, or whether today's coffee leaves room for tomorrow.
 The step that makes quick logging worth it is a number you can act on in the moment. A budget is only useful at the till if you know what is left for today, not just what is left for the month. That is the figure TrackExpenses puts on the Lock Screen and gives to Siri.
 Doing it in TrackExpenses
  Ask Siri.  Say the app's name in the phrase. "What can I spend today in TrackExpenses" answers with what is left of today's daily budget: the period's budget after repeating bills, shared across the days left. "How much did I spend on Groceries in TrackExpenses" names the category's spending against its budget, using your own category names. "How's my budget in TrackExpenses" and "What's my net worth in TrackExpenses" work the same way. Siri asks you to unlock the iPhone before it reads out any figure.
  Log by voice.  "Tell TrackExpenses what I spent" asks what you spent; answer naturally, such as "coffee 15 and taxi 40 with cash". Siri reads back what it heard and asks before saving. Each entry counts toward the free voice allowance of 10 saved voice entries a calendar month; Pro makes voice entry unlimited. "Log an expense in TrackExpenses" asks for an amount instead and is not counted.
  Log a template with one tap.  Turn on Save as template when you add an entry you repeat, such as the morning coffee or the bus fare. The Quick Log widget shows your templates as buttons: a tap logs the template's amount, category and account without opening the app. The widget marks the tile and says the entry is waiting until the app next opens, when it lands in the ledger. "Log my Coffee in TrackExpenses" does the same through Siri.
  Widgets.  Touch and hold an empty part of the Home Screen, tap Edit, then Add Widget, and search for TrackExpenses. There are seven: Today (what is left to spend today), Budget (what is left this period with a marker for today's place in it), Quick Log, Category Budgets, Spending Overview (today, the last two weeks, income and net balance), Accounts (net worth and balances) and Quick Add (type, say or paste). Quick Log, Category Budgets and Accounts can be set to one template, category or account: touch and hold the widget and choose Edit Widget.
  Lock Screen.  Touch and hold the Lock Screen, tap Customize, choose the Lock Screen, then tap the widget area and pick TrackExpenses. Today and Budget fit as a ring or a line of text; Quick Log fits as a button. On an iPhone with a passcode, the figures stay hidden until you unlock it.
  Control Center and the Action button.  On iOS 18 and later, open Control Center, tap the plus at the top, choose Add a Control and search for TrackExpenses. Five controls are available: Quick Log, Today's Budget, Add an Expense, Say an Expense and Paste an Expense. Quick Log asks which template to log when you add it. On an iPhone with an Action button, Settings → Action Button → Controls lets you choose one of them for a single press.
 A worked example
 Say your monthly budget is 4,000 and rent of 1,500 is set up as a repeating bill. Twenty days are left, and 1,300 has gone on everyday spending so far. The daily budget is (4,000 − 1,500 − 1,300) ÷ 20 = 60. At lunch you ask Siri what you can spend today; it answers that you have 60 left, out of 60. You buy a sandwich and tap the Lunch tile on the Quick Log widget, which logs 25 under Food. The Today widget on your Lock Screen then shows 35 left today. Spend nothing more, and tomorrow's daily budget rises a little, because today's unspent 35 is shared across the days that remain.
 Limits and common mistakes
 Siri's spending answers need a budget. With no budget set, "what can I spend today" tells you what you have spent today and suggests setting one. The daily budget figures on widgets and in Siri are part of Pro; free users see today's spending in their place, and "budget used up" is always shown free.
 A Quick Log tap made while the app is closed waits in a queue and is added the next time you open TrackExpenses. Totals on other widgets include it from then. If you tap by mistake, delete the entry in the app as you would any other.
 Transfers between your own accounts need the app. Siri logs purchases and income; a sentence that moves money from cash to savings is left out and Siri says so.
 Control Center controls need iOS 18 or later. Widgets, Siri and Shortcuts work from iOS 17.
 Frequently asked questions
 Are the widgets free? Yes. Every widget, control and Siri action is free to use. The daily budget figure they show is part of Pro, and voice entry includes 10 free saved entries a month.
 Does TrackExpenses send my spending anywhere to answer Siri? No. The answers are worked out on your iPhone from a summary the app keeps on the device, the same one the widgets read.
 Why does my Quick Log widget say an entry is waiting? The tap was saved while the app was closed. Open TrackExpenses and it is added to the ledger at once.
 Can I choose which category a widget follows? Yes. Touch and hold the Category Budgets widget, choose Edit Widget and pick a category. Accounts and Quick Log work the same way.

## Import Bank Email Alerts on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/bank-email-alerts-iphone.html
 Import bank email alerts on iPhone, from Gmail or any account  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    What Shortcuts can and can't see    Step 1: add Gmail to the Mail app    Step 2: create the Email automation    Step 3: hand the email to TrackExpenses    iOS 27, screen by screen    Check an alert before the next purchase    Limits worth knowing    Privacy    Frequently asked questions
 If your bank emails you about card payments, a Shortcuts Email automation can pass each alert to TrackExpenses, the same way the SMS automation passes a text. Shortcuts can't see inside the Gmail app, so the one extra step is adding your Gmail account to Apple's Mail app, which is what the Email trigger watches.
 What Shortcuts can and can't see
 The Email trigger in Shortcuts runs when Apple's Mail app receives a message that matches your filter. It has no access to the Gmail app, Outlook or any other mail app, and no automation can read a notification banner. That is why the steps below begin in Settings rather than in Shortcuts.
 Adding the account to Mail doesn't change how you read email: keep using the Gmail app. Mail only needs a copy of the alerts. If you don't want two notifications for every email, turn off notifications for Mail in Settings → Notifications → Mail. The automation still runs.
 The filter works on the subject line, much as the SMS automation works on the message's wording. Shortcuts offers no "body contains" option for email, only Sender and Subject. Open three or four alert emails from your bank and find a word that every alert subject contains and marketing emails don't, such as "transaction", "purchase" or "alert". That word is your filter.
 Step 1: add Gmail to the Mail app
 Open Settings → Apps → Mail → Mail Accounts → Add Account and choose Google. Sign in to the Gmail account your bank writes to, and leave Mail switched on for it. On iOS 17, the same screen is Settings → Mail → Accounts.
 Apple's Mail app checks Gmail on a schedule rather than receiving each email the moment it lands. On the Mail Accounts screen, open Fetch New Data and choose Every 15 Minutes, the shortest interval. An alert can therefore reach your ledger a few minutes after the email arrives. Opening Mail makes it check at once.
 iCloud Mail, Outlook and most other accounts work the same way.
 Step 2: create the Email automation
 The editor changed in iOS 27. The app shows the steps for your version too: More → SMS Auto-Import → Bank alerts by email?
 On iOS 27, open Shortcuts, go back to Library, choose Automation and tap +. If Describe a Shortcut opens, tap Editor. Tap Automation in the actions panel, then Email under Communication. The trigger reads "When I receive an email where Sender is Email Address". Tap Sender and choose Subject, then enter your filter word. Expand the trigger with its blue arrow: keep Automation on and Confirm Before Run off.
 On iOS 26 and earlier, open the Automation tab, tap + and choose Email. Tap Subject Contains, enter your filter word and leave Sender empty. Choose Run Immediately, tap Next and choose Create New Shortcut (New Blank Automation on iOS 18 and earlier). Do not choose one of the ready-made TrackExpenses tiles: they can't receive the email.
 Step 3: hand the email to TrackExpenses
 Add TrackExpenses' Import Bank Message action. It appears as "Import transaction from Message". The blue Message placeholder must be connected to the incoming email. A blank placeholder doesn't fill itself in.
 On iOS 27, tap Message, then Select Variable in the bottom bar, and tap Email directly below the trigger. Tap the inserted Email variable and choose Content from its Get list, which is the body of the email. On iOS 26, tap Message → Select Variable → Shortcut Input.
 Finally, expand the action with its arrow and switch off Show When Run, so it never stops to ask for text. Save the shortcut. The SMS automation needs the same connection; see the  bank SMS guide .
 iOS 27, screen by screen
 These are the real Shortcuts screens on iOS 27, in order.
   Choose Email  In Shortcuts, go to Library → Automation → +, tap Automation and choose Email under Communication.     Filter on the subject  Tap Sender, switch it to Subject and enter your word. Keep Automation on and Confirm Before Run off.     Add the import action  Search for Import Bank Message and add it. Its Message field is still empty.     Choose the email  Tap Message, then Select Variable, and tap Email right below the trigger.     Use the email's content  Tap the Email variable you just inserted and choose Content.     Turn Show When Run off  Expand the action with its arrow, switch Show When Run off and save.
 Check an alert before the next purchase
 Copy the text of one real alert email from Gmail. In TrackExpenses, open More → SMS Auto-Import, find "Try one of your bank's messages" and paste it. The card shows what the automation would do with that email: the amount, whether it is spending or money in, the merchant and the account, or why it would skip it. Nothing is saved.
 Look at what comes back. If the email was about a 45.67 card payment, you want a 45.67 expense with the shop's name. If the card shows another figure, such as the balance, or says it would skip the email, the automation would do the same. It is better to know now than after a week of missing entries, and a copy of that alert sent to support, with your name and account number removed, is how the reader learns your bank's format.
 After the next real alert, look at Recent activity on the same screen. Each run is listed with what it imported or why it skipped the email. No run at all points at the trigger: the subject word, or Mail not having fetched the email yet.
 Limits worth knowing
 Some banks send an email that only says "you have a new alert, sign in to view it". There is no amount in it, so nothing can be imported; ask the bank for full transaction alerts, or use SMS if it offers them.
 One email is one entry. A daily summary that lists several purchases is not split into several entries. Statements sent as PDF attachments are not read.
 Email alerts go through the same reader, rules and review as bank texts. One-time codes, declined payments, offers and unclear alerts are skipped. A purchase in another currency waits for your exchange rate, and a possible duplicate is flagged for review. If your bank sends the same purchase by SMS and by email, set up only one of the two, or every purchase arrives twice.
 Email imports count towards the same allowance as SMS imports: 10 successful automatic imports per calendar month on each device for free, unlimited with Pro.
 Privacy
 Shortcuts passes only the emails that match your filter, and only their content. TrackExpenses reads the text on your iPhone and keeps the transaction it found, never the email itself. It never signs in to Gmail or your bank. The  privacy policy  has the details.
 Frequently asked questions
 Can TrackExpenses read the Gmail app directly? No. Shortcuts' Email trigger only sees mail in Apple's Mail app, so add your Gmail account there.
 Why use the subject and not the sender? It mirrors the SMS setup, which matches the alert's wording rather than who sent it. Banks often send alerts from more than one address, while their alert subjects stay the same.
 Why did an import arrive late? Mail fetches Gmail on a schedule. Set Fetch New Data to Every 15 Minutes, or open Mail.
 My bank only sends app notifications. What can I do? Shortcuts can't read notifications. If you pay with Apple Pay, a Wallet Transaction automation covers those purchases; text your bank app lets you copy can be pasted into a new transaction.
 It still doesn't import. Where do I start? Follow the SMS troubleshooting guide, with Email in place of Message. Or contact support with the activity entry and a copy of the alert with your name and account number removed.
 Sources: Apple's  communication triggers  documentation, the Shortcuts app on iOS 27.2 and the TrackExpenses app, checked in November 2026. ## How to Set a Daily Spending Limit | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/daily-spending-limit.html
 How to set a daily spending limit  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Work it out on iPhone in a minute    Why bills come out first and today counts    Work it out once a day, not after every purchase    Keep the limit on screen in TrackExpenses    A daily limit for one category or a trip    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 A daily spending limit is the money left in your budget divided by the days left until the budget period ends, today included: 1,800 left with 15 days to go is 120 a day. Take out the bills still due before you divide, or the limit looks bigger than it really is.
 Work it out on iPhone in a minute
 You need four figures for the same period: the budget, what you have spent so far, the bills still to come before the period ends, and the number of days left. Use one currency and one period for all of them. If your month runs from payday on the 25th, count from the 25th, not from the 1st.

 Money left = budget − spent so far − bills still due.
 Days left = every day from today to the last day of the period, today included.
 Daily limit = money left ÷ days left, rounded down.

 Calculator on iPhone is enough, or use the free  daily budget calculator , which lets you subtract commitments before it divides.
 Here is a worked example. Your monthly budget is 4,000 for 25 October to 24 November. On the morning of 10 November you have spent 1,800, and a phone bill of 150 and a gym renewal of 250 are still to come. Money left is 4,000 − 1,800 − 400 = 1,800. From 10 to 24 November is 15 days. 1,800 ÷ 15 = 120 a day.
 Why bills come out first and today counts
 Skip the bills and you would divide 2,200 by 15 and get 146.66 a day. Spend that every day and the phone bill and the gym arrive with nothing left to pay them. A bill you know is coming is not money you can spend, so it leaves the pot before the pot is shared.
 Today counts because you can still spend today. Dividing by 14 instead of 15 would hand you 128.57 a day and leave the last day of the period empty. Rounding down does the same job in small: a limit that is a fraction too low never runs out early.
 Work it out once a day, not after every purchase
 Set the limit in the morning from what was left when the day began, then let today's purchases count against it. If you recalculate after every coffee, the limit drifts all day and stops being a number you can plan with.
 The next morning the arithmetic moves on by itself. Spend 90 of your 120 today and tomorrow's limit is (1,800 − 90) ÷ 14 = 122.14. Spend 200 and it drops to 114.28. Underspending raises the days ahead a little, overspending lowers them, and nobody has to make up a lost day by hand.
 Keep the limit on screen in TrackExpenses
 Set a budget under More → Budgets: the Total budget is the one the daily figure shares. Your budget month follows the start day in More → Period & Entry, so a payday month works the same way. Enter rent, phone and subscriptions as rules under More → Recurring so the app knows which bills are coming; two rules are free, more come with Pro.
 The Daily list then opens with a Today card: your daily budget, what you have spent today and what is left today, with a bar. Tap it for the working, line by line: the Monthly budget, minus Repeating bills (paid already or still to come this period), minus spending before today, gives what was Left when today began, divided by the Days left, including today. The result is rounded down in your currency's precision and holds still all day. Under it, the sheet tells you what tomorrow's figure will be if you spend nothing more.
 You can also ask Siri "What can I spend today in TrackExpenses", or keep the Today widget on your Lock Screen; the  Siri and widgets guide  shows both.
 The daily figure is part of Pro. Budgets, the pacing bars and the spent and left amounts are free, and when the budget is used up the app says so for free, with how far over you are and the days left, because that is a basic fact about your budget.
 A daily limit for one category or a trip
 Sometimes the whole budget is the wrong pot. With Pro, tap the Today card, then Daily budget for, and choose Chosen categories. Only categories with a budget of their own are listed; tick one, such as Groceries, or several, such as Food and Transport, and they are read as one daily budget.
 Turn on Stop on a date and pick a Last day inside the current budget period, and what is left is shared across the days up to that date instead of to the end of the period. That suits a trip: Travel with 3,000 left and ten days to go is 300 a day. The day after the last day, the daily budget is your whole budget again. Your budgets don't change, and widgets and Siri keep to the whole budget.
 Stats → Budget also shows a daily amount on each category budget with Pro, with that category's own repeating bills taken out first. A category that holds only bills shows none. The  budget planner page  shows the screens.
 What it doesn't do
 The daily limit is a budget reference, not a bank balance or a card limit. It doesn't stop a payment, and it only knows what you have recorded: a bill you never entered as a rule or an expense is not taken out. There is no daily amount to type in by hand either; change the period's budget and the daily figure follows, so the two can never disagree.
 The budget is kept in one period length, a week, a month or a year, and a period starts on a fixed day. There is no every-two-weeks budget period, so pay every other Friday needs a monthly or weekly convention you stick to.
 Frequently asked questions
 Should I count today in the days left? Yes. You can still spend today, so leaving it out gives every remaining day a little too much and leaves nothing for the last one.
 Why did my daily limit go down overnight? You spent more than the limit yesterday, so less is left to share across the days that remain. It also drops when a new bill is added that falls inside the period.
 Do I need Pro for a daily spending limit? Not for the arithmetic: the calculator is free, and so are budgets and pacing in the app. The app's daily figure, the per-category daily amounts and the daily budget for chosen categories are part of Pro.
 Can I set a fixed daily allowance instead? Not in TrackExpenses. The daily budget is always worked out from the period's budget, so lower or raise that budget to change it.
 Sources: TrackExpenses InsightsEngine (TodayBudget), TodayBudgetSheet, DailyBudgetFocus and FreeTier, checked in November 2026;  Apple's iPhone Calculator guide . Figures are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login.
