## Track Travel Expenses Abroad on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/travel-expenses-abroad.html
 Track travel expenses abroad on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Start with what your iPhone already keeps    Decide which rate you will use    Set up TrackExpenses before you fly    Log each purchase in the currency you paid    A daily budget for the trip    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 Record each purchase in the currency you paid, with the exchange rate your card or exchange office really used, and let one main currency carry every total. TrackExpenses does this in the free ledger: a main currency for totals, additional currencies for the trip, and your own rate on each entry.
 Start with what your iPhone already keeps
 Wallet keeps a record for some cards. Open Wallet, tap a supported card and scroll down to see its recent activity; Wallet can also search by merchant, date, amount or location. It only covers that one card, only purchases its bank shares with Wallet, and never the cash you spent.
 Calculator converts currencies too. Its Convert mode, and Math Notes, change euros or baht into your own money at a recent market rate. That is a good check at the till, but your card's rate usually includes the bank's margin and sometimes a separate foreign fee, so it is not the figure that leaves your account.
 For a written log, a note per trip works: date, what, amount and currency on each line. Numbers is better for totals, with a table of Date, What, Amount, Currency and Rate columns and a formula for Amount × Rate. Its Travel Planner template, under Personal when you tap Choose a Template, is a start. The weak points are the same everywhere: a total per currency done by hand, and cash forgotten by day three.
 Decide which rate you will use
 The true rate is the one in your own currency on your bank's alert or statement. If a 50.00 euro dinner shows as 213.50 on your card, the rate was 4.27, fees included. Use that figure for the rest of the trip's card purchases and correct it if a later alert shows the rate moved.
 Cash has its own rate. If you changed 1,000 into 230 euros at the airport, each euro cost 4.35, and that is the rate for everything you pay from that cash. A separate fee for using the card abroad is an expense of its own, so log it as one line rather than hiding it in a rate.
 Set up TrackExpenses before you fly
 Check More → Main Currency: every total, budget and account balance is reported in it. Then open More → Additional Currencies and add the currencies of the trip, such as EUR and THB. Multi-currency is free.
 If you will carry foreign cash, add an account in that currency under Accounts and record the exchange as a transfer from your bank account into it, so the cash isn't counted as spending twice. The  cash expenses guide  walks through it. The free ledger holds three accounts; more come with Pro.
 For a trip budget, add a Travel category under More → Expense Categories and give it a budget under More → Budgets.
 Log each purchase in the currency you paid
 In a new entry, type the amount, then tap the Currency row and choose the trip's currency. The row appears once you have more than one currency. A Rate to AED row follows (your main currency's code), filled with the last rate you used for that currency. A foreign entry can't be saved without a rate: saved at 1, a 45 euro taxi would be counted as AED 45, and that currency's history would be wrong from then on.
 Each entry keeps the rate it was saved with, and every total converts at those rates, so a trip in three currencies still adds up to one figure. Accounts kept in a foreign currency are converted the same way, and the Accounts screen says so.
 Voice entry hears the currency too. Say "taxi 18 euros" and the draft shows the Currency and the rate, prefilled, before you save. Ten saved voice entries a month are free, and the  voice guide  covers devices and languages.
 Bank alerts from abroad go through the same rules. When the alert prints the amount in your own currency beside the foreign one, as in "EUR 50.00 (AED 213.50)", the entry imports at what your bank charged. Otherwise it imports at the last rate you used for that currency and is flagged so you can check the rate, or it waits for a rate if you have never used one. A foreign row is never saved at 1.
 A daily budget for the trip
 With Pro, the daily budget can follow the trip instead of the whole month. Tap the Today card at the top of the Daily list, then Daily budget for, choose Chosen categories and tick Travel. Turn on Stop on a date and pick the trip's last day as the Last day.
 Say Travel has a budget of 6,000 and the flights took 1,500 before you left. On the first morning of a ten-day trip, 4,500 shared across ten days is 450 a day. Spend 380 today and tomorrow's figure rises a little; spend 600 and it drops. The working on the Today sheet counts the days up to your last day, today included. The day after the trip, the daily budget is your whole budget again, and your budgets never change.
 The last day has to fall inside the current budget period. A trip that runs past payday into the next period can be planned only to the end of this one, then chosen again. Outside a trip, the  daily spending limit guide  explains the same arithmetic for the whole budget.
 What it doesn't do
 TrackExpenses doesn't fetch exchange rates from the internet. You enter the rate, prefilled from the last one, so totals match what your bank charged rather than a market rate it never gave you. If a card charge settles a few days later at a different figure, edit the entry's amount or rate.
 It doesn't split a shared dinner between friends or keep a trip as a separate ledger. A trip is a category, a budget and, if you want, a cash account; after you come home, the Travel category's total in Stats is the trip's cost in your main currency.
 Frequently asked questions
 Does TrackExpenses update exchange rates automatically? No. You enter the rate for each foreign entry, prefilled with the last rate you used for that currency, so the totals match what you really paid.
 Should I record the foreign amount or the amount in my own currency? Record the amount you paid, in the currency you paid it, with the rate. Your main-currency total then follows, and the receipt and the ledger show the same number.
 Is multi-currency a Pro feature? No. A main currency, additional currencies and your own rates are part of the free ledger. The daily budget for chosen categories up to a date is part of Pro.
 How do I track foreign cash? Add an account in that currency, record the exchange as a transfer into it, and log each purchase from that account at the rate the cash cost you.
 Sources: Apple's  Wallet guide  and  Math Notes guide ; TrackExpenses EntrySheet, LedgerStore, BankMessageParser, DailyBudgetFocus and FreeTier, checked in November 2026. ## Get Reminded Before Bills Are Due on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/bill-reminders-iphone.html
 Get reminded before bills are due on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Set a repeating reminder in the Reminders app    Turn on bill reminders in TrackExpenses    What the reminder says    Which bills get a reminder    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 The Reminders app on iPhone can warn you before every bill: give each one a repeating reminder with its due date and an early reminder a day or two before. If you already track your bills in TrackExpenses, turn on Remind me the day before under More → Recurring and you get one notification at 9:00 the morning before each repeating expense is due, free.
 Set a repeating reminder in the Reminders app
 Reminders is already on your iPhone and needs nothing else. For each bill:

 Open Reminders and tap New Reminder. Write the bill and its usual amount, such as "Rent 4,300".
 Tap the info button to open the reminder's details. Turn on Date and pick the next due date; turn on Time if you want a set hour.
 Tap Repeat and choose Monthly, or Every 3 Months for a quarterly bill.
 Tap Early Reminder and choose how long before, such as 2 days before. Then tap Done.

 Each time the reminder comes round, tick it off and the next one is set from the repeat. Apple's  Reminders guide  shows the same steps with each button.
 App Store subscriptions carry their own dates: Settings, then your name, then Subscriptions lists each one with its renewal date.
 The Reminders route works, but it is a second list to keep. When the rent goes up, the reminder still says the old amount, and ticking a reminder doesn't mean the money was ready.
 Turn on bill reminders in TrackExpenses
 If your bills are already in TrackExpenses as recurring rules, the reminders can come from the same list that writes them into your ledger. Open More → Recurring and tap + for each bill: choose Expense, the amount, the category and the account it is paid from, set Repeats to Every Month (the step beside it makes a quarterly bill every 3 months), and pick the next due date as the First occurrence. The  subscriptions and recurring bills guide  covers the rules in detail. Two rules are free; Pro makes them unlimited.
 Once there is a repeating expense, the Recurring screen opens with one switch: Remind me the day before. Turn it on and iOS asks whether TrackExpenses may send notifications. If you decline, the switch stays off; if you turn notifications off later in Settings, the screen says so and offers Open Settings.
 With the switch on, a Next reminder row says when the next notification will arrive and which bill it is about. Bill reminders are free for everyone.
 What the reminder says
 A notification arrives at 9:00 the day before the bill comes out, early enough to move money the same day. The time is shown the way your iPhone writes times.
 For one bill, the title names it: "Rent is due tomorrow". The body gives the amount, the account it comes from and the day itself, "AED 4,300.00 from Main Bank · Tuesday, 1 December", because a notification read the next morning still says "tomorrow".
 When several bills fall on the same day you get one notification, not several. The title says "2 bills are due tomorrow", and the body names them biggest first with the total in your main currency, such as "Internet and Gym · AED 600.00 in all". With more than three, it names the two biggest and how many more. Tapping a reminder opens the Recurring screen.
 A worked example: you are paid on the 25th, rent of 4,300 leaves Main Bank on the 1st, and internet (350) and the gym (250) both renew on the 5th. On Monday 30 November at 9:00 you are told about the rent; on Friday 4 December, about internet and the gym together. Your salary rule sends nothing.
 Which bills get a reminder

 Repeating expenses above zero whose Active switch is on. A rule you have switched off sends nothing.
 Never income. A salary's real day is your employer's, and money arriving needs no warning.
 Bills that repeat weekly or less often. Rules that repeat more often than once a week, such as every day or every three days, are left out: a reminder every morning teaches you to ignore the one about the rent.
 The amount is in the rule's own currency, so a subscription billed in dollars is announced in dollars.

 A reminder whose moment has passed is never sent late. Add a rule at lunchtime for a bill due tomorrow, and the 9:00 reminder for it has already gone by, so nothing arrives.
 What it doesn't do
 You can't choose another hour or two days' notice, and there is no switch per bill; it is one setting for every repeating expense. If you need a longer warning for one bill, give that bill a reminder in the Reminders app as well.
 Reminders are written up to 60 days ahead and topped up each time you open TrackExpenses. Leave the app closed for two months and they run out until you open it again.
 The switch is a setting of each device. Your rules sync through iCloud, but an iPad gets reminders only if you turn the switch on there too, and with both on, both devices remind you.
 A reminder announces the rule's amount. For a bill that changes, such as electricity, set the rule to a typical amount and edit the entry when the real bill arrives. TrackExpenses doesn't pay anything or check that a payment went through; a bank alert or the entry itself is your confirmation.
 Frequently asked questions
 Can I be reminded two days before instead of one? Not in TrackExpenses: its reminders always come at 9:00 the day before. For a longer warning, set an Early Reminder on that bill in the Reminders app.
 Why didn't I get a reminder for my salary? Income is never announced. Only repeating expenses get a reminder.
 Why is a daily expense left out? Rules that repeat more often than once a week are skipped, so the reminders stay worth reading.
 Are bill reminders free? Yes. The switch is free for everyone. The free ledger holds two recurring rules and Pro makes them unlimited, so every subscription can be reminded.
 Will several bills on the same day send several notifications? No. Everything due on one day comes as one notification that names each bill and the total.
 Sources: Apple's  Reminders guide  and the Reminders app on iOS 26.5; TrackExpenses BillReminderPlanner, BillReminders and the Recurring screen, checked in November 2026. Amounts are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login. ## Get an Alert Before You Overspend | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/budget-alerts-iphone.html
 Get an alert before you overspend  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    What iPhone and your bank already offer    Turn on budget alerts in TrackExpenses    When an alert comes    Quiet by design    After the alert    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 iPhone has no budget alert of its own, so the built-in options are your bank app's balance or spending alerts and a reminder to check in. TrackExpenses adds free budget alerts: a notification when a budget passes 80% while it is ahead of its pace, and another when it goes over, with what is left and the days it has to last.
 What iPhone and your bank already offer
 Many bank apps can notify you about a large card payment or a balance below an amount you choose; look in your bank app's notification or alert settings. These alerts watch an account, not a budget. A low-balance alert arrives when the money is nearly gone, and a large-payment alert says nothing about fifteen small ones.
 Wallet shows recent activity on supported cards, but it has no spending limit to warn you about. The Reminders app can at least give you a habit: a reminder called "Check my spending" with Repeat set to Weekly, every Sunday evening.
 A spreadsheet can colour a warning. In Numbers, a total that passes a figure can turn red with Conditional Highlighting. It only changes colour when you open the sheet, so it tells you after the fact rather than at the moment you spend.
 Turn on budget alerts in TrackExpenses
 Alerts need a budget to watch. Open More → Budgets and set a Total budget, category budgets, or both; Stats → Budget → Edit budgets opens the same screen. Once a budget exists, the screen shows a switch at the top: Budget alerts.
 Turn it on and iOS asks whether TrackExpenses may send notifications. If notifications are later turned off in Settings, the screen says so and offers Open Settings. Budget alerts are free for everyone, like the budgets they watch, and the switch is a setting of each device.
 When an alert comes
 The app watches the whole budget and every category budget in the budget's own current period. Two moments are worth a notification.
  Near: 80% spent, ahead of pace.  Every budget bar in the app has a marker for where today falls in the period. An alert at 80% comes only when the bar is past that marker. Say Groceries has a budget of 1,000 for a 30-day month. On day 12 you reach 820: 82% spent with 40% of the month gone. You get "Groceries budget: 82% spent" and "AED 180.00 left for 19 days." Reach 850 on day 27 instead, and nothing arrives: 85% spent with 90% of the month gone is a budget working as planned. The  budget pacing guide  explains the marker.
  Over: past the budget.  When spending passes a budget, you get "Over the Food budget" and "AED 40.00 over, with 12 days left." A budget that jumps straight from below 80% to over gets the over alert only. For the whole budget the titles read "Your budget is 84% spent" and "You're over your budget". On the period's last day the body says what is left for today, or how far over you are.
 Percentages are rounded down, so a budget is never called 80% before it is.
 Repeating bills don't set off the 80% alert. Rent filling the Household budget on the 1st is the plan, not a warning, so a budget filled only by repeating bills never gets the near alert. It still gets the over alert if it goes past.
 When several budgets cross a mark at the same moment, they arrive as one notification: "2 budgets need a look", with "Beauty: over and Fuel 89%" underneath. Up to four are named; past that, three and how many more.
 Tapping an alert opens Stats → Budget.
 Quiet by design
 An alert you get every day is an alert you stop reading, so each one is said once.

  A switch just turned on starts from where the budget stands.  A category already at 90% is not news to you; the app speaks about what happens next.
  Each mark is said once per period.  A new period starts clean.
  A mark is forgotten when the budget drops back under it,  because money was moved in or an entry was deleted. Cross it again and you hear about it again. Time passing alone never repeats an alert.
  Bank imports bring their alert with them.  When a bank SMS automation files a purchase, the check runs before the import finishes, so the alert arrives with the purchase that caused it rather than the next time you open the app.

 After the alert
 Open Stats → Budget and look at the line. If one budget ran short while another has room, tap ••• on it and choose Move money in, or tap Cover on a line that is over. Moves apply to this period only, keep the total unchanged, and are free; next month starts from your usual budgets. The  envelope budgeting guide  shows the method.
 With Pro, each category budget also shows a daily amount, so "AED 180.00 left for 19 days" becomes a figure for today. The  budget planner page  shows the screens.
 What it doesn't do
 The marks are fixed at 80% ahead of pace and over. You can't choose another percentage or switch alerts on for some categories only; it is one switch for every budget with an amount. Income, account balances and card limits are not watched.
 An alert knows only what is in your ledger. Cash you haven't entered and bills you haven't added can't set one off, and lowering a budget below what you have already spent sends the over alert a moment after you save.
 Frequently asked questions
 Why didn't I get an alert at 80%? Either spending was behind the period's pace, the budget held only repeating bills, or it was already past 80% when you turned the switch on.
 Can I change the 80% threshold? No. It is fixed at 80%, and only when spending is ahead of where today falls in the period, so a budget that is simply nearly finished near the end of the month stays quiet.
 Are budget alerts free? Yes. Budgets, the pacing bars, moves between budgets and budget alerts are all free. Daily amounts per budget are part of Pro.
 Will I get the same alert twice? Only if the budget drops back below the mark, for example after you move money in, and then crosses it again in the same period.
 Do alerts arrive on my iPad too? Each device has its own switch. Turn it on where you want alerts.
 Sources: TrackExpenses BudgetAlertPlanner, BudgetAlerts and the Budgets screen, checked in November 2026; Numbers and Reminders on iPhone. Amounts are examples, not financial advice. ## How to Track Expenses on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/track-expenses-iphone.html
 How to track expenses on iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Notes: the quickest start    Numbers: totals and categories    Wallet: a record you already have    An app: the ways an entry gets in    How to choose a method    Make it a habit    What an app can't do    Frequently asked questions
 To track expenses on iPhone, write down every purchase in one place on the day you make it, in a note, a Numbers table or an expense app, and total it by category once a week. The built-in apps cost nothing; an app such as TrackExpenses takes the typing off you with voice, bank alerts and Apple Pay automations.
 Notes: the quickest start
 Open Notes and start a note for the month. Write one line per purchase: the date, what it was and the amount, such as "12 Nov, groceries, 86.40". It takes seconds and works offline.
 For the total, Calculator's Math Notes adds figures for you: type an expression with an equal sign, such as 86.40 + 12.50 + 31 =, and the answer appears. A note has no categories and no budget, though, so "how much went on food this month" means reading every line.
 Numbers: totals and categories
 Numbers is free on iPhone and turns a list into totals. Tap Choose a Template and look under Personal Finance: Simple Budget and Personal Budget are ready-made, or start from a blank table with Date, Description, Category and Amount columns. A SUMIF formula then totals each category, and a chart shows where the money went.
 The cost is the typing. Opening a spreadsheet at the till, finding the next empty row and picking a category on a phone screen is where most spreadsheet budgets stop by week three.
 Wallet: a record you already have
 If you pay with Apple Pay, Wallet keeps part of the record for you. Tap a supported card and scroll to see its recent activity, or search by merchant, date or amount. It is a statement, not a budget: one card at a time, only what that card's bank shares, nothing in cash and no categories you choose.
 An app: the ways an entry gets in
 An expense app is worth it when it makes recording faster than forgetting. TrackExpenses works without a bank login and offers several routes into one ledger:

  Typing.  A keypad opens on the amount, then category, account and description. A shop you have used before fills in its usual category and account, arrows beside the date step a day at a time, and Save as template turns a repeat purchase into one tap from Quick Add.
  Voice.  Say "coffee 15, taxi 40 and lunch 60" and you get three drafts to check and save. Speech is processed on the device. Ten saved voice entries a month are free; Pro makes voice unlimited. See the  voice guide .
  Bank SMS.  A Shortcuts automation passes each bank text to the app, which reads the amount, merchant and direction and skips codes and declined payments. Ten successful imports a month are free on each device. Start with the  bank SMS guide .
  Bank emails.  If your bank emails instead, an Email automation does the same through Apple's Mail app: the  bank email guide .
  Apple Pay.  A Wallet Transaction automation sends each Apple Pay purchase's amount and merchant: the  Apple Pay guide .
  Pasting.  Copy a bank text or email alert, paste it into a new entry, and the amount, date and payee fill themselves in.
  Cash.  Cash leaves no alert, so treat it as an account: the  cash guide .

 There are shortcuts to all of this. Touch and hold the app icon for Say an expense, New expense, Paste bank message and Ask your coach, or use Siri and the widgets in the  Siri and widgets guide .
 How to choose a method
 Choose by where your money actually goes, not by the cleverest feature.

  Mostly card payments, and your bank texts or emails each one:  an automation records them for you. Check one real alert in the app before relying on it.
  Mostly cash or many small purchases:  voice or templates, because you record at the till in a few seconds.
  You don't want to share a bank login:  a manual or alert-based app; the  no-bank-connection guide  compares the options.
  You spend in several currencies:  record each purchase in its own currency with your rate, as the  travel guide  shows.
  You are paid on a fixed day:  start your budget month on payday so income and spending share a period; see the  payday guide .

 Most people mix two: an automation for cards, and voice or typing for cash.
 Make it a habit
 Record a purchase when it happens; an entry made at the till is accurate, while one made at the weekend is a guess. If you forget, More → Daily Reminder sends a nudge to log the day at a time you pick.
 Once a week, spend ten minutes on the list. Compare it with your bank's statement, fix a category or two, and delete anything recorded twice, such as a purchase that came by alert and was also typed. Then look at the budget: in TrackExpenses every budget bar has a marker for where today falls in the month, so you can see whether spending is running ahead of time, not just how much is gone.
 What an app can't do
 TrackExpenses doesn't connect to your bank or download your statements. Automations cover banks that send texts or emails; no iPhone automation can read a push notification, and Shortcuts shows its own banner when an automation runs. An entry is only as complete as the alerts and the cash you record, which is why the weekly check matters whichever method you choose.
 Frequently asked questions
 What is the easiest way to track expenses on iPhone? The one you keep doing. For most people that means an app that records card payments from bank alerts and takes cash by voice in a few seconds, checked once a week.
 Can iPhone track my spending automatically? Not by itself. Wallet shows activity on supported cards, and Shortcuts automations can pass bank texts, emails and Apple Pay purchases to an app that records them.
 Do I need to connect my bank account? No. A note, a Numbers sheet or an app such as TrackExpenses works from what you enter and from alerts your bank already sends you.
 Is TrackExpenses free? The ledger is free: unlimited manual entries, budgets, search and private iCloud sync, with three accounts, two recurring rules, and ten voice entries and ten bank SMS imports a month. Pro adds unlimited voice and imports, more accounts and rules, planning tools and every export.
 Sources: Apple's  Wallet guide ,  Math Notes guide  and Numbers templates; TrackExpenses FreeTier, EntrySheet and HomeScreenActions, checked in November 2026. Amounts are examples. ## Envelope Budgeting on iPhone Without Cash | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/envelope-budgeting-iphone.html
 Envelope budgeting on iPhone without cash or bank sync  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    How the envelope method works    Try it in Numbers first    Set up envelopes in TrackExpenses    Move money when an envelope runs short    A daily amount for each envelope    Filling the envelopes without bank sync    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 Envelope budgeting gives each kind of spending its own pot for the month, and when a pot is empty you either stop or move money in from another pot. On iPhone you can run it without cash or a bank connection: category budgets are the envelopes, and in TrackExpenses moving money between them for this month is free and leaves your total unchanged.
 How the envelope method works
 The paper version is a set of envelopes filled with cash on payday: groceries, transport, eating out, household. You pay groceries only from the groceries envelope. When it is empty, you stop buying groceries or take money out of another envelope, and the envelope you took from now holds less.
 Three rules make it work, and they survive without paper:

 Every envelope has an amount before the month starts.
 Spending comes out of one envelope, never out of the air.
 Moving money between envelopes never creates money; the total stays the same.

 Try it in Numbers first
 A small Numbers table is enough to learn the method. Make one row per envelope with four columns: Envelope, Budget, Spent and Left, where Left is Budget minus Spent. To move money, lower one Budget and raise another by the same amount, so their sum is unchanged.
 The weak point is the Spent column. Every purchase has to be found, added and typed into the right row by hand, and a table that is a week behind can't tell you whether eating out has room tonight.
 Set up envelopes in TrackExpenses
 Open More → Budgets. The Total budget is everything you plan to spend in the period; each category budget is an envelope. Your budget month follows the start day in More → Period & Entry, so the envelopes refill on payday if you are paid on the 25th.
 Whatever the categories don't claim becomes Everything else: total minus category budgets. It is the envelope for spending you don't plan by category, so nothing you spend falls outside the system.
 A worked example: a total of 6,000, with Groceries 1,500, Transport 600, Eating out 800 and Household 1,200. Everything else is 6,000 − 4,100 = 1,900.
 Stats → Budget then shows every envelope with what is spent and what is left, labelled, and a bar with a marker for where today falls in the period. The header says how many days are left. Budgets, the bars and moves are free.
 Move money when an envelope runs short
 On the 18th, Eating out has reached 860 of its 800, while Groceries has 420 left. Here is the envelope move, done on the phone.

 On the Eating out line, tap its Cover button, or tap ••• and choose Move money in.
 In the Move money sheet, choose Groceries under From if it isn't chosen already. Cover it fills in exactly the overspend; you can type another amount.
 Tap Move.

 Eating out now holds 860 and Groceries 1,440 for this month, and the total is still 6,000. Each line says how much moved in or out, so the change stays visible. Move money out works the other way round, from a budget with room into one that needs it, and you can take from Everything else too.
 A move is for this period only: the sheet says "Just for this month. Next month starts from your usual budgets." If the change should last, edit the standing amount in More → Budgets instead. Undo all moves, under the lines, puts every budget back to its usual amount for the period.
 Two guards keep the envelopes honest. Suggested amounts leave repeating bills still due in the source envelope covered: if Household still owes a 250 bill this month, All it can spare keeps 250 back. Type an amount that would take bill money and the sheet warns you before you move it.
 Moves are offered for the current period, in the length your budget is kept in. The  budget planner page  shows the screens.
 A daily amount for each envelope
 With Pro, every envelope also shows a daily amount: what is left in it after its own repeating bills, shared across the days left, today included. Groceries with 900 left and 12 days to go reads 75.00 a day. An envelope that holds only bills, such as rent, shows no daily figure, because there is nothing in it to spend day by day. The  daily spending limit guide  explains the arithmetic.
 Filling the envelopes without bank sync
 Bank-synced budget apps download your transactions; this method doesn't need that. Each purchase reaches an envelope through its category: typed in a few seconds, said by voice ("groceries 86 at Carrefour"), or brought in from your bank's SMS or email alert by a Shortcuts automation. A shop you have used before fills in its usual category, so a Carrefour purchase lands in Groceries without a choice. The  track expenses guide  compares the routes.
 The trade is a few seconds per purchase for a ledger that never asks for a bank password.
 What it doesn't do
 Unspent money doesn't roll over. Each period starts from your usual budgets, so 200 left in Transport this month doesn't add 200 to next month's Transport. If you want it saved, move it to a savings account as a transfer.
 Envelopes are expense budgets. Income isn't divided into envelopes here; to give every part of your pay a job before payday, see the  zero-based budget guide . There are no envelope groups or sub-envelopes either: a category is one envelope.
 Envelopes are budgets, not accounts. Your money still sits in your bank and cash accounts; the envelopes say what it is for.
 Frequently asked questions
 Can I do envelope budgeting without cash? Yes. Category budgets play the envelopes, and moving money between them for the current month keeps the total unchanged, the same way taking notes out of one envelope and putting them into another does.
 Does unspent money carry over to next month? No. Every period starts from your usual budgets. Change the standing amounts in More → Budgets if a category needs more every month.
 Is moving money between budgets free? Yes. Budgets, Move money, Cover and the spent and left amounts are free. The daily amount per envelope is part of Pro.
 What happens to my moves next month? Nothing carries: the moves belong to the period you made them in, and the next period starts from your usual budgets. Past periods keep showing their moves.
 Sources: TrackExpenses BudgetMoves, MoveBudgetSheet, BudgetStatsView and FreeTier, checked in November 2026. Amounts are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login. ## Zero-Based Budget: Give Every Unit of Pay a Job
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/zero-based-budget.html
 Zero-based budget: give every unit of pay a job  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    The method in four steps    Do the arithmetic on iPhone    Zero-based and 50/30/20    Plan it in TrackExpenses with the salary plan    Months that aren't like the others    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 A zero-based budget plans your whole take-home pay before the month starts, so income minus everything planned, bills, spending and savings, comes to exactly zero. Zero doesn't mean an empty account; it means no part of your pay is left without a job.
 The method in four steps
 Work with one pay period and the money that actually reaches you after tax and deductions.

  Start with take-home pay.  Say 12,000 a month.
  Plan the fixed bills.  Rent 4,300, utilities 450, phone 150 and insurance 300: 5,200.
  Plan savings as a line, not a leftover.  1,500 to a savings account, decided now rather than hoped for at the end of the month.
  Plan everyday spending by category.  Groceries 1,800, transport 700, eating out 900 and personal 600: 4,000.

 Planned so far: 5,200 + 1,500 + 4,000 = 10,700, which leaves 1,300 without a job. Give it one: 800 for irregular costs, such as a car service or a gift, and 500 more to savings. Now 12,000 − 12,000 = 0, and the budget is zero-based.
 If the plan comes out below zero, you have planned money you don't have: lower a category before the month starts, not after the account runs dry.
 Do the arithmetic on iPhone
 Calculator on iPhone handles one month: 12,000 − 5,200 − 1,500 − 4,000 = 1,300 tells you how much still needs a job.
 For a plan you reuse, Numbers is better. Put each planned amount in its own row and add a cell for income minus the SUM of the planned column. When that cell reads 0, every unit has a job. Apple's  Numbers formula guide  shows how to build it on the phone.
 Zero-based and 50/30/20
 The 50/30/20 rule splits take-home pay by share: half for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for savings. Zero-based budgeting is stricter about the detail: every unit has a named line, whatever the shares turn out to be. They work well together. Use the  50/30/20 calculator  to set rough targets, then fill in the lines until nothing is left to plan. The  50/30/20 guide  has a worked example.
 Plan it in TrackExpenses with the salary plan
 The salary plan, part of Pro, is a zero-based budget on one screen. Open Stats → Budget and tap Salary plan at the top, or open it from More → Budgets.

  Add your income.  Tap Add your income and enter the Monthly income you expect: salary and any other regular income.
  Spending.  Each category's line is that category's budget, and Everything else is the part of your budget total no category holds, so nothing you spend falls outside the plan.
  Saving & investing.  Each Savings or Investment account gets a line for what you plan to put into it. Add such an account in Accounts first.

 Above the lines, Planned and Left to plan add it up, and a sentence under the income answers the question the plan exists for. "Your income covers your plan exactly." is a zero-based budget. "Your income covers your plan, with 1,300.00 still to plan." means some money has no job yet; "Your income is 200.00 short of your plan." means you have planned more than you earn.
 Editors open empty, with the current amount shown as a hint, and suggest figures you can take in one tap: your repeating bills, or what you spent or saved last period. Before you save, each one says what else moves, such as "Everything else becomes 1,900.00". You can type sums too: 1200 + 350 in an amount is saved as 1,550.
 Switch from Plan to Actual during the month to see what was Received, Spent and Saved, and how much of what arrived is left after spending and saving. The plan is the budget, not a second one: the category lines are the same budgets the pacing bars, budget alerts and daily budget use. To keep to the plan during the month, the  envelope budgeting guide  shows how to move money between categories.
 Months that aren't like the others
  Extra income.  A bonus or a side payment belongs to one month only. Tap Add extra income and enter it; your usual income stays as it is, and next month starts without it. While the extra is unplanned, every line's editor offers Extra income not yet planned, so giving the bonus a job is one tap, and changes made in that month apply to that month alone.
  Logged income.  Income you record never changes the plan by itself, because it may be next month's salary paid early. When more arrives than you planned, the plan says how much and leaves the decision to you.
  A different month ahead.  A change carries to the months after it unless a month has its own amount, and months already lived keep what they had. A note on a month, such as "Eid expenses" or "Holiday gifts", explains why December looks different.
 The  budget planner page  shows the screens.
 What it doesn't do
 The salary plan is part of Pro, including Lifetime. Budgets themselves, category budgets, the bars and moving money between budgets are free, so you can run a zero-based plan by hand with a free budget: set the total to your take-home pay and give it out across categories, leaving Everything else for what is left.
 Savings lines exist only for Savings or Investment accounts, and the free ledger holds three accounts. A line is a plan; the app doesn't move money for you. Record the transfer to savings, and Actual shows what reached the account.
 The plan doesn't group lines into needs and wants. Its period is your budget month with a fixed start day, so pay every two weeks needs a monthly convention you keep.
 Frequently asked questions
 Does a zero-based budget mean spending everything I earn? No. Savings and irregular costs are lines like any other. Zero means every part of your pay is assigned, not that it is spent.
 What if my income changes from month to month? Plan on the lowest income you can count on. When a better month comes, add the difference as extra income for that month and give it a job then.
 Is the salary plan free? It is part of Pro, including Lifetime. Budgets, category budgets and moves between them are free.
 How is zero-based different from envelope budgeting? Zero-based decides where every unit of pay goes before the month; envelopes are how you keep to it during the month, moving money between categories when one runs short. The envelope budgeting guide covers that part.
 Sources: TrackExpenses SalaryPlan, PlanMonths, SalaryPlanScreen and FreeTier, checked in November 2026; Apple's Numbers formula guide linked above. Figures are examples, not financial advice. ## See How Much You Spent at One Shop | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/spending-at-one-shop.html
 See how much you spent at one shop or on one thing  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Search your card history on iPhone    Search everything in TrackExpenses    Look at one thing instead of one shop    Keep shop names consistent    A worked example    What it doesn't do    Frequently asked questions
 To see how much you spent at one shop, search your records for its name and add up what comes back: Wallet and most banking apps can search a card's history, and TrackExpenses search adds up Spent and Income across every match in every period, free. For one kind of thing, such as coffee or fuel, a category does the same job.
 Search your card history on iPhone
 Wallet can search the activity on supported cards. Open Wallet, tap the search button and type the shop's name; Apple says you can also search by date, amount or location. It is quick for one card, but only for purchases that card's bank shares with Wallet, and never for cash or another card.
 Your bank's app usually has a search box over its transactions too, and a statement downloaded as a spreadsheet can be totalled in Numbers with a SUMIF on the description column. Both stop at that one bank.
 All of these meet the same snag: one shop appears under several names. The same supermarket can show up as CARREFOUR MOE, Carrefour City Centre and a payment terminal's code, so an exact search misses part of what you spent there.
 Search everything in TrackExpenses
 In TrackExpenses, open the Transactions tab and tap the magnifying glass. The search field asks for a payee, note, category or amount, and it looks through every period, not only the month you are viewing.
 Type part of a shop's name, such as "carrefour". Search ignores capitals and accents, so it finds "Carrefour City Centre" and "CARREFOUR MOE" alike, along with any entry whose note or category contains the word. A line such as "23 matches across all periods" sits above the results, and under it two totals: Spent and Income.
 The totals count every match in your ledger, not only the rows on screen. The list stops at a few hundred rows to stay quick, and when it does, a note says "Not every match is listed here. The totals count all of them."
 Amounts are in your main currency, at the rate each entry was saved with, so purchases abroad add up correctly. Transfers between your own accounts appear in the list but in neither total, because moving money is not spending. Search and its totals are free.
 You can also type an exact amount, such as 45.50, to find every entry of that amount: useful when a bank statement shows a figure you can't place.
 Look at one thing instead of one shop
 For a kind of spending rather than a shop, use its category. Typing a category name in search, such as "Fuel", lists every fuel entry from every period with its total.
 To see one period, open Stats → Overview and tap the category. You get this period's total and entries, and a bar chart of its totals over the last six months. On the Transactions tab, the Description view groups the period by description instead, each with its total and the number of entries, biggest first; tap a name to see its entries.
 Two quicker ways to ask about a category this period:

  Siri.  Say "How much did I spend on Groceries in TrackExpenses", with your own category name, and Siri answers with the spending against that category's budget.
  The money coach.  Type "How much is left for groceries?" and the coach answers on your phone, without using one of your AI questions. A question about a shop rather than a category goes to the AI model, after you agree, and uses one of your AI questions (ten a month are free). The model sees at most 20 matching purchases, so for a full total, search is the better tool.

 Keep shop names consistent
 Search can only add up what it can find, so a few habits make totals exact.
 When you type a description, Previous descriptions suggests the names you have used, and picking one keeps the spelling the same. A shop you have used before also fills in its usual category and account, and the entry says "Category and account from your past Carrefour entries", so you can see where they came from.
 Entries imported from bank alerts carry the merchant name as your bank prints it. Search for the part every version shares, such as "carrefour" rather than "Carrefour Mall of the Emirates".
 For spending that isn't a shop, such as work lunches or a home repair, put a word in the note. Search reads notes too, so "repair" later finds every entry about it.
 A worked example
 Suppose your coffee entries sit under Food, described as "Starbucks" and "Costa". Search "starbucks": 31 matches, Spent 589.00. Search "costa": 12 matches, Spent 198.00. That is 787.00 on coffee across the whole ledger, about the price of a week's groceries.
 Searching "coffee" would miss both, because the word is in neither description. If you want coffee as one figure every month, give it its own category, so Stats shows it without a search. To see what a daily habit like this costs over a year and five years, try the  habit cost calculator .
 What it doesn't do
 Search totals cover your whole ledger; search has no date range. For one month, use the Description view or the category in Stats. Totals only include what you recorded: cash you didn't enter and purchases under a name you didn't search for are not in them.
 The coach answers category questions on the phone, but not shop questions, which use an AI question. The  reports feature page  shows the views mentioned here.
 Frequently asked questions
 Can Wallet show how much I spent at one store? Wallet can search a supported card's activity by merchant. It covers only that card and the purchases its bank shares, and never cash.
 Does TrackExpenses search add up what it finds? Yes. Under the results it shows Spent and Income for every match in every period, in your main currency. It is free.
 How do I see what I spent at a shop in one month only? Open the Transactions tab for that month and switch to the Description view, which totals each description in the period.
 Why doesn't search find a purchase I know I made? It may be spelled differently or sit under another name. Search for a shorter part of the name, the category, or the exact amount.
 Sources: Apple's  Wallet guide ; TrackExpenses SearchSummary, SearchScreen, DescriptionListView, CategoryDetailSheet, PayeeRecallCopy and CoachCommand, checked in November 2026. ## December Money Reset: A Spending Challenge | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/december-money-reset.html
 December Money Reset: A Spending Challenge You Can Keep  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    Why one limit beats a no-spend month    The method, with a notebook or a spreadsheet    Doing it with the money coach in TrackExpenses    A worked example    When the challenge won't start, and other limits    Frequently asked questions
 A December money reset that lasts is one limit on one habit, not a ban on spending: find the everyday category that took the most of last month's money, set a limit about a fifth below it, and check where you stand once a week. TrackExpenses does the reading, suggests the limit and sends the weekly check-ins, but the method works on paper too.
 Why one limit beats a no-spend month
 December is the month of gifts, dinners and year-end sales, so "spend nothing" breaks in the first week. One limit on one category survives, because the rest of your month carries on and you watch one figure.
 Pick the category by last month's facts, not by guilt. Coffee feels like the problem, but groceries, delivery or eating out usually move the month more.
 Leave fixed bills out: rent and subscriptions are big, but cutting them is a decision you make once, not a habit.
 The method, with a notebook or a spreadsheet
 1.  Read last month.  Add up everything you spent in November, without rent and other repeating bills. Then add up each everyday category: food, groceries, transport, shopping. 2.  Find the one that stands out.  Look for a category with at least three purchases that took a real share of that everyday total, say 15% or more. One big purchase is a one-off, not a habit. 3.  Set the limit.  Take 80% of what that category cost in November and round it down to a figure you will remember. 960 becomes 750, not 768. 4.  Check in once a week.  Every Sunday, add up the category so far and compare it with where it should be: by the end of week two, about half the limit. Ahead of the pace means slow down. Over the limit means every day under from here still counts. 5.  Close the month.  On 1 January, write down what the category cost in December next to November's figure. That difference is what the reset saved.
 A payday month works the same way. If your money month runs from the 25th, read the last full payday month and set the limit for the one running now.
 Doing it with the money coach in TrackExpenses
 Open the  Coach  tab, the one in the middle of the tab bar. Once a full month is logged, the coach opens with a reading of it: "Hi. I looked at your November.", the category that stood out ("Groceries was 31% of your everyday spending.") and a suggestion: "Try a limit of 750 for December. I'll check in every week." It skips repeating bills and one-off big purchases on its own, and a category needs at least three purchases and 15% of your everyday spending before the coach names it. If nothing stands out, it says so rather than inventing a target.
 The suggestion is 80% of what the category took, rounded down to a round figure, with one step either side to pick from (700, 750 or 800 in the example below). The challenge card reads "December challenge: Groceries under 750". Tap  Join .
 Joining sets that category's budget for that month only, so the limit appears in Stats → Budget with its pacing bar and today notch like any other budget. The coach then checks in once a week with a notification titled "Your Groceries challenge" ("410 of 750 so far. Tap for this week's check-in."), and the check-in in the Coach tab says whether you are on pace, a little ahead of it or over. When the month ends, it tells you how it went: "You kept Groceries under 750 in December: 702." and how that compares with November.
 Changed your mind?  Stop this challenge  puts the category's budget for that month back to what it was. Nothing you logged changes.
 Reading the month and the suggestion are free. Joining a challenge and the weekly check-ins come with Pro. The  AI money coach page  covers the rest of the coach, including the questions you can type to it.
 A worked example
 Say your November everyday spending, without rent and subscriptions, was 3,000. Groceries took 960 of it over 14 trips to the shop, which is 32%. Nothing else came close.

 80% of 960 is 768, and the round figure below it is 750.
 By Sunday 14 December you have spent 410. Two weeks in, the pace says about 340, so you are ahead by about 70. You plan two shops from the freezer that week.
 By the 21st you are at 540, back on pace.
 December ends at 702. That is 258 less than November.

 The  daily spending limit guide  shows the same arithmetic for your whole budget, if you want a daily figure as well.
 When the challenge won't start, and other limits
  Start early in the month.  The coach offers a challenge for the month you are in only while less than a quarter of it has passed, so by about 7 December for a calendar month. After that it offers the challenge for January, so you don't start a target you can't meet.
  It needs a whole month logged.  With less than a full month in the ledger, the coach says "I'll have something to say once a full month is logged." Log purchases as they happen, by voice or from your bank's messages, and it reads that month as soon as it ends.
  Gifts are not everyday spending.  If December gifts would swamp the month, give them a category and a budget line of their own under More → Budgets, so they have a figure of their own and don't hide the habit the reset is about.
  Weekly check-ins need weeks.  A budget kept by the week gets one report at its end instead. With notifications off, check-ins wait in the Coach tab.
  One challenge a month.  The coach runs one challenge per budget month. If more than one habit needs work, take the biggest in December and the next in January.  Budget alerts  can watch the other categories meanwhile.
 Frequently asked questions
 Is a December money reset the same as a no-spend challenge? No. A no-spend challenge stops all optional spending for a set time. A money reset keeps your month as it is and puts one limit on the habit that cost the most last month, which is easier to keep through the holidays.
 How much lower should the limit be? About a fifth lower than last month. 80% is a real change you will notice, without being so low that one family dinner breaks it.
 Can I change the limit TrackExpenses suggests? Yes. The coach offers one step below and one above its suggestion, and after joining you can still change that category's budget like any other.
 Does the coach send my spending anywhere? No. The reading, the suggested limit and the weekly check-ins are worked out on your iPhone from your own ledger. Only questions you type that need the coach's AI are sent, and the app asks your permission first.
 Source: TrackExpenses app code (the money coach's rules: last finished budget month, repeating bills and one-off purchases left out, at least three purchases and 15% of everyday spending, a limit at 80% rounded down, a challenge for the current month in its first quarter, weekly check-ins for periods of two to eight weeks, joining with Pro), checked November 2026. Figures are examples, not financial advice.    TRACKEXPENSES FOR IPHONE, IPAD & MAC   Say it, import bank SMS, budget from payday.  Free to start, no bank login. ## Double Tap Your iPhone Back to Log Expenses | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/guides/double-tap-log-expenses-iphone.html
 Log an Expense by Double Tapping the Back of Your iPhone  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction    In this guide    What you need    Step 1: Add the Log Expense shortcut    Step 2: Turn on Back Tap    Step 3: Try it    A worked example    Limits and common mistakes    Other ways to log without typing    Frequently asked questions
 You can log a purchase without opening any app: tap the back of your iPhone twice, type the price, pick the category, and it is saved. It runs on iOS's own Back Tap setting and one shortcut from TrackExpenses, and takes about a minute to set up once.

 What you need

 An iPhone 8 or later on iOS 14 or later. Back Tap is an iPhone setting; iPad has no such option.
 TrackExpenses installed and opened once, so its "Log an Expense" action exists in Shortcuts.
 The ready-made "Log Expense" shortcut (step 1 below). Back Tap can only run shortcuts that are in your own Shortcuts library, which is why the app hands you one rather than adding itself to Back Tap.

 Nothing here connects to your bank, and the shortcut sends nothing anywhere: it asks three questions and saves the answer in your ledger on the iPhone.
 Step 1: Add the Log Expense shortcut
 Open this link on your iPhone:  Get the Log Expense shortcut . Shortcuts opens and shows "Log Expense" with one action, Log an Expense in TrackExpenses. Tap Add Shortcut. It now sits in the Shortcuts app's library under that name; keep the name as it is, because Back Tap lists shortcuts by name.
 The action asks three things each time it runs: the amount, the category, and a description you can leave empty. You can open the shortcut to look at it, but you don't need to change anything.
 Step 2: Turn on Back Tap
 Open the Settings app and follow this path: Settings › Accessibility › Touch › Back Tap › Double Tap, then scroll to the Shortcuts section and choose Log Expense. A check appears next to it.

 Touch is in the Physical and Motor group of Accessibility, and Back Tap is near the bottom of the Touch screen. Apple offers apps no link that opens this screen directly, so it takes these few taps once. If you would rather keep Double Tap for something else, choose Triple Tap instead and pick Log Expense there.
 Step 3: Try it
 Double tap the back of the iPhone, near the camera, with a fingertip. The first time, iOS asks whether "Log Expense" may run actions from TrackExpenses: tap Allow. Then type a price on the number pad, tap Done, pick a category, add a description such as the shop's name or leave it empty, and tap Done again. Shortcuts confirms what was logged, and the entry is in your ledger the next time you look, with today's date and your default account.
 A worked example
 You are paying for groceries at the till with your phone in your hand. Before you put it away, you tap its back twice. The number pad appears over whatever app was open: you type 23 and tap Done, choose Groceries, type Carrefour and tap Done. That is the whole entry. Back in TrackExpenses that evening, Carrefour · Groceries · 23 is in today's list, it counts against your Groceries budget, and your daily budget for tomorrow already accounts for it.
 Limits and common mistakes
 Back Tap needs a firm, quick double tap on the back of the phone. A thick case can make it miss; tap a little harder or nearer the camera. It may also fire by accident when you put the phone down on a hard surface; if that happens, cancel the number pad.
 The shortcut logs expenses only. Income, transfers between your own accounts, a foreign currency or a split purchase need the app, where the entry sheet has every field.
 The entry uses your default account. If you pay from several cards, change the account in the app afterwards, or use voice entry in the app ("lunch 30 with the credit card") when the account matters.
 If nothing happens when you double tap, check three things: the shortcut is still called Log Expense in the Shortcuts app, Settings › Accessibility › Touch › Back Tap › Double Tap shows a check next to it, and you tapped Allow the first time. If you renamed or deleted the shortcut, add it again from the link above and choose it again in Back Tap.
 Other ways to log without typing
 Double tap is the fastest way to log something you just paid for in cash or on a card that sends no alert. For card purchases, the automatic routes need no tap at all:  bank SMS alerts  and  bank alerts by email  can log themselves through a Shortcuts automation, and  Apple Pay purchases  can too, through the Wallet Transaction trigger. For several purchases at once,  voice entry  takes a whole list in one sentence.  Siri and widgets  cover the rest.
 Frequently asked questions
 Is Double Tap to Log free? Yes. Back Tap is part of iOS, the shortcut is free, and expenses logged through it count like any other entry in the free ledger.
 Does it work when the iPhone is locked? Back Tap works with the screen on. On a locked iPhone, iOS may ask you to unlock it before the shortcut runs, depending on your settings. The confirmation never shows a balance.
 Can I use Triple Tap instead? Yes. Choose Triple Tap in step 2 and pick Log Expense there. Both can be set to different shortcuts.
 Why do I need a shortcut at all? Back Tap only offers the shortcuts in your own library, not the actions apps provide. The Log Expense shortcut is one TrackExpenses action, Log an Expense, with its three questions set to be asked each time.
 Read next: the  Siri, widgets and Shortcuts guide  and the  widgets and shortcuts feature page .
 Source: Apple's iPhone User Guide (Back Tap, under Accessibility › Touch), the TrackExpenses app code (the Log an Expense action and the shared Log Expense shortcut, November 2026). ## Voice Expense Tracker for iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/voice-expense-tracker.html
 FEATURE · SAY IT · 10 FREE A MONTH
 Log expenses by voice. Several at once.
 Say it turns a sentence like “coffee 15, taxi 40 and groceries 120 at the supermarket yesterday” into three separate drafts — amount, category, payee and date filled in — that you check and save with one tap. It works in English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese, and speech is processed on your iPhone or iPad.

         Real app screens with example records.
 How it works
   Tap Say.  From the Transactions screen, the app icon (touch and hold it, then Say an expense), the Quick Add widget, the Lock Screen or Control Center (iOS 18 and later).   Talk normally.  As you speak, chips show what was understood — amount, category, date, payee — so a missing number is obvious while it still costs nothing to repeat it.   Pause.  Recording stops on its own after a short pause; a ring shows the pause closing. No need to tap Done.   Review and save.  Each purchase becomes a card you can edit. Save them all, or use “Save & say another” to log the next receipt in the same sitting.
 Pick the language you speak
 The language line on the listening screen is a menu. It starts on the app’s language, and you can switch to another of the five the app reads, or to another language your iPhone can hear. So you can speak German to an app set to English. The choice is kept on the device.
 What it understands
   Lists, with or without pauses:  “coffee 15, taxi 40 and lunch 60” becomes three entries, even when the words arrive without commas; “spent 45 on groceries and fuel” stays one.   Prices the way you say them:  “two pounds eighty”, “45 dollars and 50 cents”, “5 thousand rent”, “two and a half thousand”, and in Spanish “45 con 50”.   “Twelve fifty” fixed in one tap:  when a price said short is heard as 1250, the draft offers 12.50 beside it. If that category has never cost anything near 1250, it opens on 12.50, says why, and one tap takes it back.   Shops you know:  “Starbucks 22” fills the shop and its category for well-known brands.   Dates:  today, yesterday, “3 days ago”, “on the 25th”, “rent on November 1st”.   Accounts:  “with the credit card”, “cash” — and “moved 500 from cash to main bank” becomes a transfer.   Quantities:  “3 coffees at 15 each”, “hotel 1200 for 2 nights”.   Income:  “salary 12,500” is recorded as money coming in.   Notes:  “… note for the office party” keeps the note separate from the shop name.   Your habits:  if you always file Carrefour under Groceries on your card, a new Carrefour entry suggests the same — marked as remembered, not heard.
 Languages and devices
 Say it uses Apple’s on-device speech recognition for the language you pick, where your device has it. The app’s own rules then read the sentence in English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese, numbers and all. On devices with Apple Intelligence, Apple’s on-device model can suggest a category for a purchase the rules couldn’t file, and the card says the category is a suggestion to check. Audio is never uploaded by the app, and every result is a draft you confirm.
 A price in another currency gets a currency and a rate row on its card, prefilled from the last rate you used, so it converts into your main currency. More in the  voice entry guide .
 Free or Pro
 Free includes 10 saved voice entries per calendar month on each device; each purchase you save counts as one, so a sentence with three purchases uses three. Pro makes Say it unlimited. Typing, templates and pasting a bank message stay free and unlimited.
  Questions   Is the voice processed in the cloud?  No. TrackExpenses requires on-device speech recognition and does not upload your audio. Results are drafts you review before anything is saved.    Can I say several expenses in one sentence?  Yes. Separate them naturally with commas or “and”, or just keep talking. Each purchase becomes its own draft, and a date or account said once can apply to the whole list.    Which languages does Say it understand?  The app reads English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese. Pick the language on the listening screen; it starts on the app’s language. Speech recognition depends on the languages Apple supports on your device.    What if it hears twelve fifty as 1250?  The draft offers the other reading, such as 12.50, with one tap. If that category has never cost anything near 1250, the draft opens on 12.50, says why, and one tap takes it back.    Does it work in Arabic?  Yes. Arabic sentences are read by the built-in rules, including Arabic number words, category words, accounts and day words such as yesterday. The app itself is in English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese, with a right-to-left Arabic layout.    What happens if a price is in another currency?  The draft shows the currency and a rate field prefilled from the last rate you used, so the entry converts correctly into your main currency.

## Bank SMS Expense Tracker for iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/sms-expense-tracker.html
 FEATURE · BANK SMS & EMAIL · 10 FREE A MONTH
 Your bank texts you. Your ledger fills itself.
 TrackExpenses turns bank SMS and email alerts into expenses and income using an iPhone Shortcuts automation, and reads any alert you paste. It picks out the amount, merchant, card, currency and date, skips one-time codes, declined payments and offers, and never needs your bank login or access to your inbox.

         Real app screens with example records.
 How it works
   Create a Message automation once.  Choose wording from your bank’s actual alerts, then connect Shortcuts’ Message trigger to Import Bank Message. The  complete iOS 27 and iOS 26 setup guide  shows the right input variable for each version. More → SMS Auto-Import walks you through it with the real screens, step by step.   Spend as usual.  When the alert arrives, the action passes that one message to TrackExpenses. The app reads it, files it and keeps only what it read — never the message text.   Glance at what needs a look.  Anything uncertain is flagged on the Daily screen: a possible duplicate, a card it hasn’t linked yet, a foreign purchase waiting for a rate, money coming in.
 Bank alerts by email
 If your bank emails instead of texting, the same action can read those emails. Add the email account, such as Gmail, to Apple’s Mail app, because the Shortcuts Email trigger watches Mail and can’t see the Gmail app. Then create an Email automation filtered on a word that every alert subject contains, such as “transaction”, and hand the email to Import Bank Message. Filter on the subject, never the sender. Mail checks for new email on a schedule, so an alert can take a few minutes to arrive.
 The app shows the steps for your iOS version under More → SMS Auto-Import → “Bank alerts by email?”, and the  bank email alerts guide  has every screen.
 Or paste an alert
 Many banks, especially in Latin America and Europe, notify through their own app rather than by SMS, and no iPhone automation can read another app’s notification. iOS doesn’t let you copy a notification’s text either, but an SMS, an email, or a transaction detail your bank’s app lets you copy can be pasted: tap  Paste  on the Transactions screen or choose Paste bank message from the app icon: the amount, shop and date are filled in, ready to check. Pasting is free, unlimited and doesn’t use the automatic allowance.
 What it reads, and what it refuses
  Amount and currency — more than 110 currencies recognized, digits in Arabic, Persian, Devanagari and more.  Merchant, the date printed in the message, and the card’s last digits: an alert that names a card lands on the account linked to it, pasted or imported.  The category you used before for that shop, so a corrected Carrefour entry teaches every later one.  Formats from banks and wallets in the Gulf, India and the rest of Asia, Africa, Europe, the US and Latin America, from Pix in Brazil to card purchases in Mexico and Colombia, in English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese and many other languages.  ATM withdrawals, cash deposits and card bill payments can become transfers between your accounts instead of fake spending.  A purchase abroad that your bank also states in your own currency imports at the amount you were charged.  One-time codes, declined payments, fraud checks, payment requests, bills merely due and promotions are refused, not imported.  Salary credits can be imported as income and flagged for review (a switch you control).
 Want to check your bank first?
 The setup screen has a “try one of your bank's messages” box: paste an alert and see exactly what would be imported, before the next real purchase. Setup also suggests a filter word your bank’s alerts really contain, such as the currency code, or “$” for a ledger in dollars.
 Free or Pro
 Free includes 10 successful automatic imports per calendar month on each device, SMS and email together. After that, new alerts are still caught and kept — amount, merchant and date — but appear locked, outside your totals; tapping one offers Pro. Upgrading adds them all to your ledger automatically and removes the limit. Otherwise, next calendar month’s allowance releases as many as it covers. Nothing is dropped, and entries already saved are never locked.
  Questions   Does TrackExpenses read my Messages inbox?  No. iOS does not allow that. A Shortcuts automation that you create passes matching messages to the app one at a time.    Will it work with my bank?  It reads many real alert formats from banks across the Gulf, India, Asia, Africa, Europe, the US and Latin America, but not every format. Paste one of your alerts into the setup screen check to see the result before relying on it.    Can it read bank alerts that arrive by email?  Yes. Add the email account to Apple’s Mail app, then create a Shortcuts Email automation filtered on a word from the alert subject, with the Import Bank Message action. The app shows the steps under More, SMS Auto-Import, Bank alerts by email.    My bank only sends app notifications. What can I do?  No iPhone automation can read another app’s notification. If you can copy the alert text, paste it into TrackExpenses: the amount, shop and date fill in, and pasting is free. Many banks can also send SMS or email alerts, which an automation can log.    Why can Shortcuts show a notification?  Shortcuts may show a system notification depending on your iOS version and automation settings. Show When Run controls the import action’s own presentation. On iOS 27, check Automation is on, Confirm Before Run is off, and Allow Running When Locked is enabled.    What happens after 10 free imports?  Later alerts are kept but locked outside your totals. Upgrading to Pro adds them all automatically; otherwise the next calendar month’s allowance releases as many as it covers. Nothing is dropped, and saved history is never locked.

## AI Money Coach for Your iPhone Budget | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/ai-money-coach.html
 FEATURE · MONEY COACH · FREE + PRO
 A money coach that reads your month.
 Coach, the middle tab, is a clay wallet that looks back at your last budget month, names where most of your everyday money went and suggests one limit to try. Ask it anything in your own words, in English, Arabic, German, Spanish or Portuguese. Whatever your ledger can answer exactly is worked out on your iPhone, free and instant; an open question such as “What can I improve?” goes to an AI model, Anthropic's Claude, and only after you agree.

      A real app screen with example records.
 Each month, one suggestion
   It reads your last month.  When a budget month ends, the coach names your biggest everyday category. Repeating bills such as rent are left out, because a bill isn't a habit.   It suggests one limit.  A round figure below what that category took, for this month if it has only just begun, otherwise for the next. Before you join, it says what else in your budget moves.   Join it as a challenge (Pro).  The limit becomes that category's budget for the month, and the coach checks in every week with a notification saying how you stand. Leave the challenge and the budget goes back to what it was.   See how it went.  When the month closes, the coach tells you whether you stayed under.
 Ask in your own words
 Type a question or tap a suggestion. A small pill beside the field says what Send will do before you press it:  Log  and  Show  are worked out on your phone,  Ask  goes to the AI. Cards made on the phone are marked “On your phone”; AI answers are marked “AI · check the figures”.
 Answered on your phone, free and instant
   Today and yesterday:  “What did I spend today?” gives the day’s total with its biggest purchase, repeating bills named beside it, and what is left of today’s budget where you have one.   One category:  “How much is left for groceries?” or just “groceries this month”, using your own category names.   Your balances:  “What’s my balance?” gives your net worth and a line for each account.   How you're doing:  “Am I on pace this month?”, “Where does my money go?” and “Better than last month?”, tapped or typed your own way, answered from your ledger with a chart where one helps.   Any month, any year:  “How was September 2023?” gives what that month came to, how it compares with the month before, where the money went with a category chart, and what changed most. It reaches as far back as your ledger does.   A weekly report:  “show my week” draws your last seven days, with your top category and your biggest day.   Files:  “export last 7 days” makes a CSV file to share or save. Files come with Pro, like every export.   Logging:  type “coffee 15, taxi 40” and the coach shows one draft per purchase with its category; save them with one tap. Logging is free and never counts as a question.
 None of these is sent anywhere, and none uses one of your AI questions; neither does a “thanks” or a “hello”. While Send would show a chart or make a file, the line under the field says so: “Worked out on your phone, never sent anywhere.”
 Open questions, answered by AI
 Ask what the rules can't answer: “What can I improve?”, “My spending habits”, or “Why was last month so expensive?”. These go to Anthropic's Claude, which reads a summary of your month and can ask the app for earlier totals or a few purchases; the answer streams back as it is written, and the send button turns into  Stop  if you want to end it early. If a question turns out to be purchases, the answer comes back as drafts to save. Ten AI questions a month are free on each device; Pro gets many more.
 What leaves your phone
 Nothing goes to the AI until you agree on the screen titled “Typed questions leave your device”. After that, a question the phone can't answer travels with the earlier questions and answers in the same conversation and a summary of this month and last month (totals, categories and their budgets, your biggest shops, your salary plan lines and your challenge) to a small relay the developer runs on Cloudflare, which passes it to Anthropic's Claude and streams the answer back. If the model asks for more, the app answers from your ledger: totals by category, shop, day or month for up to the last 13 months, or up to 20 purchases with their date, shop name, category and amount.
 It never sends your notes, receipts, account names or numbers, balances or your whole transaction history. The relay keeps nothing you wrote or asked and logs no content; Anthropic does not use the data to train its models and deletes it within 30 days under its own terms. To keep free questions fair, the relay counts questions per install, per subscription and, for a day, per network address, without their content. Switch typed questions off at any time in More → Privacy & data; the coach still answers everything it works out on your phone. The  privacy policy  has the full wording.
 Five languages
 The coach works in English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese: the monthly reading, the tapped questions, typed purchases, and questions about a day, a category or a month, typed with or without accents, such as “ كم صرفت في أيلول 2023 ” or “ ¿cuánto gasté hoy? ”. AI answers come back in the app’s language, with amounts written the way the app writes them.
 Free or Pro
 Free: the monthly reading and its suggestion, every answer worked out on your phone, charts and the weekly report, logging typed purchases, and 10 AI questions a month on each device. Pro: joining a challenge with weekly check-ins, many more AI questions, and files for today, yesterday, the last 7 days, this budget month or last month. The coach works from the records you keep; it is not financial advice.
  Questions   Is the money coach free?  The monthly reading, every answer worked out on your phone, charts and logging typed purchases are free. Ten typed questions a month answered by the AI are free on each device. Pro adds challenges with weekly check-ins, many more AI questions and CSV files.    Which questions does the coach answer without AI?  What you spent today or yesterday, what is left in a category, your balances, how a named month went, whether you are on pace, where your money goes and how you compare with last month, plus charts, files and typed purchases. These are worked out on your phone and never use a question.    Which AI answers, and what does it see?  Anthropic's Claude, through a relay the developer runs, and only after you agree. It gets your question, the conversation so far and a summary of this month and last month: totals, categories and their budgets, your biggest shops, your salary plan lines and your challenge. If it needs more, the app can send totals for up to the last 13 months or up to 20 purchases with their date, shop, category and amount. It never gets your notes, receipts, account names or numbers, balances or your whole transaction history.    Does logging a purchase in the coach use up a question?  No. “coffee 15, taxi 40” is read on your phone and shown as drafts you save with a tap. Logging is free and never counts as a question.    Which languages does the coach speak?  English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese. The reading, the tapped questions, typed purchases and month names work in all five, and AI answers come back in the app’s language.
