## Budget Planner: Move Money & Daily Amounts | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/budget-planner.html
 FEATURE · BUDGETS · FREE + PRO
 A budget that starts on payday and knows what day it is.
 Move money between category budgets, cover an overspend and see what is left to spend each day. Your total budget stays the same, your month can start on payday, and Pro adds a daily amount for each budget alongside your salary plan and forecasts.

               Real app screens with example records.
 Your month, not the calendar's
 Paid on the 25th? Set More → Period & Entry to start on the 25th and every list, chart, budget and total runs from 25th to 24th. Days past the end of a short month are clamped, so “31” simply means the last day.
 Pacing, not just totals
 Sixty percent spent means nothing until you know where the month is. Every budget bar pairs the amount spent with a notch for today, so you can see at a glance whether you are ahead of or behind the month. Set a total budget and per-category budgets under More → Budgets. You keep one budget, in the period length you use; a week or a year is worked out from it by day, and the app says so. Turn on  budget alerts  to hear when a budget passes 80% ahead of its pace or goes over.
 Move money where this month needs it
 Need more for transport and less for groceries? Open  Stats → Budget , tap  •••  on a budget, then choose  Move money in  or  Move money out . Pick the other budget and the amount, check both before-and-after figures, and confirm. Money moves between budget amounts inside your ledger; no money is transferred between bank accounts.
 Moves apply to the  current budget period only  and keep your total unchanged. Next period starts from your usual budget amounts. To change those ongoing amounts, use Budget Setting or the salary plan. Move controls appear in the budget’s own period length, in the period containing today.
   Example: move 100 from Groceries to Transport, in your main currency    Budget  Before  After      Groceries  1,500  1,400    Transport  500  600    Total budget  2,000  2,000
 Cover an overspend without rebuilding your budget
 An over-budget row offers  Cover , taking you straight to a move from a budget with money to spare. Cover suggestions leave enough for repeating bills still due. If you manually choose an amount that would use money reserved for those bills, the move sheet warns you before you confirm.
 Moving money and covering an overspend are  free . Each row shows what moved in or out, and a budget stays visible even if you move all of its available amount away.
 A daily amount for each budget, with Pro
 Each budget shows a daily spending amount for the days left in your period. Its own repeating bills come out first, then earlier spending is accounted for and the available amount is shared across the remaining days. The allowance is worked out before today’s spending, so today’s purchases count against it instead of constantly changing the target.
 A category made up entirely of repeating bills does not show a daily amount. There is no extra daily target to enter: each figure comes from that budget’s amount, your records and the days left. Per-budget daily guidance is included with  Pro, including Lifetime .
 Spent, left and days to go
 Days left appear once in the Budget header. Every budget labels what you spent and what is left, while  Everything else  shows spending in categories without their own budget, using the part of the total not assigned to categories. Your total and category amounts remain part of one budget.
 Plan your salary before it arrives
 The salary plan (Pro, in Stats → Budget) answers one question before payday: will your income cover everything you plan? Enter your monthly income, give each category its amount, and plan what goes into each savings or investment account. The plan answers in one sentence — your income covers it with this much still to plan, or falls short by this much — and shows each line’s share of your income. The  50/30/20 budget guide  and the  zero-based budget guide  use it for worked examples, and the  monthly budget calculator  does the same arithmetic in your browser. Suggestions come from your repeating bills and last month, one tap each, never filled in for you.  Each month can keep its own amounts, and a change carries to the months after unless a later month set its own. Add a bonus or side income to one month only, give a line a short note such as “Eid expenses”, and type sums like 1200 + 350 straight into any planned amount, budget or move.
 Switch to  Actual  to see what you really spent and saved against every line, and how much of what you received is left. The plan is your budget, not a second one: a category’s planned amount is its budget, so your daily budget and budget bars always agree with it, and the plan never changes your budget total without telling you first.
 What Pro adds
   Salary plan:  income at the top, every part of it given a job — spending by category, savings and investments — what is left to plan, and Plan beside Actual.   Daily budget:  the first thing in your daily list — today’s budget, what you spent today and what is left. Repeating bills such as rent come out first, then what is left is shared across the days remaining. Tap it to see how the figure was worked out and what tomorrow looks like, or work it out from chosen categories up to a date, such as a trip. If the budget runs out you see “Budget used up” — free, always. More on the  daily budget .   Forecast:  where this period is heading at your current pace.   What-if plans:  try a daily target or a planned purchase and see the effect before you spend.
 Your overall daily budget and each category’s daily amount are calculated from the same budget and records; you never type in a separate daily target. Historical comparisons, averages and category changes stay free. Try the arithmetic without the app in the  daily budget calculator .
  Questions   Can I move money between budgets without changing the total?  Yes. In Stats → Budget, tap ••• on a budget and choose Move money in or Move money out. The move applies only to the current budget period and leaves the total unchanged. It is free.    How do I cover an overspent budget?  Tap Cover on an over-budget row. The suggested source leaves repeating bills still due covered. You can review the budgets and amount before confirming.    Is the daily amount for every budget included in Lifetime Pro?  Yes. Per-budget daily guidance is included in every Pro option, including Lifetime. Bills are accounted for first, and bills-only categories do not show a daily amount.    Can the budget month start on my payday?  Yes. Choose any start day from 1 to 31 under More, Period and Entry. It applies to the whole ledger, not just one budget.    Is budgeting free?  Yes. Total and category budgets, the today marker and the payday month are free. Move money, Cover, days left and the clearer spent/left amounts are free too. The salary plan, overall and per-budget daily guidance, forecasts and what-if plans are Pro.    Can I plan my salary like a zero-based budget?  Yes, with Pro. The salary plan puts your expected income at the top and shows how much of it is still to plan after spending by category and savings. It uses your existing categories and budgets rather than a second set of numbers.    Does it support biweekly pay?  The setting is a fixed monthly start day. Weekly and yearly views are worked out from your monthly budget, but there is no rolling two-week pay cycle.    Can I set my own daily budget?  No. The daily budget is your period’s budget, minus repeating bills and what you have spent, shared across the days left. To spend less per day, lower the budget.

## Daily Budget: What You Can Spend Today | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/daily-budget.html
 FEATURE · DAILY BUDGET · FREE + PRO
 What you can spend today, worked out for you.
 TrackExpenses turns your budget into one figure for today: what the period has left after its repeating bills, shared across the days to go. It sits at the top of your daily list, holds still all day, and says plainly when the budget is used up. You never type it in.

         Real app screens with example records, from an earlier version.
 How today’s figure is worked out
   Start from the period’s budget.  The total you set in More → Budgets, for a month that can start on your payday.   Take out repeating bills.  Rent, subscriptions and every other repeating expense in the period come out first, paid or still to come, so a bill due next week is already set aside.   Take out what you have spent.  Everything spent before today, plus anything you logged for a later date.   Share the rest across the days left,  today included, rounded down so the figure never promises more than there is.
   Example, in your main currency    Step  Amount      Monthly budget  4,000.00    Repeating bills this month (rent and subscriptions)  −1,500.00    Spent before today  −900.00    Left for everyday spending  1,600.00    Shared across 16 days, today included  100.00 a day
 Spend 40.00 today and the card says 60.00 left today. Tomorrow’s figure is worked out again from what is left: 1,560.00 across 15 days is 104.00. Spending less today raises tomorrow’s figure, and spending more lowers it. Tap the card to see the working step by step and what tomorrow looks like.
 It holds still all day
 Today’s figure is worked out before today’s spending, so it doesn’t shrink each time you buy something: today’s purchases count against it, and the card shows what you spent and what is left. It turns over at midnight. The figure always uses your budget’s own period, so a week or a year on screen never cuts a month’s rent into the wrong slice.
 When the budget is used up
 Once nothing is left to share, the card stops being about today. It says you are over your monthly budget and by how much, shows a bar with a notch where the budget ended, and counts the days left and any bills still due. Today’s budget sheet says when a fresh budget starts. This part is free, always: a used-up budget is a fact you should see without paying.
 A daily amount for each budget
 In Stats → Budget, every category budget shows its own daily amount for the days left, worked out the same way: that category’s repeating bills first, then what it has spent. A category made only of repeating bills shows no daily amount. See the  budget planner  for moving money between budgets and covering an overspend.
 A daily budget for a trip or the household
 With Pro, today’s figure can come from the budgets you choose instead of the whole budget. Open today’s budget, tap  Daily budget for  and pick  Chosen categories : one category, such as Travel, or several read as one, such as Groceries and Household. Only categories with a budget of their own are listed.
 Turn on  Stop on a date  for a trip: what those budgets have left is shared across the days up to that date, inside the current budget period, instead of to the end of the month. With 3,000.00 left and 10 days to go, that is 300.00 a day. The day after the last day, the daily budget is your whole budget again. Every place that shows the focused figure names the budgets it comes from, such as “Travel · until 20 Nov”.
 This changes only which daily figure the app shows you. Your budgets stay exactly as they are, and widgets and Siri keep to the whole budget. The choice is kept on the device where you made it.
 Free or Pro
 Free: budgets with a marker for today, spent and left amounts, days left, and the “Budget used up” and over-budget view. Pro, including Lifetime: today’s daily budget and its working, a daily amount for each budget, the daily budget for chosen categories up to a date, forecasts and what-if plans. Try the arithmetic in the browser with the  daily budget calculator  or, for a trip, the  travel budget calculator , and read  how to set a daily spending limit  and  tracking travel expenses abroad .
  Questions   Is the daily budget free?  The daily figure, the sheet that shows how it is worked out, a daily amount for each budget and the daily budget for chosen categories are part of Pro, including Lifetime. When the budget is used up, the app says so for free, with how far over you are and the days left.    Can I type my own daily budget?  No. It is always your period’s budget, minus repeating bills and what you have spent, shared across the days left. To spend less each day, lower the budget.    Why didn’t today’s figure change after I bought something?  It is worked out before today’s spending, so it holds still all day and today’s purchases count against it. The card shows what you spent today and what is left. Spending less today raises tomorrow’s figure.    Can I see a daily budget for a trip?  Yes, with Pro. In today’s budget, tap Daily budget for, choose the categories such as Travel, and turn on Stop on a date. What those budgets have left is shared across the days up to that date. The day after, the daily budget is your whole budget again.    Do widgets and Siri show the chosen categories?  No. Widgets and Siri keep to the whole budget. Choosing categories only changes the figure in the app, and your budgets stay as they are.

## Budget Alerts and Bill Reminders on iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/budget-alerts-and-bill-reminders.html
 FEATURE · ALERTS & REMINDERS · FREE
 A heads-up before the budget runs out, and before a bill is due.
 Two notifications, both free and both off until you turn them on. Budget alerts tell you when a budget is running ahead of its pace or has gone over. Bill reminders arrive the morning before rent, a subscription or any other repeating expense comes out.

         Real app screens with example records, from an earlier version.
 Budget alerts
 Open  More → Budgets  and turn on  Budget alerts ; iOS asks once whether TrackExpenses may send notifications. From then on the app watches the whole budget and every category budget in the current budget period.
   Ahead of pace at 80%:  when a budget passes 80% while spending is ahead of the month, past the marker for today. A typical alert reads “Groceries budget: 82% spent. AED 171.00 left for 12 days.”   Over, once:  when spending passes a budget. “Over the Food budget. AED 40.00 over, with 12 days left.”   Several at once, one notification:  when a few budgets cross a mark together, for example after a batch of bank alerts, you get one notification naming them.   No burst when you switch it on:  it starts from where your budgets stand and tells you about what happens next, not about the month so far.   News again only if it changes:  each mark is said once a period. If a budget drops back under it, because you moved money in or deleted an entry, crossing it again is news again.   Bills aren’t a warning:  a budget filled only by repeating bills, such as rent on the 1st, never gets the 80% alert. It still tells you if that budget goes over.
 Why not a flat 80%? Eighty percent spent with two days left is a budget working as planned. Every budget bar in the app pairs what you spent with where today falls, and the alerts follow the same rule. Tapping an alert opens Stats → Budget. A purchase that a bank alert automation imports is checked straight away, so an alert about it arrives with it rather than the next time you open the app.
   When the 80% alert fires, for a 30-day month    Day of the month  Share spent  Alert?      Day 12  82%  Yes, ahead of pace    Day 28  85%  No, on plan    Any day  Over 100%  Yes, once
 Bill reminders
 Open  More → Recurring  and turn on  Remind me the day before . The switch appears once you have a repeating expense. A  Next reminder  row then says which one comes next.
   9:00 the morning before:  early enough to move money the same day. “Rent is due tomorrow. AED 4,300.00 from Main Bank · Wednesday, 25 November.”   One notification a day:  bills due on the same day come together, biggest first, with the total, such as “3 bills are due tomorrow”.   Expenses only:  income never gets a reminder, and an expense that repeats more often than once a week is left out, so the one about the rent is never lost in daily noise.   Never late:  a reminder whose moment has passed is not sent afterwards.
 Tapping a reminder opens the Recurring screen. Reminders follow your repeating rules: add, change or stop a rule and the reminders change with it. More on rules in  accounts, cards and recurring  and the  subscriptions and recurring bills guide .
 Set on each device
 Notifications belong to a phone, so both switches are kept on the device where you turn them on, even with iCloud sync. If notifications are off for TrackExpenses in iOS Settings, the switch shows  Open Settings  and says why nothing can be sent.
 Free or Pro
 Both are free. Bill reminders cover your repeating expenses: 2 repeating rules are free, and Pro makes them unlimited. To see what is left for today rather than wait for an alert, see the  daily budget . Step by step:  get an alert before you overspend  and  get reminded before bills are due .
  Questions   Are budget alerts and bill reminders free?  Yes, both are free. Bill reminders cover your repeating expenses: 2 repeating rules are free, and Pro makes them unlimited.    Why didn’t I get an alert at 80%?  The 80% alert comes only when spending is ahead of the month’s pace, past the marker for today. 80% spent with two days left is a budget working as planned. A budget filled only by repeating bills never gets it. Also check that notifications are allowed for TrackExpenses in iOS Settings.    What time do bill reminders arrive?  At 9:00 in the morning, the day before the bill is due. Bills due on the same day come in one notification, biggest first.    Will I get a reminder for my salary?  No. Only repeating expenses get reminders. Income never does, and expenses that repeat more often than once a week are left out.    Do I have to turn them on on every device?  Yes. Notifications belong to each iPhone or iPad, so each switch is set on the device where you want the notifications.
  Step-by-step guides    Get Reminded Before Bills Are Due on iPhone    Get an Alert Before You Overspend      More features   Say it voice entry  Bank SMS and email alerts  Money coach  Budget moves, daily amounts & payday  Daily budget  Reports, calendar & insights  Multi-currency  Accounts, cards & recurring  Widgets, Siri & Shortcuts  iCloud sync  Private by design

## Expense Reports and Spending Insights | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/expense-reports.html
 FEATURE · REPORTS · FREE
 See where the money went, five different ways.
 TrackExpenses shows the same period as a daily list, a calendar, a month-by-month table, a summary and a by-description view, with stats for cash flow, daily average and the categories that changed most, and a search that adds up what it finds — all free.

            Real app screens with example records.
 The five lenses
   Daily:  every entry, grouped by day, with each day's total.   Calendar:  income and spending in a month grid; tap a day for its entries.   Monthly:  one row per period for the whole year, each with income, expenses and total.   Summary:  accounts and budget progress on one screen.   Description:  totals by payee, so recurring shops stand out.
 Stats that answer real questions
 Stats → Overview compares spending with the same point of the previous period, counts entries and the average per entry, names the top category, shows cash flow (income minus expenses), your average per calendar day and how many days had no spending. “What changed?” lists the categories that moved most; tap one to see its entries. Switch between weekly, monthly and yearly units.
 Know your money
 The Overview also carries a few plain facts about your habits, each shown only once there is enough history to say it:
   Fixed costs:  your repeating expenses, as a month and as a year.   Small purchases:  how much the little ones add up to.   Biggest spending day:  the weekday you tend to spend most, from the last eight weeks, with one-off big bills left out.   Kept from income:  what you kept last complete month, and your three-month rate.   Budget runway (Pro):  the day your budget runs out at your everyday pace, or how much you would have to spare.
 Facts only: no praise, no scolding.
 Filter and search
 Filter any lens by income, expense or transfer and by category — the totals strip always describes the same filtered set. Search looks through every period, by payee, note, amount or category, and adds up what it finds: under the number of matches it shows  Spent  and  Income  for every match, in your main currency, so “how much have I spent at this shop, ever?” takes one search ( how to see what you spent at one shop ). Transfers are counted as matches but in neither total. When there are more matches than the list shows, the totals still count all of them.
 Export & Share
 The share button on Transactions, in every lens, opens Export & Share; so does More → Backup & Export. It writes a spreadsheet (CSV) of this month, the last 3 or 6 months, this fiscal year or all transactions, each with how many entries it holds, optionally only what your filter shows, and the full JSON backup. Every export is part of Pro since version 1.15.0, and Pro adds CSV import. Your records stay in the app either way, free, and are never locked. See the  CSV export guide .
 Quicker to type
 When you add an entry by hand, arrows beside the date step one day back or forward and keep the time, and the date itself opens the calendar. Type a shop you have used before and its usual category and account fill in, but only the fields you haven’t picked yourself; the line under the description says where they came from.
  Questions   Are the reports free?  Yes. All five transaction views, Stats overview, category changes, Know your money (apart from the Pro budget runway), search with its totals and filters are free. Export and Share is Pro.    Can I export to Excel or Numbers?  Yes, with Pro. Tap the share button on Transactions to open Export and Share, write a CSV of a month, a range or every transaction, and open it in Numbers, Excel or Google Sheets. Every export is part of Pro.    Does search show a total?  Yes. Under the number of matches, search shows Spent and Income for every match in every period, in your main currency. Transfers are counted as matches but in neither total.

## Multi-Currency Expense Tracker for iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/multi-currency-expense-tracker.html
 FEATURE · CURRENCIES · FREE
 Spend in any currency. Read one total.
 TrackExpenses records each transaction in the currency you paid in, with the exchange rate you choose, and converts every total, budget and account balance into one main currency — so a trip abroad doesn’t break your month.

         Real app screens with example records.
 How it works
   Pick a main currency  under More → Main Currency. Every total is reported in it.   Add the currencies you use  under More → Additional Currencies.   Log in the currency you paid.  The entry sheet asks for the rate to your main currency and prefills the last rate you used for that currency.
 Accounts can hold money in their own currency, such as a USD travel account. The Accounts screen converts each balance into your main currency using the rate each entry was made at, and says so on screen.
 Why your own rate
 TrackExpenses doesn't fetch live rates from the internet. The rate your bank or card actually charged is the true one, and it often differs from a market rate. A foreign entry can't be saved without a rate, because saving it at 1 would quietly distort that currency's history.
 Built for
  Travel spending in several countries.  Expats paid in one currency and sending money home in another.  Bank alerts in foreign currencies: imported purchases wait for their rate instead of guessing, and a purchase abroad that your bank also states in your own currency imports at the amount you were charged.  Voice: say “dollars”, “pounds”, “rupees” or “riyals” and it means your own money when your ledger is kept in it, and the one most people mean otherwise.  Trips: give Travel a budget and see a  daily budget for the trip  up to its last day (Pro), or try the  travel budget calculator .
  Questions   Does TrackExpenses update exchange rates automatically?  No. You enter the rate, prefilled from the last one you used for that currency. This keeps the figures equal to what your bank actually charged.    Is multi-currency a Pro feature?  No. Main and additional currencies are part of the free ledger.
  Step-by-step guides    Track Travel Expenses Abroad on iPhone      More features   Say it voice entry  Bank SMS and email alerts  Money coach  Budget moves, daily amounts & payday  Daily budget  Budget alerts & bill reminders  Reports, calendar & insights  Accounts, cards & recurring  Widgets, Siri & Shortcuts  iCloud sync  Private by design

## Accounts, Credit Cards and Recurring Bills | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/accounts-and-transfers.html
 FEATURE · ACCOUNTS · 3 FREE
 Every account, every transfer, no double counting.
 TrackExpenses tracks cash, bank, card, savings, investment and loan accounts, records transfers between them, and shows assets, liabilities and a total that always reconcile. Recurring rules add your salary, rent and subscriptions on schedule.

         Real app screens with example records.
 Transfers are not spending
 Withdrawing cash, moving money to savings or paying off a credit card moves money between places you own. TrackExpenses records those as transfers, so the lunch you later buy with that cash is counted once. Bank SMS and email imports recognize ATM withdrawals, cash deposits and card bill payments and file them as transfers when both accounts are clear. An alert that names a card’s last digits lands on the account linked to that card, whether it is imported or pasted.
 Credit cards
 A card account carries what you owe as a liability. Purchases on the card are expenses; the monthly payment is a transfer from your bank to the card. Read the  credit card guide  for the full method.
 Recurring transactions
 More → Recurring creates rules every day, week, month or year — or every N of them, such as every 2 weeks. Each occurrence is created once, even when two of your devices sync. Turn on  Remind me the day before  on the same screen for a notification at 9:00 the morning before a repeating expense is due; see  bill reminders .
 Safe with history
 Want the same arithmetic without the app? The  net worth calculator  adds what you own and subtracts what you owe. An account with history is archived rather than deleted, so past balances still add up. A deleted transaction can be undone for a few seconds, everywhere in the app.
 Free or Pro
 Free includes 3 accounts and 2 recurring rules — enough for salary and rent. Pro makes both unlimited.
  Questions   How do I record paying my credit card bill?  Record it as a transfer from your bank account to the card account, not as an expense. The purchases on the card were already your spending.    Can I have more than three accounts?  Free covers three accounts, for example cash, bank and one card. Pro allows unlimited accounts.
  Step-by-step guides    Credit Card Payment vs Expense: Avoid Double Counting    Track Subscriptions and Recurring Bills on iPhone      More features   Say it voice entry  Bank SMS and email alerts  Money coach  Budget moves, daily amounts & payday  Daily budget  Budget alerts & bill reminders  Reports, calendar & insights  Multi-currency  Widgets, Siri & Shortcuts  iCloud sync  Private by design

## Expense Tracker Widgets and Shortcuts | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/widgets-and-shortcuts.html
 FEATURE · WIDGETS, SIRI & SHORTCUTS · FREE
 Your budget, one glance away.
 Ask Siri what you can spend today, log your morning coffee with one tap from a widget, and keep your budget on the Home Screen, the Lock Screen and in Control Center. Seven widgets, five controls, ten Siri phrases and four actions on the app icon, and the app shows each one with your own figures in More → Siri, Shortcuts & Widgets.

         Real app screens with example records.
 Ask Siri
 Say the app's name in the phrase. “What can I spend today in TrackExpenses” answers with what is left of today's daily budget: the period's budget after repeating bills, shared across the days left. “How much did I spend on Groceries in TrackExpenses” uses your own category names. “Tell TrackExpenses what I spent” takes a sentence such as “coffee 15 and taxi 40 with cash”, reads it back and saves it when you say yes. “Log my Coffee in TrackExpenses” logs a saved template. Siri asks you to unlock before it reads out a budget or a balance; logging works hands-free with the phone locked. The phrases also work in Arabic. Read the  Siri and widgets guide  for every phrase.
 Seven widgets
   Today:  what you can spend today, after bills, shared across the days left.   Budget:  what is left this period, with a marker for where today falls.   Quick Log:  your saved templates as buttons; one tap logs the coffee, fare or lunch without opening the app.   Category Budgets:  each category against its budget, with today's pace beside it.   Spending Overview:  today, the last two weeks, income and net balance.   Accounts:  net worth and your balances, all in your main currency.   Quick Add:  type, say or paste a bank message; a Lock Screen microphone opens Say it.
 Quick Log, Category Budgets and Accounts can each follow one template, category or account: touch and hold the widget and choose Edit Widget. Every widget but Quick Add’s larger size also fits the Lock Screen, and figures stay hidden there until you unlock an iPhone with a passcode.
 Actions on the app icon
 Touch and hold the TrackExpenses icon on your Home Screen for four shortcuts:  Say an expense ,  New expense ,  Paste bank message  and  Ask your coach . Each opens the app straight on that screen. They appear once you have finished setting up the app.
 Control Center and the Action button
 On iOS 18 and later, add  Quick Log ,  Today's Budget ,  Add an Expense ,  Say an Expense  and  Paste an Expense  to Control Center or the bottom of the Lock Screen. Set Quick Log to your morning coffee and put it on the Action button: one press logs it and the app never opens.
 Shortcuts and automations
 Every action is ready in the Shortcuts app, from Log an Expense and Log Income to Today's Budget, Category Spending and Account Balance, plus Import Bank Message and Import Wallet Transaction for automations. Try a morning automation that says what you can spend today, or a Wallet automation that logs Apple Pay purchases (see the  Apple Pay guide ).
 Quick Add and templates
 The Quick Add button holds two shortcuts: paste a bank message to fill the amount, merchant and date, or tap a saved template for the things you buy every week. Turn on “Save as template” in the entry sheet to make one, and it appears on the Quick Log widget, in Siri and on the Quick Log control too.
  Questions   Are the widgets and Siri free?  Yes. Every widget, control and Siri phrase is free. The daily budget figure on the Today widget and in Siri's answer is part of Pro; without Pro, Today shows what you have spent today. “Tell TrackExpenses what I spent” counts as voice entry: 10 saved entries a month free, unlimited with Pro.    Does a Quick Log tap need the app open?  No. The entry is saved on your iPhone straight away and the widget says it is waiting; it appears in your ledger the next time you open TrackExpenses.    Does anything leave my phone?  No. Widgets, controls and Siri read a short summary TrackExpenses keeps on the device; nothing is sent anywhere to make them work.    What does touching and holding the app icon do?  It shows four actions: Say an expense, New expense, Paste bank message and Ask your coach. Each opens the app on that screen, and they are free.    Which iOS do I need?  Control Center and Lock Screen controls need iOS 18 or later. Widgets, Siri and Shortcuts work from iOS 17.

## iCloud Sync for iPhone, iPad and Mac | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/icloud-sync.html
 FEATURE · ICLOUD SYNC · FREE
 One ledger on your iPhone, iPad and Mac.
 Log a coffee on your iPhone and it is on your iPad and Mac a moment later, with your budgets, accounts and settings. TrackExpenses syncs through your own private iCloud. It is free for everyone, there is nothing to press, and there is no account to create.

         Real app screens with example records. With sync on, every device shows the same ledger.
 How it works
   Automatic:  every entry, budget, account and setting syncs on its own. More → iCloud Sync shows whether this device is up to date.   Private:  the ledger is kept in the private part of your own iCloud, under your Apple Account. There is no TrackExpenses account and no server of the developer’s in between, so the developer can’t see it.   Works offline:  log entries anywhere. They are saved on the device and sync when it is back online.   Free:  sync is part of the free app. It uses a little of your iCloud storage.
 Add another device
   Sign in with the same Apple Account  on the other device, with iCloud on.   Install TrackExpenses  from the App Store. It runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS or iPadOS 17 or later, and on Mac computers with Apple silicon.   Open it.  Your ledger arrives within a minute or two. Keep the app up to date on every device that shares your iCloud.
 What stays on each device
 A few things belong to one device and are set there: the App Lock passcode; the theme, appearance and app icon; and the switches for  budget alerts and bill reminders , because a notification belongs to the phone it arrives on. The bank SMS and email automation runs on the iPhone that receives the messages, and what it files appears on every device. Free allowances, such as 10 voice entries and 10 automatic bank imports a month, are counted on each device.
 When devices disagree
 If two devices end up with different month start days or currencies, for example because both were set up before sync caught up, More → iCloud Sync shows  Your devices disagree  with both sets side by side. Tap the one you want and confirm  Use on Every Device . Your entries, accounts and budgets stay as they are; only the settings change.
 Erase and restore reach every device
 Because the ledger is shared,  Erase all data  in More → Backup & Export deletes it from this device and every device that syncs with your iCloud, and restoring a backup (Pro) replaces it everywhere. Both ask before they do anything. The  privacy page  explains what stays where, and the  privacy policy  has the full wording.
  Questions   Is iCloud sync free?  Yes. Sync is part of the free app for everyone. It uses a little of your iCloud storage.    Can the developer see my synced data?  No. The ledger is kept in the private part of your own iCloud, under your Apple Account. There is no TrackExpenses account and no developer server in the sync.    Does TrackExpenses run on a Mac?  Yes, on Mac computers with Apple silicon, from the App Store. With iCloud sync on, the Mac shows the same ledger as your iPhone and iPad.    What doesn’t sync?  The App Lock passcode, the theme, appearance and app icon, and the switches for budget alerts and bill reminders are set on each device. The bank SMS and email automation runs on the iPhone that receives the messages, and what it files appears everywhere.    My devices show different months or currencies. What do I do?  Open More, then iCloud Sync. Under Your devices disagree, tap the settings you want and confirm Use on Every Device. Your entries, accounts and budgets stay as they are.    Can I share my budget with my partner?  No. Sync joins the devices signed in to one Apple Account. There are no shared budgets between two people.
  More features   Say it voice entry  Bank SMS and email alerts  Money coach  Budget moves, daily amounts & payday  Daily budget  Budget alerts & bill reminders  Reports, calendar & insights  Multi-currency  Accounts, cards & recurring  Widgets, Siri & Shortcuts  Private by design

## Private Expense Tracker, No Bank Login | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/features/private-expense-tracker.html
 FEATURE · PRIVACY · FREE
 A money app that never asks for your bank password.
 TrackExpenses has no bank connection and no app account. Your ledger lives on your own devices, with optional sync through your own private iCloud, and App Lock protects it with a passcode and Face ID.

         Real app screens with example records.
 What stays where
   No bank login:  entries come from you, your voice, alerts you paste, or bank texts and emails you choose to pass in through Shortcuts.   No account:  nothing to sign up for; no email required.   On your devices:  the ledger is stored on your iPhone or iPad. Optional  iCloud sync  uses the private part of your own iCloud to keep it the same on your iPhone, iPad and Mac.   Messages aren't kept:  an imported alert is read and discarded; only the transaction is saved.   Voice stays local:  speech is recognized on the device.   The coach asks first:  questions the phone can answer, charts and logging stay on the device. An open question goes to an AI only after you agree, and never with your notes, receipts, account names or numbers, or balances.  What leaves your phone .
 App Lock
 More → App Lock sets a passcode, with Face ID to unlock. The passcode protects this device only and never leaves it.
 When Pro or a trial ends
 Nothing you saved is locked. Your entries, accounts and repeating bills stay as they are and keep working, even past the free limits of 3 accounts and 2 repeating rules. A short note says what changed: a Pro theme goes back to the standard one and a Pro app icon to the main icon, and both come back by themselves if you get Pro again.
 Your data, portable
 Your records stay in the app, free, and are never locked. Pro adds Export & Share (a CSV of any span and the full JSON backup), restoring a backup and CSV import, so you can move in or out without losing history. More → Backup & Export → Erase all data deletes everything from this device and every device that syncs with your iCloud. The  privacy policy  explains each kind of data in detail.
  Questions   Does TrackExpenses connect to my bank?  No. There is no bank connection and no bank login. Transactions come from manual entry, voice, alerts you paste, or bank messages you choose to pass in.    Do I need an account?  No. There is no app account. Sync, if you turn it on, uses your own private iCloud.    Can I lock the app?  Yes. App Lock sets a passcode with Face ID unlock, and it is free.    What happens to my data if Pro ends?  Nothing you saved is locked. Entries, accounts and repeating bills stay and keep working. A Pro theme and app icon go back to the standard ones and return if you get Pro again.

 Pro is available as a monthly or annual subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase. Lifetime does not renew. If Pro or a trial ends, nothing you saved is locked. More answers in the  FAQ , and every release is listed in  what’s new .

 Who it suits

  People whose bank texts or emails every purchase  — common in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, India and much of Africa, Asia and Latin America. The reader understands alerts in English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese and many other languages.
  People paid monthly on a fixed day  who want the budget, charts and totals to run payday to payday, and a daily figure for what is left.
  Cash spenders and busy people  who would rather say “taxi 40” than open a form.
  Anyone who won't hand a budgeting app their bank password.  Nothing here connects to your bank.
  Travellers and expats  spending in more than one currency.
  People who want their money app in Arabic, German, Spanish or Portuguese , written for each language rather than translated word for word.

 The interface is in English, Arabic (right to left), German, Latin American Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. It is not a bank-sync app, it doesn't pay bills, and it has no shared budgets between two people. If you need automatic bank feeds, a different kind of app will suit you better.

## Press Kit: Screenshots, Icon and Facts | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/press.html
 TrackExpenses press kit.
 Expense Tracker: SMS & Voice (TrackExpenses) is an iPhone, iPad and Mac expense tracker that keeps itself up to date: bank alerts log themselves, you can say several purchases in one sentence, and it tells you what you can spend today. Everything on this page may be used in coverage.
  Download the press kit   ZIP, about 7 MB: app icon, English and Arabic screenshots, share images in five languages.

 Facts
   Name  Expense Tracker: SMS & Voice (short: TrackExpenses). In Mexico “Control de Gastos por Voz”, in Brazil “Controle de Gastos por Voz”, in Germany „Haushaltsbuch: Budget & Coach“.    Developer  Mohamed Elatabany, an independent developer in the United Arab Emirates    Platforms  iPhone and iPad with iOS/iPadOS 17 or later; Mac computers with Apple silicon    Languages  English, Arabic (right to left), German, Spanish (Latin America), Portuguese (Brazil)    First release  September 2026 on the App Store; version 1.16.0 on 18 November 2026    Business model  Free to download with a complete free ledger; Pro as a monthly or yearly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase    Category  Finance    Privacy  No bank login and no app account. The ledger stays on the device, with optional private iCloud sync

 Descriptions to copy
  One line:  The iPhone expense tracker that logs itself from bank alerts and your voice.
  Short:  TrackExpenses logs spending without the typing. A Shortcuts automation hands each bank SMS or email alert to the app, which reads the amount, shop, card and date, and you can say several purchases in one sentence. The budget month starts on payday, and the app shows what you can spend today. No bank login, no account.
  Long:  Most expense trackers fail at the same step: people stop typing receipts. TrackExpenses removes that step. Banks already text or email every card purchase; an Apple Shortcuts automation passes those alerts to the app, which reads the amount, shop, card and date across many bank formats in the Gulf, India, Latin America, Europe and the US, and leaves one-time codes and declined payments out. Saying “coffee 15, taxi 40 and lunch 60” creates three drafts, processed on the iPhone. Budgets follow a month that starts on payday, every budget bar shows where today falls, and the daily figure shares what is left across the days left after the bills still to come. An AI money coach answers questions about spending in plain language, most of them on the device. There is no bank connection and no account: the ledger stays on the user’s devices, with optional private iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Mac. The whole app, voice entry and coach included, works in English, Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese.

 What makes it different

  Bank alerts without a bank connection.  Many markets have no open-banking feed, but every bank texts or emails each purchase. The app reads those alerts; it never sees a bank password or the Messages inbox.
  Several purchases in one spoken sentence,  read on the device, with prices said the way people say them, in five languages.
  A budget month that starts on payday  (any day from the 1st to the 31st), with pacing that shows where today falls.
  A daily number : what is left after the bills still to come, shared across the days left.
  Built for Arabic speakers as much as English ones:  a full right-to-left interface, Arabic voice entry and Arabic bank alerts.

 Tap a screenshot for the full-size image (1320 × 2868). Arabic screenshots are in the ZIP; Spanish, Portuguese and German ones are on the App Store listing in those countries.

 About the developer
 TrackExpenses is designed, built and supported by  Mohamed Elatabany , an independent iOS developer in the United Arab Emirates. It is built around a simple fact: in the Gulf, India and much of Latin America, banks text or email every card purchase, yet most expense apps still ask people to type it again.

## Privacy Policy | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/privacy.html
 Privacy Policy
  Expense Tracker: SMS & Voice (TrackExpenses)  — last updated 18 November 2026.
 The short version
 TrackExpenses has no account and no login. Your ledger lives on your iPhone, and — if you leave iCloud on — in your own private iCloud database, never on a server of ours. We cannot see it, and neither can anyone else. The one server we run is the money coach's relay, which passes on a question you choose to type and keeps none of it (see  Ask your coach  below).
 This policy covers the app on iPhone, iPad and Mac, and the app for Android. Where Android works differently, the section  TrackExpenses for Android  below says how; everything else applies to both.
 What TrackExpenses stores

 The ledger you build: transactions with their amount, currency, date, category, account, payee and any note you write.
 Your accounts, account groups and their balances, your budgets, and your recurring rules.
 The categories you keep or create.
 Your settings: the day your fiscal month starts, your main and additional currencies, your reminder time, your app icon, and whether the app lock is on.

 Where it is stored
 On your device, in the app's own container. If iCloud is on for TrackExpenses, the same data syncs through  your private iCloud database  — that is Apple's infrastructure inside your Apple Account,  not a server of ours . We have no key to it, no console for it, and no way to read it. Turning iCloud off for TrackExpenses in your iOS settings keeps everything on the one device.
 Deleting the app removes the copy on that device. There is no copy on any server of ours: the coach's relay, the only server we run, keeps no content.
 What leaves your device
  Purchases.  TrackExpenses uses RevenueCat to manage subscriptions and restore purchases. RevenueCat receives purchase and receipt information, an anonymous app user ID it generates, a device identifier, and basic app and OS version details. This is used to work out whether you have Pro access and to understand purchases, subscriptions and advertising performance. It is not shared with data brokers. RevenueCat's own policy is at  https://www.revenuecat.com/privacy .
  Apple Ads measurement.  On app launch, RevenueCat can receive Apple's standard AdServices attribution token and use it to ask Apple whether an install came from an ad for TrackExpenses on the App Store. Apple may return the campaign, ad group, keyword, ad placement and country or region associated with that install. RevenueCat associates this attribution with the anonymous purchase record so we can measure which campaigns lead to purchases. Your ledger entries, balances, budgets, bank messages and voice recordings are never sent to RevenueCat or Apple Ads. This measurement does not request the advertising identifier (IDFA), use a custom account identifier, or send your subscription events back to Apple Ads.
  Apple.  Purchases are processed by Apple under Apple's own privacy policy, and iCloud sync is carried by Apple under your Apple Account. We never see your payment details.
  Ask your coach.  If you type a question to the money coach or tap one of its questions marked ✦, and only after you have agreed on the screen that asks, the question travels with a summary of this month and last month — totals, categories and their budgets, your biggest shops, your salary plan lines and your challenge — and with the questions you asked earlier in the same conversation and the coach's answers to them, to a small relay we run on Cloudflare, which passes it to Anthropic's Claude model and streams the answer back. If the model asks for more, the app answers from your ledger: totals by category, shop, day or month for up to the last 13 months, or, for a question about particular purchases, up to 20 of them with their date, shop name, category and amount.  Nothing else is sent : never your notes, receipts, account names or numbers, balances, or your whole transaction history. The relay keeps nothing you wrote or asked and logs no content; Anthropic does not use the data to train its models and deletes it within 30 days under its own terms at  https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy . To keep free questions fair, the relay counts how many questions each install asks (ten a month free), how many free questions come from one network address in a day, and, for subscribers, how many each subscription asks — counts that hold no content and don't say who you are; the network-address counts are deleted within two days. The questions the coach answers on your device (the green ones, and any month you name), the entries you type to log, the charts and the files it makes are worked out on your device and never leave it. You can withdraw your agreement at any time under More → Privacy & data.
 On iPhone, iPad and Mac, that is the complete list. Apart from Apple's services, RevenueCat's purchase and Apple Ads measurement, and the coach relay described above, there is no separate analytics SDK, advertising network SDK or crash reporter in the app. The Android app's list is in  TrackExpenses for Android  below.
 TrackExpenses never connects to your bank
 There is no bank login, no account aggregator, and no place to type a banking credential. TrackExpenses knows your balances because you told it, and for no other reason. It cannot move money, and it cannot see an account you have not entered yourself.
 SMS auto-import is not access to your messages
 iOS never hands an app your Messages inbox, and TrackExpenses does not ask for it. The optional SMS auto-import is a  Shortcuts automation that you set up and control : when a bank alert arrives, Shortcuts passes that one message's text to the app. The optional Apple Pay import works the same way through a Shortcuts Transaction automation, which hands the app the amount, the merchant and the card's name, and nothing else.
 It is read on your device. Only the amount, the merchant, the date and the last digits of the card the message names reach your ledger — as a transaction you can edit or delete like any other, marked as imported until you have looked at it. The message text itself is  never saved . Two small records are kept on the device so you can see the automation working: a short numeric fingerprint of each message for up to 24 hours, purely so that a retried automation cannot enter the same purchase twice, and an activity log of what each run did — the time, the outcome, and the amount and payee that reached your ledger, never the message. If you turn on import notifications, the app posts them locally. Nothing about the message leaves your device, and deleting the automation in Shortcuts ends the whole arrangement.
 You can also paste a bank message in yourself, on the new-transaction screen. It is read on the same terms: on your device, into a draft you check before saving, with the message text  never stored . On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, a message the app's own rules cannot read is passed to Apple's on-device model so that banks and languages the app was never taught can still be understood — that model runs on your iPhone, and the message does not leave it.
 Voice entry runs on your device
 On iPhone, iPad and Mac, speech is recognised on your device by Apple's on-device speech and Apple Intelligence models. Audio is streamed straight to the recogniser as you speak — it is  never written to a file , never stored, and never uploaded — and it is discarded as soon as the draft transaction appears. What voice entry produces is a draft you confirm, not an entry made behind your back. On Android, voice entry runs on the phone whenever the phone can recognise your language; when it can't, see  TrackExpenses for Android  below.
 TrackExpenses for Android
 The Android app keeps the same ledger and the same promises: no account, no login, and no connection to your bank. As on iPhone, the only server we run is the money coach's relay, which keeps no content. It differs from the iPhone app in these ways.

  Where your ledger is stored.  On your phone, in the app's private storage. There is no iCloud on Android, and the app does not sync between devices. If backup to your Google Account is on, Android includes the app's data  only when that backup is end-to-end encrypted  with your screen lock (Android 9 or later, with a PIN, pattern or password set); without that encryption the app tells Android to leave its data out of the cloud backup. The app lock's passcode is never backed up.
  Bank alerts come from notifications, not from your messages.  The Android app asks for no SMS permission and cannot read your messages. The optional automatic import uses Android's  Notification access , which you turn on yourself in Android's settings after the app explains what it will read and you tap Agree. It reads notifications only from the banking and messaging apps you pick, ignores every other app's, and reads them on your phone. As on iPhone, only the amount, the merchant, the date and the last digits of the card reach your ledger, the notification text is  never saved , and the same 24-hour message fingerprint and activity log are kept on the phone. You can turn Notification access off at any time in Android's settings. A bank message you share to the app or paste in yourself is read on the same terms.
  Voice entry: on your phone first, Google's speech service otherwise.  When your phone can recognise your language on the device, speech is recognised there and the audio does not leave the phone. When it can't (some phones, older Android versions, or a language the phone's on-device recogniser doesn't have), the app uses Google's speech recognition service on your phone, which may send the audio to Google to turn it into text, under Google's privacy policy at  https://policies.google.com/privacy . When that is the case, the app says so before you speak, in one line on the listening screen, the voice limit screen and the first microphone question: "On this phone, Google's speech service turns what you say into text. Nothing is saved." The listening screen also says "Google speech" while it listens. Either way the app streams the audio to the recogniser, never writes it to a file and never keeps it; only the words come back, as a draft you confirm.
  The on-device model and ML Kit diagnostics.  On Android phones that have Google's on-device Gemini Nano model, a sentence or a pasted message the app's own rules cannot read may be passed to that model through Google's ML Kit. The model runs on your phone, and the text does not leave it. ML Kit, which the app includes for this, sends Google diagnostic information about how it is working: device and app information, performance metrics, the API configuration, event types, error codes, the languages configured, and a per-installation identifier. It never includes your messages, your sentences or your ledger. Google describes it at  https://developers.google.com/ml-kit/android-data-disclosure .
  Purchases.  On Android, purchases are made through Google Play, under Google's privacy policy, and we never see your payment details. RevenueCat receives the Google Play purchase information, the anonymous app user ID it generates, and basic device, app and OS version details, to work out whether you have Pro access and to understand purchases. There is no Apple Ads measurement, and no other advertising measurement, on Android. A purchase belongs to the store it was made in: Pro bought on the App Store does not unlock the Android app, and Pro bought on Google Play does not unlock the iPhone app, because there is no TrackExpenses account to connect the two.
  Ask your coach.  Works on Android exactly as described above under  Ask your coach : only after you agree on the screen that asks, the question, the conversation so far and the same summary of this month and last month go to the same relay we run and on to Anthropic's Claude model, with the same limits on what is sent and nothing kept. The relay counts free questions by the install's random identifier and checks Pro with RevenueCat's anonymous app user ID. You can withdraw your agreement at any time under More → Privacy & data.
  Ratings.  When the app asks for a rating, it uses Google Play's in-app review, which Google Play handles.
  Permissions.  The microphone, only when you tap to speak. Notifications, only for what you turn on: import notices, the daily reminder, bill reminders the day before a repeating expense, budget alerts, and the coach's weekly check-ins while you are in one of its challenges; all of them are worked out and posted on the phone, and none of them is sent from a server. Fingerprint or face unlock through Android's own prompt, which tells the app only whether it succeeded. A receipt photo through Android's photo picker, which hands the app only the photo you choose. The app asks for no SMS, contacts, location or storage permission, and does not request the advertising ID.
  Deleting.  Uninstalling the app removes its data from the phone. To remove an encrypted backup, delete it from your Google Account's backups in Android's settings. For the purchase record Google Play and RevenueCat hold, email us and we will request its deletion on your behalf.

 Things people reasonably assume, that aren't true here

  TrackExpenses does not access your contacts, your photos, your location, or any other app.
  Face ID / Touch ID.  If you turn on the app lock, authentication is handled entirely by iOS. TrackExpenses is told only whether it succeeded. Your biometric data never reaches the app.
  Notifications  are scheduled locally on your device. Nothing is sent through a server.
  The widget and the Siri shortcuts  read a small summary from a shared container on your device only.

 Tracking
 TrackExpenses  does not track you  across other companies' apps or websites and does not share data with data brokers. It never requests the advertising identifier. Apple's standard attribution described above is used only to measure ads for TrackExpenses; it does not use your ledger to target ads or build an advertising profile.
 Your data, your control

  Export.  With TrackExpenses Pro, Export & Share on the Transactions screen exports any month, any date range or the whole ledger as a CSV for spreadsheets, and writes a full-fidelity JSON backup of everything the app holds, which More → Backup & Export can restore. You choose where each file goes; nothing is uploaded. Without Pro, everything you logged stays in the app, and on iPhone, iPad and Mac in your own iCloud, readable as before.
  Import.  With Pro, More → Backup & Export also reads a CSV file you pick — from a spreadsheet, another money app, or a bank. The file is read entirely on your device, you see exactly what it would add before anything is written, and nothing about it is uploaded. TrackExpenses only ever sees the one file you hand it.
  Delete.  Deleting the app removes its data from that device. To remove the synced copy, delete the app's iCloud data from your iOS settings under your Apple Account. For the purchase record Apple and RevenueCat hold, email us and we will request its deletion on your behalf.

 Children
 TrackExpenses is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect any information from children under 13.
 Not financial advice
 TrackExpenses is a record-keeping tool. Its insights — safe-to-spend, projected spending, comparisons against last period — are arithmetic on the numbers you entered. They are  not financial advice , and they are only ever as accurate as what you have recorded.
 Changes
 If this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it, and material changes will be noted in the app's release notes.

  18 November 2026:  the Android section now covers  Ask your coach  on Android, which uses the same relay as on iPhone, so it no longer says there is no server of ours; it also lists the Android app's bill reminders, budget alerts and the coach's weekly check-ins among its notifications, and the Export paragraph no longer suggests that Android keeps anything in iCloud. Nothing about the iPhone, iPad and Mac app changed.
  14 November 2026:  exporting a CSV, the month on screen included, is part of TrackExpenses Pro from version 1.15.0, where it was free before. Nothing about what the app stores or sends changed.
  9 November 2026:  the coach no longer uses Apple's App Attest, so the relay keeps no key for an install; a question you tap marked ✦ goes to the model like a typed one; the short version now names the coach's relay as the one server we run.
  8 November 2026:  added  Ask your coach : a question you type to the money coach, only after you agree on the screen that asks, is sent with a summary of this month and last month and the conversation so far to a relay we run and on to Anthropic's Claude model, which may ask the app for monthly totals or a few purchases. The relay counts questions per install, per subscription and, for a day, per network address, without content, and checks with Apple's App Attest that questions come from the real app. The tapped questions and everything else the coach says stay on your device.
  4 November 2026:  added  TrackExpenses for Android , which describes the Android app. Nothing about the iPhone, iPad and Mac app changed.

 Contact

## Support and Free / Pro Limits | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/support.html
 Support, from the developer.  Questions, bugs or corrections:  atabany.apps@gmail.com . Include your app version, device and iOS version. Redact identifying details in samples.  Most questions are answered in the  FAQ .  What stays free?  Unlimited manual transactions and pasted bank alerts, budgets, current-period budget moves and Cover, days left, budget alerts, bill reminders, historical stats, search with its totals and private iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Mac; up to 3 accounts and 2 recurring rules. Includes 10 successful automatic bank SMS or email imports, 10 saved voice entries and 10 AI questions to the money coach per calendar month on each device.  After the SMS allowance, later alerts are still caught and kept, but appear locked outside your totals; tapping one offers Pro. Upgrading adds them all to your ledger automatically. Otherwise, the next calendar month’s allowance releases as many as it covers. Nothing is dropped, and saved history is never locked.  What does Pro add?  Unlimited SMS and email imports, accounts and recurring rules; unlimited voice entry on compatible devices/languages; money coach challenges and many more coach questions; a salary plan, spending forecasts, overall and per-budget daily guidance, a daily budget for chosen categories and what-if planning; Export & Share (CSV of any range and the full JSON backup), CSV import, backup restore, themes and alternate icons. Monthly and annual subscriptions and a one-time lifetime purchase are available. Check current purchase details in the app.  If Pro or a trial ends, nothing you saved is locked: entries, accounts and repeating bills keep working, and a Pro theme and app icon come back if you get Pro again.  Restore or cancel  Tap Restore purchases in More (under Help & about), or Restore at the foot of the Pro screen, using the same Apple Account that bought Pro. If it remains locked, email the developer. Manage auto-renewing plans in  Apple's subscription settings . Lifetime does not renew.  Your month and your records  More → Period & Entry changes your fixed monthly start day. Every export is part of Pro since version 1.15.0: the share button on Transactions, or More → Backup & Export, opens Export & Share, with CSV for this month or a longer span and a full JSON backup. Backup & Export also imports CSV and restores a backup. Your records stay in the app, free, and are never locked.  Move money and Cover  Open Stats → Budget for the current period in your budget’s own period length. Tap ••• on a budget, then Move money in or Move money out. Moves are free, apply to this period only and keep the total unchanged. Tap Cover on an over-budget row for a suggested move; repeating bills still due are left covered in suggestions. Pro adds daily guidance per budget, including with Lifetime. See the  budget planner walkthrough .  SMS and voice help  See  SMS setup videos and complete guide ,  automation troubleshooting  and  voice requirements . SMS automation does not read your inbox. Voice produces drafts, and supported languages/devices vary.  Privacy and deletion  Your ledger is on your device with optional private iCloud sync. See the  complete policy  for storage, processing, purchase records and deletion. For purchase-data deletion requests, email the developer.

## FAQ: Bank Alerts, Privacy, Free and Pro | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/faq.html
 TrackExpenses questions, answered.
 Plain answers to what people ask before and after installing Expense Tracker: SMS & Voice (TrackExpenses): bank logins, messages, banks and countries, free and Pro, the money coach, languages and devices. Each answer describes version 1.16.0, the version on the App Store.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction
  Privacy and your data  ·  Bank alerts  ·  Free and Pro  ·  Budgets, alerts and reminders  ·  Money coach and voice  ·  Languages and devices
  Privacy and your data
  Does TrackExpenses connect to my bank?  No. There is no bank connection and no bank login. Entries come from typing, voice, alerts you paste, or Shortcuts automations you set up that pass bank texts, bank emails or Apple Pay purchases to the app.  How to track expenses on iPhone
  Do I need to create an account?  No. There is no TrackExpenses account and no email sign-up. If you turn on sync, it goes through your own private iCloud.
  Does TrackExpenses read my Messages or my email?  No. iOS doesn’t let an app read your inbox. A Shortcuts automation that you create passes each matching bank text or email to the app, one at a time. The app keeps what it read from the alert, never the message itself.
  Where is my data stored?  On your iPhone or iPad, and in the private part of your own iCloud if sync is on. The developer runs no server for your ledger. The one exception is a typed question you send to the money coach’s AI after agreeing to it.
  How do I delete all my data?  Open More, then Backup and Export, then Erase all data. It deletes your transactions, accounts, categories, budgets, recurring rules, templates, period notes and settings from this device and every device that syncs with your iCloud, and it can’t be undone. Deleting the app alone leaves the synced copy in your iCloud.
  Can I lock the app?  Yes, for free. More, then App Lock, sets a passcode with Face ID to unlock. The passcode stays on that device.

  Bank alerts
  Which banks and countries does it work with?  It reads alert formats from banks and wallets in the Gulf, India and the rest of Asia, Africa, Europe, the US and Latin America, in English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese and many other languages, but not every format. Paste one of your own alerts into the check on the SMS Auto-Import screen before relying on it: it shows exactly what would be saved.  Bank SMS and email alerts
  My bank only sends app notifications. Can TrackExpenses still log them?  Not automatically: no iPhone automation can read another app’s notification. iOS doesn’t let you copy a notification’s text, but if your bank’s app lets you copy a transaction’s details, tap Paste on the Transactions screen and the amount, shop and date are filled in, ready to check. Pasting is free and unlimited. Many banks can also send SMS or email alerts, which an automation can log.  Pasting an alert
  Can it log bank alerts that arrive by email?  Yes. Add the email account, such as Gmail, to Apple’s Mail app, then create a Shortcuts Email automation filtered on a word from the alert subject, with the Import Bank Message action. Shortcuts can see Mail, not the Gmail app. The app shows the steps under More, SMS Auto-Import, Bank alerts by email.  Bank email alerts guide
  What does the bank alert reader skip?  One-time codes, declined payments, fraud checks, payment requests, bills that are only due and promotions are left out. Anything uncertain, such as a possible duplicate or a card it doesn’t know yet, is saved and flagged for a look.
  How many bank alerts are free?  Ten successful automatic imports per calendar month on each device, SMS and email together. Later alerts are caught and kept, locked outside your totals; Pro adds them all, otherwise next month’s allowance releases as many as it covers. Pasting an alert by hand is free and unlimited.

  Free and Pro
  Is TrackExpenses free?  Yes. The free ledger has unlimited manual entries, budgets with a marker for today, moving money between budgets, reports, search, budget alerts, bill reminders, multiple currencies, widgets and private iCloud sync, with 3 accounts and 2 recurring rules. Voice entry, automatic bank imports and AI questions to the coach are free 10 times a month on each device.  Free and Pro side by side
  What does Pro add?  Unlimited voice entry, bank imports, accounts and recurring rules; coach challenges and many more coach questions; today’s daily budget, a daily amount for each budget and a daily budget for chosen categories; the salary plan, forecasts and what-if plans; Export and Share, CSV import and backup restore; themes and alternate app icons. Pro is a monthly or annual subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase, with prices shown in the app.
  What happens when Pro or a free trial ends?  Nothing you saved is locked. Entries, accounts and repeating bills stay and keep working, even past the free limits. A Pro theme goes back to the standard one and a Pro app icon to the main icon, and both come back if you get Pro again. A short note says what changed.
  Can I export my data?  Yes, with Pro. Export and Share, from the share button on Transactions or More, Backup and Export, writes a CSV of this month, the last 3 or 6 months, this fiscal year or all transactions, and the full JSON backup. Every export is part of Pro since version 1.15.0. Your records stay in the app either way.

  Budgets, alerts and reminders
  Can my budget month start on payday?  Yes. More, Period and Entry sets any start day from 1 to 31, and every list, chart, budget and total follows it. A day past the end of a short month means its last day. There is no rolling two-week period.  Payday budget guide
  How is today’s budget worked out?  Your period’s budget, minus its repeating bills, paid or still to come, and what you spent before today, shared across the days left including today and rounded down. It holds still all day. The figure is part of Pro; when the budget is used up, the app says so for free.  How to set a daily spending limit
  Can TrackExpenses warn me before I overspend?  Yes, for free. Turn on Budget alerts in More, Budgets: a notification when a budget passes 80% while ahead of its pace, and once when it goes over, with what is left and the days it has to last.  Get an alert before you overspend
  Can it remind me about bills?  Yes, for free. Turn on Remind me the day before in More, Recurring: a notification at 9:00 the day before a repeating expense is due, with the amount and the account. Bills due on the same day come in one notification.  Get reminded before bills are due
  Does it handle several currencies?  Yes, for free. Pick a main currency and log in more than 110 others at the rate your bank charged; every total and balance converts to the main currency. Rates are not fetched from the internet.  Track travel expenses abroad

  Money coach and voice
  What does the money coach send to an AI?  Only open questions the phone can’t answer, and only after you agree on screen. It sends your question, the conversation so far and a summary of this month and last month, and, if the model asks, totals for up to 13 months or up to 20 purchases with date, shop, category and amount, through the developer’s relay to Anthropic’s Claude. It never sends notes, receipts, account names or numbers, or balances.  What leaves your phone
  Which questions does the coach answer without AI?  What you spent today or yesterday, what is left in a category, your balances, how a named month went, whether you are on pace, where your money goes and how you compare with last month, plus charts, files and typed purchases. These are worked out on your phone and never use one of your questions.
  Does voice entry send my audio anywhere?  No. Speech is recognized on your device, and every result is a draft you check before saving. Ten saved voice entries a month are free on each device; Pro makes it unlimited.  Say it voice entry

  Languages and devices
  Which languages is TrackExpenses in?  English, Arabic with a full right-to-left layout, German, Latin American Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. Voice entry, the bank alert reader and the money coach work in all five. To change it, tap Language in More, which opens the app’s page in iOS Settings.
  Does it work on iPad and Mac?  Yes. It runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS or iPadOS 17 or later, and on Mac computers with Apple silicon through the App Store. With iCloud sync on, all of them show the same ledger.  iCloud sync
  Is there an Android version?  No, it is not on Google Play. TrackExpenses is on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and runs on Mac computers with Apple silicon.
  Can two people share one budget?  No. Sync joins the devices signed in to one Apple Account, and there are no shared budgets between two people.

 Not answered here? See  support , the  guides ,  what’s new  in each version, or write to the developer.
