## Daily Budget Until Payday Calculator | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/daily-budget.html
 What is left to spend per day?
 Subtract spending and any extra commitments from your period budget, then divide by the days left, including today. This is budget arithmetic; an unrecorded bill or purchase can change the answer.
  Daily budget until payday  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount.
   Period budget    Recorded spending    Extra upcoming commitments   Only commitments not already in recorded spending.   Today's date    Last day of this budget period   Usually the day before your next payday.    Calculate daily budget
 Example: 1,200 − 480 − 120 = 600 remaining. Over 10 days including today, that is 60.00 per day.   JavaScript enables the calculator. Use the formula and table below without it; all guides and examples remain readable.
 Reference examples    Illustrative amounts in one currency; remaining days include today    Budget  Spent  Extra commitments  Days left  Per day      1,200  480  120  10  60.00    1,200  600  0  15  40.00    900  850  50  5  0.00    900  950  0  5  0.00 (50 over budget)    600  420  0  1  180.00
 The formula and its limits   Daily amount = max(0, budget − recorded spending − extra commitments) ÷ days left.  We include today and the last day. A period ending today has one day left. A date in the past produces an error instead of an invented allowance. The daily amount is rounded down to the cent, as TrackExpenses does, so it never promises more than is left.  Only subtract extra commitments once. If next week's rent is already included in recorded spending, leave it out of the extra-commitments field. This calculator offers an optional reserve you choose; it is not an exact replica of every TrackExpenses forecasting scenario.  From an example to your ledger  TrackExpenses lets your month start on a fixed monthly payday and keeps transactions, budgets and charts in the same window. Ordinary budget facts and pacing stay free. Pro adds daily guidance, forecasts and what-if plans based on your recorded figures.   Set your monthly payday period  ·  Check recorded spending in CSV   More calculators:  Budget pacing calculator  ·  Payday calculator  ·  Monthly budget calculator  ·  Travel budget calculator  ·  50/30/20 budget calculator  ·  All calculators
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## Budget Pacing Calculator: Am I Overspending? | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/budget-pacing-calculator.html
 Budget pacing calculator
 Compare how much of your budget is spent with how much of the period has passed. The calculator shows whether you are spending faster or slower than an even pace, where the period ends if nothing changes, and what you can spend per day from today.
  Am I spending too fast?  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount.
   Period budget    Spent so far   Up to the end of yesterday gives the cleanest reading.   First day of the period   Usually your payday.   Last day of the period   Usually the day before your next payday.   Today's date     Check my pace
 Example: 60% of a 3,000 budget is spent with 50% of the period gone. That is 300.00 more than an even pace.
   Your pace    Measure  Result      Budget spent  60%    Period passed  50% (15 of 30 days)    Even pace by today  1,500.00    Against an even pace  300.00 over    Period ends at this pace  3,600.00 (600.00 over budget)    Per day to stay within budget  80.00 for 15 days
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 An even pace through a 30-day period
   Days already completed, and what an even pace has spent of a 3,000 budget    Day of period  Days completed  Period passed  Even pace      1  0  0%  0    6  5  16.7%  500    11  10  33.3%  1,000    16  15  50%  1,500    21  20  66.7%  2,000    26  25  83.3%  2,500    30  29  96.7%  2,900
 The budget pacing formula
  Budget spent = spending ÷ budget. Period passed = days completed ÷ days in the period.  When the first share is larger than the second, you are spending faster than an even pace. The gap in money is spending − budget × period passed.
 Days completed are the days before today, so on the first day nothing has passed yet. The days in the period include both its first and its last day. In the example, 25 September to 24 October is 30 days; at the start of 10 October, 15 are complete. Spending of 1,800 is 60% of 3,000, the period is 50% gone, an even pace would have spent 1,500, and the gap is 300.
  Period ends at this pace = spending ÷ days completed × days in the period.  1,800 over 15 days is 120 a day; 30 such days come to 3,600, which is 600 over.  Per day to stay within budget = what is left ÷ days left, today included.  1,200 over 15 days is 80 a day.
 How to read the answer
 An even pace is a reference line, not a rule. Rent, a loan payment or a yearly insurance bill paid in the first week puts anyone far over an even pace on day five, and nothing is wrong. Two ways to get a truer reading:
   Pace only what varies.  Take your fixed bills out of both figures: enter the budget without them and spending without them. What remains is groceries, transport, eating out and the rest of everyday spending, which is the part a pace can describe.   Look at the daily figure.  If the amount per day for the rest of the period is one you can live on, an early bill has not hurt you. If it is far below what you normally spend in a day, the pace is telling you something real.
 Being under pace is not automatically good news either: a bill that has not arrived yet is not money saved. Check what is still due before the period ends.
 The same check on your real spending
 In TrackExpenses every budget bar carries a marker for today, so spending and time are read together without a calculation; that is free, and your month can start on your payday. An optional budget alert tells you when a budget passes 80% while ahead of pace. Pro adds the daily budget, worked out after repeating bills, and a forecast of where the period ends.
  Guide: budget pacing explained  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator  ·  Payday calculator  ·  Budget planner in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  What is budget pacing?  Budget pacing compares the share of a budget already spent with the share of the period already passed. Spending 60% of the budget when half the period is gone means you are spending faster than an even pace.
  What is the budget pacing formula?  Divide spending by the budget, and divide the days completed by the days in the period. The difference in money is spending minus the budget multiplied by the share of the period passed.
  Is spending faster than an even pace always a problem?  No. Fixed bills paid early in the period, such as rent, put you over an even pace without any overspending. Leave fixed bills out of both figures to pace only everyday spending.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## Monthly Budget Calculator: Zero-Based Plan | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/monthly-budget-calculator.html
 Monthly budget calculator
 To make a monthly budget, start from your take-home pay for the month and subtract every spending line and what you will save, until nothing is left to plan. Enter your pay and your lines below: the calculator shows the planned total, what is left to plan or how far over you are, and each line's share of your income.
  Plan your month  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount.
   Take-home pay   One paycheck, after tax and deductions.   I am paid   Once a month  Twice a month  Every two weeks  Every week   Turned into a month: weekly pay × 52 ÷ 12, every two weeks × 26 ÷ 12, twice a month × 2.
  Your lines for the month  Change, add or remove lines. Mark what you put aside as Saving.
   Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove    Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove    Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove    Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove    Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove    Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove    Line    Per month    Counts as   Spending  Saving    Remove
  Add a line
 Plan my month
 Example: take-home pay of 4,000 a month with 3,310 planned (83%) leaves 690 (17%) to plan.
   Your plan for the month    Line  Per month  Share of income      Housing  1,400.00  35%    Groceries  500.00  13%    Transport  250.00  6%    Bills and utilities  300.00  8%    Eating out  200.00  5%    Subscriptions  60.00  2%    Savings  600.00  15%      Spending  2,710.00  68%    Saving  600.00  15%    Planned  3,310.00  83%    Left to plan  690.00  17%
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 One paycheck as a month
   Monthly take-home pay from one paycheck, in one currency    Paycheck  Every week  Every two weeks  Twice a month      500  2,166.67  1,083.33  1,000.00    1,000  4,333.33  2,166.67  2,000.00    1,500  6,500.00  3,250.00  3,000.00    2,000  8,666.67  4,333.33  4,000.00    2,500  10,833.33  5,416.67  5,000.00    3,000  13,000.00  6,500.00  6,000.00
 How it is calculated
  Monthly income = one paycheck × paychecks in a year ÷ 12.  A year holds 52 paychecks for weekly pay, 26 every two weeks, 24 twice a month and 12 once a month, so the result is an average month. Paid every two weeks, most months bring two paychecks and two months of the year bring three, so the average is slightly more than two paychecks. To plan only on money that arrives every month, choose twice a month, which counts two paychecks, and give each third paycheck a job when it arrives.
  Planned = every spending line + every saving line. Left to plan = monthly income − planned.  When that figure is below zero, the plan is over your income by that much. Each line's share is its amount ÷ monthly income × 100, shown as a whole percent and rounded half away from zero, so 12.5% shows as 13%. Left to plan shows 100% less the planned share, so the two always add up to 100% on screen, however each one rounds. In the example, 3,310 of 4,000 is 82.75%, shown as 83%, and the 690 left is 17%.
 Why aim for zero left to plan
 A zero-based budget does not mean spending everything. It means every part of your pay has a job before the month starts, and saving is one of the jobs. Money left without a job tends to disappear into small purchases, which is why the calculator keeps it visible as its own figure.
   Start with what you cannot move:  rent or mortgage, bills, insurance, transport to work and minimum debt payments.   Then the flexible lines:  groceries, eating out, shopping and subscriptions, at amounts your last two or three months support.   Give the rest a job:  savings, an emergency fund or extra debt payments, until left to plan reaches zero.
 If the plan comes out over, lower the flexible lines first. Want a rule of thumb instead of line by line? The  50/30/20 budget calculator  splits the same pay into needs, wants and savings.
 How TrackExpenses does this
 In TrackExpenses, the salary plan answers the same question from your ledger: will this income cover everything you plan? It lists your income, a line for each spending category, Everything else, and a line for each Savings or Investment account under Saving & investing. Every planned line shows its share of income as a whole percent, rounded the same way as here, and the top of the plan shows Planned beside Left to plan, or Over by. Switch from Plan to Actual and each line shows what was spent or saved against its amount. A category's line is that category's budget, so the plan and your budgets never disagree.
 The salary plan is part of Pro. Category budgets, pacing against today and moving money between budgets are free. The plan follows your budget period, which starts on a day of the month you choose, usually payday. There is no every-two-weeks period, so if you are paid every two weeks, plan the month.
  Guide: a zero-based budget, step by step  ·  50/30/20 budget calculator  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator  ·  Emergency fund calculator  ·  Budget planner in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  What is a zero-based budget?  A budget in which take-home pay minus every planned spending and saving line comes to zero. Every part of your pay is given a job before the month starts, and saving counts as a job.
  How do I make a monthly budget if I am paid every two weeks?  Multiply one paycheck by 26 and divide by 12 for the average month: 2,000 every two weeks is 4,333.33. Most months bring only two paychecks, 4,000, so a safer plan is built on two and gives each third paycheck a job of its own, such as savings.
  Should savings count as a budget line?  Yes. Put savings in the plan as a line of its own, decided at the start of the month, instead of saving whatever is left at the end. In this calculator, mark it as Saving to see it apart from spending.
  What if my budget comes out over my income?  Lower the flexible lines first, such as eating out, shopping and subscriptions, then look at the fixed ones when a contract ends. Do not plan to cover the gap from savings without deciding to.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## 50/30/20 Budget Calculator: Weekly, Biweekly or Monthly Pay
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/50-30-20-calculator.html
 50/30/20 budget calculator
 Enter your take-home pay, whether you are paid every week, every two weeks, twice a month or once a month, and see what 50% for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for savings come to per paycheck, per month and per year. Change the three shares if 50/30/20 does not fit your rent.
  Split your take-home pay  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved.
   Take-home pay   After tax and deductions.   I am paid   Once a month  Twice a month  Every two weeks  Every week    Needs %    Wants %    Savings %   The three shares must add up to 100.    Calculate my split
 Example: take-home pay of 4,000 once a month gives 2,000 for needs, 1,200 for wants and 800 for savings.
   Your split    Share  Per paycheck  Per month  Per year      Needs (50%)  2,000.00  2,000.00  24,000.00    Wants (30%)  1,200.00  1,200.00  14,400.00    Savings (20%)  800.00  800.00  9,600.00
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 50/30/20 for common take-home amounts
   Monthly take-home pay split 50/30/20, in one currency    Take-home pay  Needs (50%)  Wants (30%)  Savings (20%)      2,000  1,000  600  400    3,000  1,500  900  600    4,000  2,000  1,200  800    5,000  2,500  1,500  1,000    6,500  3,250  1,950  1,300    8,000  4,000  2,400  1,600    12,000  6,000  3,600  2,400    20,000  10,000  6,000  4,000
 How the calculator works
  Each amount = take-home pay × its share ÷ 100.  The per-year column multiplies one paycheck by the number of paychecks in a year: 12 when you are paid once a month, 24 twice a month, 26 every two weeks and 52 every week. The per-month column is the year divided by 12, so someone paid every two weeks sees a month slightly larger than two paychecks: 26 paychecks do not fit evenly into 12 months.
 The display rounds to two decimal places. The three shares must add up to 100; if they do not, the calculator says what they add up to instead of guessing which one you meant to change.
 What goes in each share
   Needs  are payments you would have to make even in a tight month: rent or mortgage, utilities, groceries, insurance, getting to work, childcare and the minimum payment on any loan or card.   Wants  are the things you choose: eating out, delivery, shopping, entertainment, travel and most subscriptions.   Savings  is money you keep: an emergency fund, investments, retirement, and loan payments above the minimum.
 The split comes from the book All Your Worth by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi (2005), and it works on take-home pay. The  50/30/20 budget guide  has a full worked example, with every category sorted into its group.
 When 50/30/20 does not fit
 Add up your needs first. If rent alone takes 40% of your pay, needs will not stop at 50%, and no calculator changes that. Enter the shares your month really has, such as 60/20/20, and treat 50/30/20 as the direction to move in when a lease or a loan ends. What matters is that the three shares are decided on purpose and add up to all of your pay.
 From three numbers to a working budget
 A split is a plan for the month; it helps only if you compare it with what you spent. In TrackExpenses, category budgets, pacing against today and moving money between budgets are free. The salary plan, a Pro feature, lists your income, each spending category and your savings with each line's share of income, and shows Plan beside Actual at the end of the month.
  Monthly budget calculator  ·  Savings goal calculator  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator  ·  Subscription cost calculator  ·  Budget planner in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  Is the 50/30/20 rule based on income before or after tax?  After tax. Use your take-home pay: what reaches your account after tax and deductions. Where salaries are not taxed, that is the salary that arrives.
  Where do debt payments go in a 50/30/20 budget?  The minimum payment on a loan or card is a need. Anything you pay above the minimum counts in the 20% for savings, because it reduces what you owe.
  How does the 50/30/20 rule work with weekly or biweekly pay?  Apply the three shares to each paycheck, or turn the pay into a month first: multiply one paycheck by 52 if you are paid every week or by 26 if every two weeks, then divide by 12. 1,000 a week is 4,333.33 a month, so 2,166.67 for needs, 1,300 for wants and 866.67 for savings.
  Does the calculator work in pounds or other currencies?  Yes. The amounts carry no currency, so enter pounds, dollars, euros or any other currency. In the UK, use the net pay on your payslip, after Income Tax, National Insurance and any other deductions.
  What if my needs are more than 50% of my pay?  Then the split has shown you the real constraint. Use shares that match your month for now, such as 60/20/20, and bring needs down when you can. Do not take the difference out of savings without deciding to.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction

  When am I paid next?  Everything stays in this browser. Nothing is sent or saved.
   I am paid   Every two weeks  Every week  Once a month  Twice a month    A payday you know   Any past or coming payday. The others are counted from it.   Day of the month   31 means the last day of every month.   Second day of the month    If payday falls on a weekend   Keep the date  Pay on the Friday before    Today's date     Show my paydays
 Example: paid every two weeks from Friday 1 January 2027, the year has 27 paydays, and January, July and December have three.
   Paydays month by month    Month  Paydays  Count      January 2027  1, 15, 29  3    February 2027  12, 26  2    March 2027  12, 26  2    April 2027  9, 23  2    May 2027  7, 21  2    June 2027  4, 18  2    July 2027  2, 16, 30  3    August 2027  13, 27  2    September 2027  10, 24  2    October 2027  8, 22  2    November 2027  5, 19  2    December 2027  3, 17, 31  3
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the reference table and the counting rule below.
 Three-paycheck months in 2027
 If you are paid every second Friday, 2027 runs on one of two calendars. Find the first Friday you are paid in January.
   Paid every two weeks on a Friday: months with three paydays and paydays in the year, 2027    First payday  Three paydays in  In 2027      Friday 1 January  January, July, December  27    Friday 8 January  April, October  26
 Paid every Friday instead? In 2027 there are 53 Fridays, and January, April, July, October and December each have five. For any other weekday, enter one payday above and read the table the calculator prints.
 How the paydays are counted
  Every two weeks:  each payday is 14 days after the one before, counted from the date you entered. A year has 52 weeks and one day (two in a leap year), so it holds 26 such paydays and, once in a while, 27. Twelve months of two paydays make only 24, which is why two months of the year, sometimes three, carry a third.
  Every week:  each payday is 7 days after the one before. Most months have four and four or five months have five.
  Once or twice a month:  the payday is the same day number every month. A day that a short month does not have, such as the 31st in June or the 30th in February, moves to that month's last day. If you choose it, a payday on a Saturday or Sunday moves to the Friday before; when that Friday is in the month before, the table keeps it in its own month's row and writes the date with its month. Employers and countries differ here: some pay on the working day after, and where the weekend is Friday and Saturday the rule is different again, so check your contract or a past payslip.
  Days until payday  are counted from today to the next payday on the calendar. If today is a payday, the answer is zero and the result names the one after.
 What to do with a third paycheck
 Most monthly bills are sized for two paychecks. The simplest plan when you are paid every two weeks is to budget every month on two, then decide in advance what a third one is for: a yearly bill such as insurance, a savings goal, or paying a debt down faster. Decided ahead of time it is a plan; left open it tends to disappear into ordinary spending.
 The same reasoning works the other way round. Twice-a-month pay is 24 paydays a year, so there is never a third paycheck, but each one is a little larger than a two-weekly one for the same yearly salary.
 A budget month that starts on payday
 If you are paid once a month, TrackExpenses can start your month on that day: choose a start day from 1 to 31 in More → Period & Entry, and your transactions, budgets and charts all run from payday to the day before the next. The start day is a fixed day of the month; the app does not follow a two-weekly schedule by itself. With Pro, the salary plan has a place for extra income that belongs to one month only, which is where a third paycheck fits.
  Guide: budget from payday to payday  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator  ·  Budget pacing calculator  ·  50/30/20 budget calculator
 Questions
  How many paychecks are there in a year when you are paid every two weeks?  Usually 26. A year is 52 weeks and one day, so every eleven years or so a two-weekly schedule fits 27 paydays into one calendar year. In 2027 that happens when the first payday is Friday 1 January.
  Which months have three paychecks in 2027?  For pay every second Friday: January, July and December if your first payday of the year is 1 January, or April and October if it is 8 January. For another weekday, enter one of your paydays in the calculator.
  What is the difference between biweekly and twice a month?  Biweekly pay comes every 14 days, 26 times a year, on the same weekday. Twice-a-month pay comes on two fixed dates, 24 times a year, on changing weekdays. For the same yearly salary a biweekly paycheck is smaller, and two or three months a year contain a third one.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## Travel Budget Calculator: Daily Trip Budget | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/travel-budget-calculator.html
 Travel budget calculator
 Your daily budget for a trip is what is left of the trip budget divided by the days left, today included. Enter the budget, the trip's length and what you have spent so far; add the local currency and your own rate to see the same daily figure in the money you pay with there.
  Daily budget for a trip  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Enter the budget and spending in your home money.
   Trip budget   For spending during the trip. Leave flights or a hotel paid in advance out of both amounts.   Spent so far   Up to the end of yesterday gives the cleanest daily figure.   Count the trip by   Number of days  Dates    Days in the trip   Count the first and the last day.   Days already over   Whole days before today: 0 on the first day.   First day of the trip    Last day of the trip    Today's date    Local currency (optional)   A code or a name, used only as a label.   Rate (optional): what 1  unit of local money  costs in your home money     Work out my daily budget
 Example: 1,100 left for 6 days is 183.33 a day, or 166.67 EUR at 1 EUR = 1.10. That is 100 over an even pace.
   Your trip    Measure  Result      Left of the budget  1,100.00 1,000.00 EUR    Days left, today included  6 of 10    Per day from today  183.33 166.67 EUR    Planned per day  200.00 181.82 EUR    Even pace by today  800.00    Against an even pace  100.00 over
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 Daily budget for what is left
   What is left of a trip budget, shared across the days left, in one currency    Left  3 days  7 days  14 days      300  100.00  42.86  21.43    500  166.67  71.43  35.71    1,000  333.33  142.86  71.43    1,500  500.00  214.29  107.14    2,000  666.67  285.71  142.86    3,000  1,000.00  428.57  214.29    5,000  1,666.67  714.29  357.14
 How it is calculated
  Per day from today = (trip budget − spent so far) ÷ days left.  Days left count today and the last day of the trip. In the example, a 10-day trip with 4 days over has 6 left; 2,000 less the 900 spent leaves 1,100, which is 183.33 a day.
  Even pace by today = trip budget × days over ÷ days in the trip.  After 4 of 10 days, an even pace has spent 800 of 2,000. Spending 900 is 100 over that pace, which is why each day left gets 183.33 instead of the 200 a day planned at the start. When nothing is left, the daily figure is zero and the calculator says by how much the budget was passed.
  In local money = the home figure ÷ the rate , where the rate is what 1 unit of local money costs in your home money. At 1 EUR = 1.10, 183.33 is 166.67 EUR. Use the rate your card or exchange actually gives you, fees included, not the rate in the news: that is the one your spending is really converted at. The display rounds to two decimal places, or to the local currency's usual decimals when you enter a currency code such as JPY.
 Keeping to it on the road
   Set the big costs aside first.  If the hotel is paid at check-out, take it out of the budget before you start, or the first days will look richer than they are.   Check the daily figure each morning,  before the day's spending. An expensive day is fine; the figure for the days after it simply goes down.   Keep cash in the count.  Note each cash purchase, or count the money as spent when you take it out. Doing neither is how a trip budget drifts without anyone noticing.
 How TrackExpenses does this
 TrackExpenses records a purchase in the currency you paid in. Add the trip's currency under More → Additional Currencies; on a new entry, choose it and type the rate to your main currency (the field is filled in with the last rate you used for it). The entry then counts in your main currency in every total and budget. Entries in other currencies are free.
 For the daily figure, give the trip a category of its own, such as Travel (More → Expense Categories), and a budget for it in More → Budgets. With Pro, tap the Today card at the top of your daily list, then Daily budget for, choose Chosen categories and tick Travel; switch on Stop on a date to end it on the trip's last day. The app then shares what is left of that budget, after its own repeating bills, across the days left, today included, worked out before today's spending so the figure holds still all day. The last day has to fall inside the current budget period, and when it passes, the daily budget goes back to the whole budget by itself. Your budgets do not change, and widgets and Siri keep to the whole budget.
 Budget alerts, a free switch at the top of More → Budgets, tell you when the Travel budget passes 80% ahead of its pace and when it goes over.
  Guide: track travel expenses abroad  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator  ·  Budget pacing calculator  ·  Savings goal calculator  ·  Multi-currency expenses in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  How do I work out a daily budget for a trip?  Subtract what you have spent from the trip budget and divide what is left by the days left, today included. 1,100 left with 6 days to go is 183.33 a day.
  Should flights and the hotel be in the travel budget?  Leave out what is already paid, from the budget and from the spending, so the daily figure is only about money you can still decide on. A hotel paid at the end of the stay belongs in the budget, or set it aside before you start.
  Which exchange rate should I use?  The rate your card or exchange really gives you, fees included. Divide what a purchase cost in your home money by what it cost in local money to find it, and use that rate for the rest of the trip.
  What if I have already spent the whole trip budget?  Then there is nothing left to share across the days that remain, and the calculator shows zero a day and how far over you are. Decide on purpose where the extra money comes from, instead of letting it come out of next month.

## Savings Goal Calculator: How Much to Save | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/savings-goal-calculator.html
 Savings goal calculator
 Enter what you are saving for and what you already have. The calculator shows how much to put aside each month, week and day to get there by a date, or how long it takes at the amount you can save.
  Plan a savings goal  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount.
   Goal amount    Already saved    I want to know   How much to save to reach it by a date  How long it takes at a monthly amount    Reach it by   Counted from today.   I can save per month     Calculate my plan
 Example: 4,500 still to save over 365 days is 375.00 a month, 86.30 a week or 12.33 a day.
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 What to save each month
   Monthly amount for what is still to save, with no interest, in one currency    Still to save  In 12 months  In 24 months  In 36 months      1,000  83.33  41.67  27.78    3,000  250.00  125.00  83.33    5,000  416.67  208.33  138.89    10,000  833.33  416.67  277.78    20,000  1,666.67  833.33  555.56    50,000  4,166.67  2,083.33  1,388.89
 How it is calculated
  Still to save = goal − already saved.  With a date, the calculator divides that by the days from today to the date:  per day = still to save ÷ days . A week is seven of those days, and a month is the daily amount times 365 ÷ 12, so a goal 365 days away comes to one twelfth a month. In the example, 5,000 less the 500 already saved leaves 4,500; over 365 days that is 12.33 a day, 86.30 a week and 375.00 a month.
 With a monthly amount,  months needed = still to save ÷ monthly amount, rounded up . 4,500 at 300 a month takes 15 months; the last month completes the goal.
 The calculator does not add interest. For a goal a year or two away, interest on an ordinary savings account changes the monthly figure very little, and leaving it out means you arrive slightly early instead of slightly short. For goals many years away, or money that is invested, the result here is the most you would need to put in, not a forecast.
 Make the monthly amount real
 A monthly figure works when it leaves your account before you can spend it. Three things help:
   Move it on payday.  Transfer the amount to a separate savings account the day you are paid, and budget the month on what is left.   Check it against your pay.  If the figure is more than you can spare, move the date instead of giving up on the goal: twice the time is half the monthly amount.   Keep goals apart.  An emergency fund, a trip and a new phone are easier to follow as separate amounts than as one balance.
 In a 50/30/20 budget, savings are the 20%. If one goal needs more than that share of your take-home pay, you can see at once that either the date or another part of the budget has to change.
 Follow it in your ledger
 In TrackExpenses, Savings is its own kind of account, and money moved into it is a transfer, not an expense, so your spending totals stay honest while the savings balance grows. Three accounts are free. With Pro, the salary plan gives each savings account a monthly line next to your spending, and says in one sentence whether your income covers everything you planned.
  Emergency fund calculator  ·  50/30/20 budget calculator  ·  Payday calculator  ·  Habit cost calculator  ·  Accounts and transfers in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  How much should I save each month to reach my goal?  Subtract what you already have from the goal and divide by the number of months left. To save 4,500 in 12 months you need 375 a month; in 24 months, 187.50 a month.
  Should a savings goal calculation include interest?  For a goal one or two years away it makes little difference, and leaving interest out is the safer estimate. This calculator leaves it out, so any interest you earn brings the goal a little closer.
  Where should the money for a savings goal come from in a budget?  Treat it like a bill you pay to yourself on payday. In a 50/30/20 budget it is part of the 20% for savings. If the goal needs more, lengthen the time or reduce another part of the budget.

## Emergency Fund Calculator: How Much You Need | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/emergency-fund-calculator.html
 Emergency fund calculator
 An emergency fund target is your essential monthly costs times the months you want covered: 2,000 a month for six months is 12,000. Enter your costs, the months, what you have saved and what you can add each month to see the gap and the month you would close it.
  Size your emergency fund  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount.
   Essential costs per month   Rent or mortgage, bills, groceries, transport, insurance and minimum debt payments.   Months of cover   3 months  6 months  9 months  12 months  Another number    Number of months    Saved for it so far    I can add per month   0 shows only the target and the gap.    Calculate my fund
 Example: six months of 2,000 is a 12,000 target. With 3,000 saved, 9,000 is still to save, which takes 18 months at 500 a month.
   Your emergency fund    Measure  Result      Target  12,000.00    Saved so far  3,000.00 (1.5 months)    Still to save  9,000.00    Months to get there  18 (1 year and 6 months)    You get there  18 months from now
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 Emergency fund targets
   Essential monthly costs times the months of cover, in one currency    Costs a month  3 months  6 months  12 months      1,000  3,000  6,000  12,000    1,500  4,500  9,000  18,000    2,000  6,000  12,000  24,000    2,500  7,500  15,000  30,000    3,000  9,000  18,000  36,000    4,000  12,000  24,000  48,000    5,000  15,000  30,000  60,000
 How it is calculated
  Target = essential costs per month × months of cover. Still to save = target − saved so far.  Your savings also count as months: 3,000 against costs of 2,000 a month covers 1.5 months today.
  Months to get there = still to save ÷ what you add each month, rounded up , because the last month is the one that completes it. 9,000 at 500 a month takes 18 months. The month shown assumes you add the amount once a month, starting next month, so 18 payments end 18 months from now.
 The calculator adds no interest. Money for emergencies belongs somewhere safe and easy to reach, where interest is small; leaving it out means you arrive a little early rather than a little short. It also assumes your costs stay where they are, so recheck the target when your rent or your household changes.
 Three months, six or twelve?
 There is no single right number; it depends on how quickly your income could come back and how many people depend on it.
   Three months  suits a steady job, a second income in the household and no one else relying on you.   Six months  is the common middle: one income, or a job that would take a while to replace.   Nine to twelve months  suits freelance or commission income, a single income with children, or work in a field where jobs are scarce.
 Count only essentials, not your whole budget: in an emergency the eating out and the subscriptions stop. Building it slowly still helps, because one month of cover already turns a broken car or a sudden bill into an inconvenience instead of a debt.
 How TrackExpenses does this
 In TrackExpenses, an emergency fund fits a Savings account of its own. Money moved into it is a transfer, not spending, so your spending totals stay honest while the balance grows, and the Accounts tab shows what it holds. For the essential costs, Stats → Overview shows your repeating bills as Fixed costs, a month and a year, which is a good first figure to start from. Both are free; three accounts are free, and Pro removes the limit.
 With Pro, the salary plan gives the fund its own monthly line under Saving & investing, beside your spending, and its Actual view shows how much reached the account this period and how much is still to go.
  Savings goal calculator  ·  Monthly budget calculator  ·  Net worth calculator  ·  Accounts and transfers in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  How much should my emergency fund be?  A common target is three to six months of essential costs: rent or mortgage, bills, groceries, transport, insurance and minimum debt payments. With an irregular income or people who depend on you, aim nearer nine to twelve months.
  Should I count my whole budget or only essentials?  Only essentials. In an emergency you would stop eating out, shopping and most subscriptions, so the fund needs to cover what you could not stop.
  Does the calculator include interest?  No. Emergency money is best kept safe and easy to reach, where interest is small, so the result is the most you would need to put in. Any interest you earn brings the date a little closer.
  Should I build an emergency fund before paying off debt?  Many people first save a small fund, about one month of essentials, so a surprise bill does not go on a card, then pay down expensive debt, then build the full fund. Keep paying at least the minimum on every debt throughout.

## Net Worth Calculator: Own Minus Owe | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/net-worth-calculator.html
 Net worth calculator
 Your net worth is everything you own minus everything you owe. List your cash, accounts and investments on one side and your cards, loans and mortgage on the other: the calculator adds up each side, subtracts, and shows the sum so you can check it.
  Work out your net worth  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every amount, and today's value for anything you own.
   What you own
   Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove
  Add something you own
  What you owe
   Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove    Item    Amount    Remove
 Enter what you owe as a positive amount. An overdrawn bank account goes here too, as the amount overdrawn.
  Add something you owe
 Calculate my net worth
 Example: 12,800 owned − 4,200 owed = 8,600 net worth.
   Your net worth    Measure  Amount      What you own  12,800.00    − What you owe  4,200.00    = Net worth  8,600.00
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the examples below.
 Net worth examples
   What is owned, what is owed, and the difference, in one currency    Situation  Own  Owe  Net worth      Starting out  5,000  1,000  4,000    Example above  12,800  4,200  8,600    Student loan  3,000  25,000  −22,000    Car loan  18,000  14,000  4,000    Home and mortgage  330,000  240,000  90,000
 How it is calculated
  Net worth = what you own − what you owe.  What you own is the sum of every amount in the first list; what you owe is the sum of the second. In the example, 300 + 2,500 + 6,000 + 4,000 = 12,800 owned, 1,200 + 3,000 = 4,200 owed, and 12,800 − 4,200 = 8,600. The result is worked out from the two totals, never added up separately, so the three figures always agree.
 A net worth below zero means you owe more than you own. That is common while paying off a student loan or after a large purchase on credit, and it is a starting point, not a verdict: what matters is which way it moves from one month to the next.
 What to count, and at what value
   Own:  cash, every bank and savings account, investments at today's value, and, if you want them in, a home or car at what they would sell for now, not what you paid.   Owe:  the full balance on each card, even if you pay it off every month, and the amount still outstanding on every loan and mortgage, not the monthly payment.   Leave out  what you cannot sell or would not count on, and money that is not yours, such as a card you only track for someone else.
 Work it out on the same day each month, such as payday, so the comparison is fair. A home or car makes the figure larger but not easier to spend; many people also track the version with only cash, accounts and investments.
 How TrackExpenses does this
 The Accounts tab in TrackExpenses opens with your net worth, with Assets and Liabilities side by side beneath it. Card and Loan accounts count as liabilities; Cash, Bank, Savings, Investment and Other accounts count as assets. A card's balance owed shows as a positive figure under Liabilities, and a card paid more than it owed lowers that figure. An overdrawn cash or bank account stays under Assets as a negative balance rather than vanishing, which gives the same net worth as listing the overdraft as something owed, as this calculator does. Net worth is always Assets minus Liabilities, worked out from the two, so the three figures cannot disagree.
 An account with Include in totals switched off keeps its own balance but stays out of the three figures, and accounts in another currency are shown in your main currency. Ask the money coach "what's my net worth?" and it answers on your phone from your accounts, without using an AI question. Three accounts are free; Pro makes them unlimited.
  Emergency fund calculator  ·  Savings goal calculator  ·  Monthly budget calculator  ·  Accounts and transfers in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  How do I calculate my net worth?  Add up everything you own, add up everything you owe, and subtract the second total from the first. 12,800 owned and 4,200 owed is a net worth of 8,600.
  Should I include my home in my net worth?  You can, at what it would sell for today, with the mortgage under what you owe. Many people also track their net worth without the home, because that money cannot be spent without selling it.
  Is a negative net worth bad?  It means you owe more than you own, which is common with a student loan or soon after buying a car on credit. What matters more is the direction: a figure that rises each month, even below zero, shows debt going down or savings going up.
  Do credit cards count if I pay them in full every month?  Yes. Count the balance on the day you work it out. It is money already spent that the card will collect, so leaving it out makes your net worth look larger than it is.

## Subscription Cost Calculator | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/subscription-cost-calculator.html

 List what you pay for each subscription and how often. The calculator adds them up as a month, a year and five years, and shows which ones cost the most.
  Add up your subscriptions  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved. Use one currency for every price.
    Name    Price    Billed   Every week  Every month  Every 3 months  Every year    Remove    Name    Price    Billed   Every week  Every month  Every 3 months  Every year    Remove    Name    Price    Billed   Every week  Every month  Every 3 months  Every year    Remove
  Add a subscription
  Monthly take-home pay (optional)     Add them up
 Example: 3 subscriptions come to 24.50 a month, 294.00 a year and 1,470.00 over five years.
  Video streaming: 144.00 a year  Music: 120.00 a year  Cloud storage: 30.00 a year
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 What a monthly price adds up to
   One subscription at an unchanged price, in one currency    Per month  Per year  Over five years      5  60  300    10  120  600    15  180  900    20  240  1,200    30  360  1,800    50  600  3,000    100  1,200  6,000
 How it is calculated
  Yearly cost = price × times billed in a year.  A weekly price is multiplied by 52, a monthly one by 12, one billed every three months by 4, and a yearly one counts once. The monthly figure is the yearly total divided by 12, which is why a yearly plan of 30 shows as 2.50 a month. Five years is the yearly total times five.
 The five-year figure assumes prices stay where they are. They usually rise, so read it as the least you would pay, not a forecast. The list under the result sorts your subscriptions by yearly cost, biggest first: the top two or three are where a decision changes the total.
 Find every subscription you pay for
 On iPhone, open Settings, tap your name, then tap Subscriptions. That list shows what is billed through Apple, with each renewal date and price; Apple's  subscriptions help page  shows the same steps and how to cancel there. Anything you signed up for on a website is not in that list, so go through one full month of card and bank statements as well, and look back a year for yearly renewals, which are the easiest to forget.
 Monthly or yearly plan?
 Divide the yearly price by 12 and compare it with the monthly price. A plan that costs 10 a month or 96 a year works out at 8 a month on the yearly plan, 24 less over the year. That saving is real only if you keep the subscription all year: cancel after three months and the yearly plan cost 96 where three monthly payments would have cost 30.
 Keep them in your ledger
 A total you worked out once goes stale the next time a price changes. In TrackExpenses a subscription is a repeating transaction: it is written into your ledger on its day without you entering it, and a changed price is one edit to the rule. Two repeating rules are free and Pro makes them unlimited. Stats → Overview then shows your fixed costs as a month and as a year.
  Guide: track subscriptions and recurring bills  ·  Habit cost calculator  ·  50/30/20 budget calculator  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator
 Questions
  How do I see my subscriptions on iPhone?  Open Settings, tap your name, then tap Subscriptions. The list shows subscriptions billed through Apple. Ones you pay for directly, by card or through your bank, appear only on your statements.
  Is a yearly plan cheaper than paying monthly?  Usually, if you keep it for the whole year. Divide the yearly price by 12 and compare it with the monthly price. A yearly plan you stop using after three months costs more than three monthly payments would have.
  How much should I spend on subscriptions?  There is no fixed rule. In a 50/30/20 budget most subscriptions are wants, so they share the 30% with eating out, shopping and entertainment. Seeing the yearly total beside your pay is what makes the decision clear.

## Habit Cost Calculator: Daily Coffee Per Year | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/habit-cost-calculator.html
 Habit cost calculator
 A coffee, a delivery fee, a snack on the way home: enter the price and how often you buy it. The calculator shows what that one habit costs in a week, a month, a year and five years.
  What does it add up to?  All figures stay in this browser. They are not sent or saved.
   What you buy    Price each time    How many times    Every   Day  Week  Month    Monthly take-home pay (optional)     Add it up
 Example: coffee at 4.50, 5 times a week, costs 1,170.00 a year. One fewer a week saves 234.00 a year.
   What it costs    Over  Cost      A week  22.50    A month  97.50    A year  1,170.00    Five years  5,850.00    Ten years  11,700.00
  JavaScript enables the calculator. Without it, use the formula and the reference table below.
 What a small price costs in a year
   One purchase at an unchanged price, in one currency    Price each time  5 times a week  Every day      2  520  730    3  780  1,095    4  1,040  1,460    5  1,300  1,825    8  2,080  2,920    12  3,120  4,380    15  3,900  5,475
 How it is calculated
  Yearly cost = price × times × periods in a year.  A year counts as 365 days, 52 weeks or 12 months, depending on how you entered the habit. The month is the yearly cost divided by 12. The week is seven days of a daily habit, and the yearly cost divided by 52 for one counted by the week or the month. In the example, 4.50 five times a week is 22.50 a week; 52 weeks make 1,170 a year, which is 97.50 a month.
 The five- and ten-year figures assume the price never changes. Prices usually rise, so read them as the least the habit would cost. The line about buying one fewer is the price times the periods in a year: at 4.50, skipping one coffee a week is 4.50 × 52, or 234 a year.
 What the number is for
 The yearly figure is not a verdict. A daily coffee that costs 1,170 a year may be worth every bit of it to you; the point is to decide with the real number in front of you, because a price seen once at the counter never looks like much. Two comparisons make it useful:
   Against your pay.  Enter your monthly take-home pay and the result shows the habit's share of it.   Against your fixed costs.  A habit of 100 a month weighs the same as a 100 a month subscription. If you are looking for room in a budget, compare both lists before choosing what to change.
 Find how often you really buy it
 People usually guess the price right and the count wrong. Before trusting the result, count: open your card or bank statement for last month and count the purchases at that shop, or search your expense records for its name. If you pay in cash, keep the receipts for two weeks and double the count.
 See it in your own spending
 TrackExpenses can do the counting once purchases are in your ledger. Search lists every entry for a shop or a word, so you can count them. On Stats → Overview, the Know your money card adds up the small purchases of the current period, how many there were and what share of your spending they made, once there are at least five; the same card shows your fixed costs as a month and as a year. Both are free.
  Subscription cost calculator  ·  Savings goal calculator  ·  Daily budget until payday calculator  ·  Reports and stats in TrackExpenses
 Questions
  How much does a daily coffee cost in a year?  Multiply the price by 365. A coffee at 4 every day is 1,460 a year; bought only on five days a week it is 1,040 a year.
  How do I work out the yearly cost of a habit?  Multiply the price by how many times you buy it in a week, then by 52. For something bought monthly, multiply the monthly spending by 12.
  Do small purchases matter more than big bills?  Not necessarily. Rent, loans and subscriptions are often larger in total. Work out the yearly cost of each and compare them before deciding what to change.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## Free Budget Calculators | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/tools/index.html
 Free budget calculators
 Eleven small calculators for the questions a budget starts with. They run in your browser: nothing you type is sent or saved, and there is nothing to sign up for.
   UNTIL PAYDAY   Daily budget until payday   What is left of your budget, divided by the days until you are paid again, today included.    AM I OVERSPENDING?   Budget pacing calculator   The share of your budget spent against the share of the period passed, the gap in money, and where the period ends at this pace.    PLAN THE MONTH   Monthly budget calculator   Give every part of your pay a job: spending lines and savings, each line's share of income, and what is left to plan or how far over you are.    A RULE OF THUMB   50/30/20 budget calculator   Your take-home pay split into needs, wants and savings, per paycheck, per month and per year, for weekly, biweekly or monthly pay.    PAYDAYS   Payday calculator   Days until your next payday and every payday for twelve months, with the three-paycheck months when you are paid every two weeks.    ON A TRIP   Travel budget calculator   What you can spend per day for the rest of a trip, in your own money and the local currency, and whether you are over an even pace.    SAVING   Savings goal calculator   How much to put aside each month, week and day to reach a goal by a date, or how long it takes at the amount you can save.    SAFETY NET   Emergency fund calculator   Your target from essential costs and months of cover, the gap to what you have, and the month you would get there.    THE BIG PICTURE   Net worth calculator   Everything you own minus everything you owe, with the sum written out so you can check it.    FIXED COSTS   Subscription cost calculator   Every subscription added up as a month, a year and five years, sorted by what costs the most.    SMALL PURCHASES   Habit cost calculator   What a daily coffee or any small habit costs in a week, a month, a year and five years, and what buying one fewer saves.    MISSING ONE?   Suggest a calculator   If there is a budget sum you keep doing by hand, write to us. The useful ones get built.
 How these calculators are made
 Each page states its formula and prints a reference table, so you can check a result by hand or use the page with JavaScript switched off. Amounts carry no currency symbol: use one currency for everything you enter. The results are arithmetic on the figures you type, not financial advice.
 When you want the same answers from your real spending,  TrackExpenses  works them out from your ledger, and the  guides  explain each method step by step.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction


## Best iPhone Expense Trackers: How to Choose
https://trackexpenses.app/compare/best-expense-trackers.html
 Choose an iPhone expense tracker by workflow.
 The best expense tracker for you is the one whose entry method you will keep using. Compare how purchases get in, how the month works, which languages and devices you need, and where your data goes before choosing by a feature count.  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction
 This is the developer’s comparison on the TrackExpenses website. It is not an independent ranking. The tables report what each product’s own listing, website or help pages say; “—” means I couldn’t verify it, not that the feature is missing. Prices change often and are left out here; the linked pages have them.
  Seven popular apps  ·  Bank SMS  ·  Bank connection  ·  Payday month  ·  Currencies  ·  Languages  ·  Voice  ·  Sharing  ·  Try it

   Money Manager  (Realbyte)  iPhone, iPad, Vision Pro, Android  No aggregator; “connect your debit card” not explained  —  Yes  No / Yes / Yes

   Spendee   iPhone, iPad, web; Android not checked  Optional, Premium  Apple Pay logging on iOS 27 (release notes); Siri adds entries  Budget start date documented (checked 5 October 2026)  No / Yes / Yes

   Monefy   iPhone (no iPad), Android  Not offered  None  First day of month 1–31 (help center, checked 5 October 2026)  No / Yes / Yes
   PocketGuard   iPhone, Apple Watch, Android, web  Central (US, Canada, UK); cash accounts allowed  Apple Wallet connection  —  English only

 Sources: each app’s linked page and App Store listing; YNAB’s  pay-cycle article ; Monefy’s  help center ; Spendee’s  budget help ; Wallet’s month-start help article was readable only as a search snippet; Copilot’s  manual accounts .
 If your bank sends useful SMS or email alerts  None of the seven apps above documents reading bank SMS or email alerts on iPhone. TrackExpenses does it through a Shortcuts automation you create: the app never reads your inbox, it receives one matching alert at a time. Two smaller apps also document iOS message workflows, checked on 5 October 2026:  Monetal  documents SMS and email recognition, offline operation and no registration, and  Tab.it  documents an SMS Shortcuts setup that uses a token tied to a Tab.it account. None of these workflows proves that your bank’s format will work: test a real alert before relying on it. If your bank only sends app notifications, no iPhone automation can read them; pasting the alert is the way in.
 If you want your bank connected  YNAB, PocketGuard and Copilot Money are built around bank connections, in the countries they list, and Spendee and Wallet offer them with Premium. TrackExpenses has no bank connection at all, by design. If automatic bank feeds are what you need, one of those will suit you better.
 If payday is your month boundary  TrackExpenses, Money Manager and Monefy document a month that starts on a day you choose; Spendee documents a budget start date. YNAB documents that it has no such setting. A date option alone doesn’t mean every list and chart follows it: TrackExpenses applies its month to the ledger, budgets, charts and the  daily budget .
 If you spend in several currencies  Money Manager, Spendee, Wallet and Monefy list multiple currencies. YNAB doesn’t convert currencies within a plan and suggests one plan per currency. TrackExpenses keeps each entry in the currency you paid, at your own rate, and converts every total to one main currency.
 If you want Arabic, Spanish or Portuguese  Of the seven, only Wallet ships Arabic; YNAB, PocketGuard and Copilot Money are English only. TrackExpenses is in English, Arabic with a right-to-left layout, German, Latin American Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese, and its voice entry, bank-alert reader and money coach work in all five.
 If you prefer to say purchases  Compare supported languages, device requirements and whether audio is processed locally or remotely. TrackExpenses makes drafts on the device from a whole sentence, several purchases at once (10 saved entries free a month, unlimited with Pro). Spendee and YNAB document Siri actions, and  Cash Book  documented voice logging through a relay to an AI model when checked on 5 October 2026.
 If you share money with someone  YNAB shares one budget with up to 6 people. TrackExpenses syncs between the devices on one Apple Account and has no shared budgets, so a couple keeping one budget together will be better served elsewhere.
 Try a small real ledger  Add one expense, one income and a transfer between accounts. Check a payday boundary, export a sample and read the privacy policy. Those actions show whether the workflow fits you better than any claim that one app is “best” for everyone.
  Money Manager comparison  ·  YNAB comparison  ·  Monefy comparison  ·  TrackExpenses SMS setup  ·  Voice entry guide  ·  All TrackExpenses features


## Money Manager Alternative for iPhone | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/compare/money-manager-alternative.html
 A Money Manager alternative with bank alerts, voice and Arabic.
 Realbyte’s Money Manager is a widely used ledger you fill in by hand, with a custom month start, budgets and an Android version. Consider TrackExpenses if you want bank texts and emails to log themselves, purchases said aloud, free private iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Mac, or the app in Arabic. Stay with Money Manager if you need Android or one of its many other languages.
 By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction
 This page is written by TrackExpenses’ developer, so read it as one side’s comparison, not an independent review. Money Manager’s facts come from its two App Store listings and its website, checked on 19 November 2026. Realbyte’s help center refused automated reading, so the few points that rest on it are marked. “Not documented” means I couldn’t confirm it, not that the feature is missing. TrackExpenses’ facts are checked against version 1.16.0.

 Sources:  Money Manager Expense & Budget on the App Store ,  Money Manager (Remove Ads) ,  realbyteapps.com , and Realbyte’s  backup article  (read only as a search snippet). Prices are US App Store prices on the day checked and may differ where you live.
 When to keep Money Manager
   You need Android,  now or later, or you share records between an iPhone and an Android phone. TrackExpenses is not on Android.   Your iPhone can’t run iOS 17,  or you use Vision Pro. Money Manager supports iOS 15.6 and Vision Pro.   You want a language TrackExpenses doesn’t have.  Money Manager lists 19 languages; TrackExpenses has five.   You want separate weekly, monthly and annual budgets.  TrackExpenses keeps one budget and works out a week or a year from it.   Manual entry already works for you.  A habit you keep is worth more than a feature you don’t need, and Money Manager is widely used: 4.8 from about 20,000 US ratings when checked.
 When to try TrackExpenses
   Logging is the part you drop.  A Shortcuts automation passes each bank text or email alert to the app, which files the amount, shop, card and category; or paste an alert, or say “coffee 15, taxi 40”. See  bank SMS and email alerts  and  voice entry .   You want your ledger on every device without a sync subscription.   iCloud sync  is free and private, and includes the Mac.   You read Arabic,  or prefer German, Spanish or Portuguese: the whole app, voice entry, bank alerts and the coach work in those languages.   You want the budget to warn you.  Budgets carry a marker for today,  alerts  come when you run ahead of pace, and a  daily budget  says what you can spend today.   You want answers, not only charts.  The  money coach  answers “what did I spend today?” or “how was September?” on your phone.
 Both apps let the month start on payday, so that alone is not a reason to switch.
 Moving your records
 Keep your original Money Manager file. TrackExpenses imports CSV files with Pro, so save Money Manager’s Excel export as CSV in Numbers or Excel first. The importer tries to recognise a Money Manager export by its column names and sets the columns for you, but every column stays editable and you see every row before anything is saved. It asks when a date could be read two ways, such as 03/04/2026, and an import can be undone in one tap.
 This page doesn’t promise that every Money Manager export imports cleanly. Try a small sample first and check dates, amounts, currencies, categories, and that the shop name and the note land where you expect. A move between your own accounts should come in as a transfer, not a new purchase. More in the  CSV export and import guide .
  Questions   Can I import my Money Manager data into TrackExpenses?  Possibly, with Pro. Save Money Manager’s Excel export as CSV, then use CSV import in More, Backup and Export: you check the columns and every row before anything is saved, and an import can be undone. Try a small sample first, because not every export has been tested.    Does TrackExpenses charge for sync?  No. Sync goes through your own private iCloud and is free for everyone, across iPhone, iPad and Mac.    Is TrackExpenses on Android?  No. It is on the App Store for iPhone, iPad and Mac with Apple silicon. If you need Android, Money Manager has an Android version.    Do both apps support a month that starts on payday?  Yes. Money Manager can change the start date of the month, and TrackExpenses lets the month start on any day from 1 to 31 for every list, budget and chart.

## YNAB Alternative Without Bank Sync | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/compare/ynab-alternative.html
 A YNAB alternative for payday months, several currencies and no bank link.
 YNAB is a complete zero-based budgeting system with optional bank import and a budget you can share. Consider TrackExpenses if your budget month starts on payday, you spend in more than one currency, you want the app in Arabic, German, Spanish or Portuguese, or you would rather log from bank texts and your voice than link a bank. YNAB’s own support pages document the first three as things it doesn’t do. Stay with YNAB if you want bank import, a shared budget or its method.

 When YNAB is the better choice
   You want transactions to arrive from your bank by themselves  and you bank in the US, Canada, the UK or the EU. TrackExpenses never connects to a bank.   You share money with a partner or family.  YNAB shares one budget with up to 6 people; TrackExpenses has no shared budgets.   You want a web app, Android or Apple Watch.  TrackExpenses is on iPhone, iPad and Mac only.   You want a strict zero-based method  and the way YNAB builds the whole app around it. TrackExpenses’ salary plan shows what is left to plan, but its budgets are simpler and unspent money doesn’t roll over.
 When to try TrackExpenses
   Your month runs from payday.  Set the start day once and every list, budget and chart follows it. See the  payday budget guide .   You spend in more than one currency  and want one budget: each entry keeps the currency and rate you paid, and every total converts to your main currency. See  multi-currency .   You want the app in Arabic, German, Spanish or Portuguese,  including voice entry, bank alerts and the coach.   You won’t link a bank, but don’t want to type everything.  Bank texts and emails can log themselves through a Shortcuts automation, alerts can be pasted, and purchases can be said aloud. See  bank SMS and email alerts .   You want no account and a free ledger.  Manual entry, budgets, moving money between budgets, alerts, reminders and iCloud sync are free; YNAB is subscription only.   You want to export from your phone.  Export & Share writes a CSV or a full backup on the iPhone, with Pro.
 Moving your records
 Export your register from YNAB’s web app as CSV and keep the file. TrackExpenses Pro imports CSV: you check which column is which, including files with separate money-in and money-out columns, answer a question if a date could be read two ways, see every row before anything is saved, and undo the import in one tap if something looks wrong. YNAB’s plan targets and notes aren’t in its export, so set up your budgets in TrackExpenses by hand. This page doesn’t promise every YNAB file imports cleanly; try a small sample first. More in the  CSV export and import guide .
  Questions   Can my budget month start on payday in YNAB?  Not as a setting. YNAB’s support says it uses a monthly plan to accommodate all pay cycles. TrackExpenses lets the month start on any day from 1 to 31.    Can I keep several currencies in one budget?  YNAB’s support says it doesn’t convert currencies within a plan and suggests one plan per currency. TrackExpenses keeps each entry in the currency you paid, at your own rate, and converts every total to one main currency.    Is TrackExpenses a zero-based budgeting app?  Not in YNAB’s sense. With Pro, its salary plan puts your income at the top and shows what is left to plan after spending and savings, but budgets are per period and unspent money doesn’t roll over.    Does TrackExpenses connect to my bank like YNAB?  No. It has no bank connection. Bank texts and emails can log themselves through a Shortcuts automation you set up, and any alert can be pasted.    Can I share TrackExpenses with my partner?  No. iCloud sync joins the devices on one Apple Account, and there are no shared budgets. YNAB shares with up to 6 people.

## Monefy Alternative with SMS and Voice | TrackExpenses
https://trackexpenses.app/compare/monefy-alternative.html
 A Monefy alternative for SMS and voice entry.  Consider TrackExpenses if you want optional bank SMS imports and on-device voice drafts alongside a fixed monthly payday budget. Monefy already documents a custom first day of month, so payday reporting alone is not a reason to switch.  By  Mohamed Elatabany  · Updated November 2026 ·  Suggest a correction   This page is written by TrackExpenses' developer. It compares documented workflows and does not claim to have tested every Monefy feature.
  When to keep Monefy  ·  When to try TrackExpenses  ·  Check your data first
 When to keep Monefy  If you are comfortable with manual entry and Monefy already gives you the records you need, there may be little value in moving. Its  official help  documents a first-day-of-month setting from 1 to 31, including aligning the month with payroll. Monefy also runs on Android and, per its App Store listing and website checked on 19 November 2026, syncs through your own Google Drive or Dropbox. A familiar entry habit is valuable.  When to try TrackExpenses  Try it when logging is the part you struggle to maintain. Optional Shortcuts automations pass supported bank alerts or Wallet purchases into the ledger. The app does not read your Messages inbox and does not need a bank login. One spoken sentence can become several on-device drafts that you review before saving. TrackExpenses also runs on iPad and Mac with free private iCloud sync, and is in Arabic, German, Spanish and Portuguese; the Monefy listing checked on 19 November 2026 shows iPhone only and no Arabic.  The free ledger includes budgets, historical stats and private iCloud sync, with 3 accounts, 2 recurring rules, 10 saved voice entries and 10 successful automatic bank SMS imports per calendar month per device. Pro adds forecasts/daily guidance, unlimited voice entry/SMS imports/accounts/rules and CSV import and export and full backups. Device and language support apply to voice.  Check your data before moving  Keep an original copy of your old records. Do not assume a CSV's columns have the same meanings in another app. TrackExpenses Pro previews CSV import and lets you map columns, but this page does not promise that every Monefy export is compatible. Test a small sample and check date, amount, currency, category and direction before confirming a larger import.  Account transfers are especially important to check: a move between your own accounts should not become a new purchase. A change of app should improve your workflow while preserving your understanding of the figures.  Compare a week of ordinary use  Try the same three or four real tasks: record a cash expense, review a bank alert, browse your payday month and export records. Keep the tool that makes those tasks easiest for you. No website comparison can measure that personal fit in advance.         10 مجانًا كل شهر · بلا حدود مع Pro  جملة واحدة تكفي لعدة مشتريات.  «قهوة 15، تاكسي 40 ومقاضي 180 من كارفور أمس.»  قل عملية واحدة أو مشتريات يوم كامل دفعة واحدة. يعرض TrackExpenses ما فهمه وأنت تتكلم، ويتوقف وحده حين تنتهي من الكلام، ثم يحوّل كلامك إلى مسودة لكل عملية بمبلغها وفئتها ومحلها وتاريخها. والتعرّف على الكلام يجري على جهازك نفسه. راجِع ثم احفظ.   عدة مشتريات في جملة واحدة  يفهم الأرقام كما تُقال: «خمستاشر» و«ألفين ونص»  اختر اللغة التي تتحدث بها من شاشة الاستماع  سُمع السعر 1250 وأنت تقصد 12.50؟ صحّحه بلمسة واحدة  قل «طلبات» أو «كارفور» فيعرف المحل وفئته   كيف يعمل التسجيل بالصوت (بالإنجليزية)  ←

        10 مجانًا كل شهر · بلا حدود مع Pro  تصل رسالة البنك، فتجدها في دفترك.  يرسل لك بنكك رسالة أو بريدًا مع كل عملية شراء. وبتحكم تلقائي واحد في «الاختصارات» تصل هذه التنبيهات إلى TrackExpenses، فيسجّل المبلغ وعملته، والمحل والبطاقة والتاريخ. أما رموز التحقق والعمليات المرفوضة والعروض فتبقى خارج دفترك.   رسائل البنك النصية، أو بريده عبر تطبيق «البريد» من Apple، حتى لو كان بريدك على Gmail  بالعربية والإنجليزية، وبالأرقام العربية أو الغربية، وبصيغ كثيرة غيرها  آخر أرقام البطاقة تختار الحساب الصحيح  التطبيق لا يفتح صندوق رسائلك ولا بريدك أبدًا   إعداد رسائل البنك خطوة بخطوة  ←    إعداد التنبيهات بالبريد  ←

       إيقاف مؤقت
       رسم متحرك لتسجيل رسائل البنك، برسائل ومبالغ للتوضيح.



        مجاني  الصق الرسالة، أو المس الأداة، أو اسأل Siri.  لا تريد إعداد تحكم تلقائي؟ انسخ رسالة البنك أو بريده والصقه في التطبيق، فتمتلئ العملية وحدها. والمس أيقونة التطبيق مطولًا لتسجّل بصوتك أو تضيف مصروفًا أو تلصق رسالة البنك مباشرة. سجّل مشترياتك المعتادة من أداة دون أن تفتح التطبيق، واسأل Siri: «كم تبقى من ميزانيتي في TrackExpenses؟»   الصق التنبيه، سواء وصلك برسالة أو ببريد  سبع أدوات للشاشة الرئيسية وشاشة القفل، ومركز التحكم وزر الإجراءات  مشتريات Apple Pay عبر تحكم تلقائي لبطاقات «المحفظة»  اكتب اسم محل سجّلت منه من قبل، فتُملأ فئته وحسابه المعتادان   الأدوات وSiri والاختصارات (بالإنجليزية)  ←
           شاشة حقيقية من التطبيق · بيانات للتوضيح





    جرّب بنفسك  اضغط على مثال، وانظر ماذا يفهم التطبيق.  كل نتيجة هنا هي ما يخرج به التطبيق فعلًا من هذه الكلمات، بالقواعد نفسها التي تعمل على iPhone. ولا يُرسَل شيء من هذه الصفحة إلى أي مكان.

    رقمك لهذا اليوم  اعرف كم يمكنك صرفه اليوم.  اجعل شهرك المالي يبدأ يوم الراتب، أي يوم من 1 إلى 31. يخصم TrackExpenses أولًا الفواتير التي لم تُدفع بعد، ثم يقسم الباقي على الأيام المتبقية. وما توفّره اليوم يزيد حصة الغد.   على كل شريط ميزانية علامة تبيّن أين وصل الشهر، فتعرف إن كان صرف 46% كثيرًا أم لا  انقل المال بين الميزانيات أو غطِّ أي تجاوز، ويبقى الإجمالي كما هو (مجانًا)  ميزانية يومية لفئات تختارها حتى تاريخ تحدده، مفيدة في السفر (Pro)  تجاوزت الميزانية؟ يخبرك بكم، ومتى تبدأ ميزانية جديدة   الميزانية اليومية والتوقعات من مزايا Pro. أما الوتيرة والأيام المتبقية والمصروف والمتبقي فمجانية.

     جرّبها · كم يمكنني أن أصرف يوميًا؟

      الأيام المتبقية مع اليوم   −   +

     إيقاف مؤقت
     محادثة وأرقام للتوضيح

    المدرّب المالي  مجاني + Pro   اسأل عن أموالك بكلماتك أنت.  «هل أنا على الوتيرة الصحيحة؟» «كيف كان سبتمبر؟» «كم صرفت على البقالة؟» يجيب مدرّبك عن أسئلة كهذه على هاتفك نفسه، فورًا ومجانًا. وللأسئلة المفتوحة يستعين بـ Claude من Anthropic بعد موافقتك فقط، ويرسل له ملخصًا لشهرك، لا ملاحظاتك ولا إيصالاتك ولا أسماء حساباتك ولا أرصدتك.   يقرأ شهرك الماضي ويقترح حدًّا واحدًا، وإذا انضممت إلى التحدّي يطمئن عليك كل أسبوع (Pro)  اكتب «قهوة 15 تاكسي 40» فيسجّل العمليتين، مجانًا  10 أسئلة للذكاء الاصطناعي مجانًا كل شهر على كل جهاز، وأكثر مع Pro  يتحدث العربية والإنجليزية والألمانية والإسبانية والبرتغالية   تعرّف إلى المدرّب المالي (بالإنجليزية)  ←

      🔔  تنبيهات الميزانية  إشعار حين تبلغ 80% من ميزانية قبل أوانها، وآخر حين تتجاوزها.  مجاني
      🗓️  تذكير بالفواتير  إشعار في التاسعة من صباح اليوم السابق لموعد الإيجار أو أي اشتراك.  مجاني
      ✈️  ميزانية يومية للسفر  اختر ميزانيات الرحلة وآخر يوم فيها، فتعرف كم يمكنك أن تصرف كل يوم.  PRO
      📱  الأدوات وSiri  سجّل مشترياتك المعتادة بلمسة، واسأل Siri كم تبقى من ميزانيتك.  مجاني
      🔎  البحث يجمع لك المبالغ  ابحث عن محل لترى كم صرفت فيه، في كل الأشهر.  مجاني
      💻  على كل أجهزتك  سجل واحد على iPhone وiPad وMac، بمزامنة خاصة عبر iCloud.  مجاني
      💱  أي عملة  سجّل ما دفعته في السفر بسعر الصرف الذي تحدده، والمجاميع بعملتك.  مجاني
      📤  التصدير والمشاركة  جدول بيانات لأي شهر أو فترة، أو النسخة الاحتياطية الكاملة.  PRO
      💼  خطة الراتب  وزّع دخلك على المصاريف والتوفير بندًا بندًا، واعرف هل يكفي لكل ما خططت له.  PRO
      💳  الحسابات والبطاقات  نقد وبنك وبطاقات وتوفير وقروض، والتحويلات لا تُحسب مرتين.  3 مجانًا
      🔒  قفل التطبيق  افتحه ببصمة الوجه أو رمز الدخول. لا ربط بالبنك ولا إنشاء حساب.  مجاني

      شهرك من الراتب إلى الراتب     جملة واحدة، ثلاث عمليات     ميزانية لكل فئة، وعلامة تبيّن أين وصل اليوم     مدرّب مالي يقرأ شهرك
   لقطات حقيقية من iPhone، والبيانات فيها للتوضيح.



    ابدأ مجانًا  دفتر مصاريف كامل ومجاني. ومع Pro يصبح أسهل.

      مجاني  كل ما تحتاجه لتجعل التسجيل عادة.   عمليات يدوية وميزانيات وبحث بلا حدود  شهر مالي يبدأ يوم الراتب، مع الوتيرة والإحصاءات  نقل المال بين الميزانيات وتغطية التجاوز  تنبيهات الميزانية والتذكير بالفواتير  مزامنة خاصة عبر iCloud على iPhone وiPad وMac  3 حسابات وقاعدتا تكرار  كل شهر وعلى كل جهاز: 10 إدخالات صوتية، و10 تنبيهات بنكية تُسجَّل تلقائيًا، و10 أسئلة للمدرّب بالذكاء الاصطناعي
      PRO  والباقي علينا.   إدخال صوتي وتسجيل تنبيهات البنك بلا حدود  حسابات وعمليات متكررة بلا حدود  خطة الراتب والتوقعات وخطط «ماذا لو»  ميزانية يومية للإجمالي، أو لكل ميزانية، أو لميزانيات تختارها حتى تاريخ تحدده  تحدّيات المدرّب ومزيد من الأسئلة  التصدير والمشاركة، واستيراد CSV، والنسخة الاحتياطية الكاملة  السمات وأيقونات التطبيق البديلة   اشتراك شهري أو سنوي، أو شراء لمرة واحدة مدى الحياة، بالسعر الذي تجده في App Store ببلدك. وإذا انتهى Pro فلن يُقفل شيء مما حفظته.




   أسئلة في محلها  قبل أن تنزّل التطبيق.
    هل يتصل TrackExpenses بحسابي البنكي؟  لا. لا ربط بالبنك، ولا دخول إلى حسابك البنكي، ولا حاجة إلى حساب في التطبيق. تسجّل عملياتك بنفسك: بصوتك، أو بلصق التنبيه، أو بتحكم تلقائي في «الاختصارات» يسجّل تنبيهات البنك ومشتريات Apple Pay.
    كيف يقرأ تنبيهات البنك دون أن يقرأ رسائلي؟  تنشئ في «الاختصارات» تحكمًا تلقائيًا يمرّر إلى TrackExpenses كل تنبيه من البنك يحتوي على كلمة تختارها، سواء وصل برسالة نصية أو بالبريد الإلكتروني. يقرأ التطبيق ما يمرّره التحكم التلقائي فقط، ويحتفظ بالعملية دون نص الرسالة، ولا يفتح صندوق رسائلك ولا بريدك.
    بنكي يرسل إشعارات من تطبيقه فقط. هل يفيدني TrackExpenses؟  نعم. لا يستطيع التحكم التلقائي في iPhone قراءة إشعارات تطبيق آخر، ولا يتيح iOS نسخ نص الإشعار نفسه، لكن يكفي أن تقول المبلغ والمحل بصوتك لتسجّل العملية في ثوانٍ، أو أن تنسخ نص العملية من تطبيق البنك إن كان يتيح ذلك وتلصقه في TrackExpenses. وإن كان بنكك يرسل أيضًا رسائل نصية أو بريدًا، فالتحكم التلقائي يسجّلها لك.
    هل يقرأ رسائل بنكي بالذات؟  يقرأ صيغًا كثيرة من تنبيهات البنوك بالعربية والإنجليزية في الإمارات والسعودية والكويت وقطر والبحرين وعُمان ومصر والأردن وغيرها، بالأرقام العربية أو الغربية، لكن لا يمكن ضمان كل بنك. جرّب إحدى رسائل بنكك في شاشة الإعداد داخل التطبيق قبل أن تعتمد عليه، وأي رسالة يتركها التحكم التلقائي يمكنك لصقها، أو إدخال عمليتها بنفسك.
    هل التطبيق مجاني؟  نعم. السجل المجاني فيه عمليات يدوية بلا حدود، وميزانيات، وشهر مالي يبدأ يوم الراتب، وإحصاءات، وبحث، ومزامنة خاصة عبر iCloud، ومعها كل شهر وعلى كل جهاز 10 إدخالات صوتية و10 تنبيهات بنكية تُسجَّل تلقائيًا و10 أسئلة للمدرّب بالذكاء الاصطناعي. ويرفع Pro هذه الحدود ويضيف خطة الراتب والتوقعات والميزانية اليومية وكل أنواع التصدير والنسخة الاحتياطية الكاملة، باشتراك شهري أو سنوي أو بشراء لمرة واحدة مدى الحياة.
    هل يرسل المدرّب المالي بياناتي إلى الذكاء الاصطناعي؟  فقط حين تسأل سؤالًا لا يستطيع هاتفك الإجابة عنه وحده، وبعد موافقتك. عندها يُرسَل سؤالك وما سبقه في المحادثة وملخص لهذا الشهر والشهر الماضي إلى Claude من Anthropic عبر خادم وسيط يديره المطوّر، وإذا احتاج المدرّب المزيد فمجاميع حتى 13 شهرًا أو حتى 20 عملية شراء. ولا تُرسَل أبدًا ملاحظاتك ولا إيصالاتك ولا أسماء حساباتك أو أرقامها ولا أرصدتك.
    بأي اللغات يعمل؟  بالعربية بواجهة كاملة من اليمين إلى اليسار، وبالإنجليزية والألمانية والإسبانية لأمريكا اللاتينية والبرتغالية البرازيلية: كل الشاشات، والتسجيل بالصوت، وتنبيهات البنك، والمدرّب المالي.
    هل يمكن أن يبدأ شهري المالي يوم الراتب؟  نعم. اختر أي يوم من 1 إلى 31، فتُحسب عليه عملياتك وميزانياتك ورسومك البيانية. فإذا نزل راتبك يوم 25 مثلًا، يمتد شهرك من 25 أكتوبر إلى 24 نوفمبر.
    هل يعمل على iPad وMac؟  نعم. يعمل TrackExpenses على iPhone وiPad بنظام iOS 17 أو أحدث، وعلى أجهزة Mac بشريحة Apple، والمزامنة الخاصة عبر iCloud تُبقيها كلها على السجل نفسه.
    أين تُحفظ بياناتي؟  على جهازك، مع مزامنة اختيارية عبر iCloud الخاص بك بين أجهزة Apple التي تملكها. لا حاجة إلى حساب في التطبيق. وتشرح سياسة الخصوصية كيف تُحفظ البيانات، وكيف يُعالَج الصوت، وما يخص المدرّب والمشتريات.  اقرأ سياسة الخصوصية (بالإنجليزية) ←



    تعلّم وخطّط  أدلة وحاسبات مجانية.

      أدلة بالعربية  تسجيل المصاريف من رسائل البنك، خطوة بخطوة  تسجيل تنبيهات البنك من البريد الإلكتروني
